domains.name: player
domains.description: Single source of truth for all player identity, profiles, accounts, authentication, preferences, and segmentation across console, PC, and mobile platforms. Owns player registration, parental controls, COPPA/GDPR consent records, player demographics, behavior patterns, engagement metrics (DAU, MAU, WAU, retention), LTV calculations, and player lifecycle management. The authoritative domain for WHO the business serves.

products.name: player_account
products.description: Master identity record and single source of truth for every registered player across all platforms (console, PC, mobile). Stores the canonical player_id, username, display name, avatar, bio, preferred language, locale, timezone, account status (active, suspended, banned, deactivated), account tier, registration timestamp, platform of origin, country of residence, age-verified flag, date of birth, gender identity (self-reported), profile visibility settings, account creation source, and last profile update timestamp. This is the root entity to which all other player domain entities relate via FK. Encompasses both the authentication/identity layer and the player-facing social/demographic profile layer as a single unified entity — industry standard in gaming platforms (PlayFab, AccelByte, GameSparks). Supports GDPR right-to-erasure workflows. Sourced from platform SDK registration flows (Steamworks, PSN, Xbox Live, Nintendo) and Salesforce CRM.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the player account. Primary key for the player_account entity. This is the root identity to which all other player domain entities relate.

attributes.name: test_account_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Gaming studios require employees (QA, designers, developers) to maintain test accounts for playtesting, bug reproduction, and compliance verification. Tracking which employee owns each test account is

attributes.name: account_level
attributes.description: Player's overall account progression level, earned through gameplay achievements and experience points. Used for matchmaking, content gating, and progression analytics.

attributes.name: account_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the player account. Active accounts have full access; suspended accounts have temporary restrictions; banned accounts are permanently blocked; deactivated accounts are player-initiated closures; pending_verification accounts await email confirmation; locked accounts require password reset.
attributes.references: Platform Terms of Service, Community Standards

attributes.name: account_tier
attributes.description: Subscription or membership tier of the player account. Determines access to premium features, exclusive content, and priority support. Founder tier for early supporters; developer tier for internal testing accounts.

attributes.name: age_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player's age has been verified through a trusted mechanism (ID verification, credit card validation, or parental consent for minors). Required for access to age-restricted content and features.
attributes.references: COPPA Compliance, ESRB Age Verification, PEGI Age Verification

attributes.name: avatar_url
attributes.description: URL pointing to the player's profile avatar image stored in the CDN (Content Delivery Network). Used for display in social features, leaderboards, and player profiles.

attributes.name: bio
attributes.description: Player-written biography or description displayed on their public profile. Limited to 500 characters. Subject to content moderation policies.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the player's country of residence. Used for regional content delivery, compliance with local regulations (GDPR, COPPA, PEGI, ESRB), and geo-specific monetization strategies.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, GDPR Territorial Scope, Regional Rating Bodies (ESRB, PEGI, USK, CERO, GRAC)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this player_account record was first created in the data warehouse. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: creation_source
attributes.description: Marketing attribution source indicating how the player discovered and registered for the game. Used for CPI (Cost Per Install), ROAS (Return on Ad Spend), and marketing campaign effectiveness analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: organic|paid_social|influencer|referral|cross_promotion|app_store|web_direct — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AppsFlyer Attribution Standards, Adjust Attribution Standards, Marketing Analytics Framework

attributes.name: data_processing_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has provided explicit consent for data processing activities beyond essential service delivery (analytics, personalization, third-party sharing). Required for GDPR compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6, GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent)

attributes.name: data_processing_consent_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player provided data processing consent. Required for GDPR audit trails demonstrating lawful basis for processing.

attributes.name: date_of_birth
attributes.description: Player's date of birth. Required for age verification, COPPA compliance (children under 13), GDPR consent requirements, and age-gated content access (ESRB, PEGI ratings).
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act), GDPR Article 8, ESRB Age Ratings, PEGI Age Ratings

attributes.name: display_name
attributes.description: Public-facing display name shown to other players in-game and in social features. May differ from username and can be changed by the player.

attributes.name: email_address
attributes.description: Primary email address used for account registration, authentication, password recovery, and marketing communications. Must be unique and verified.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4, COPPA Compliance, CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: email_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has verified their email address through the verification link sent during registration.

attributes.name: experience_points
attributes.description: Total experience points (XP) accumulated by the player through gameplay activities. Used to calculate account level progression and unlock rewards.

attributes.name: failed_login_attempts
attributes.description: Count of consecutive failed login attempts since the last successful login. Used for account lockout policies and fraud detection. Reset to zero upon successful authentication.
attributes.references: Account Security Standards, Fraud Prevention Framework

attributes.name: gdpr_right_to_erasure_requested_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Right to Erasure Requested Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has submitted a GDPR Article 17 Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) request. Triggers data deletion workflows while preserving legally required records.

attributes.name: gender_identity
attributes.description: Self-reported gender identity of the player. Optional field used for demographic analytics and personalized content recommendations. Collected with explicit consent per GDPR and privacy regulations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9 (Special Categories), Privacy Best Practices

attributes.name: last_login_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time of the player's most recent successful login. Used for DAU (Daily Active Users), MAU (Monthly Active Users), WAU (Weekly Active Users) calculations, churn prediction, and re-engagement campaigns.
attributes.references: Player Engagement Analytics, Retention Metrics Framework

attributes.name: last_profile_update_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player last modified their profile information (display name, avatar, bio, or privacy settings). Used for audit trails and profile activity tracking.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: Locale identifier combining language and region (e.g., en_US, fr_FR, ja_JP). Used for region-specific formatting of dates, numbers, currency, and culturally appropriate content.

attributes.name: marketing_opt_in_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has consented to receive marketing communications (newsletters, promotional offers, game updates). Required for GDPR and CAN-SPAM compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing), CAN-SPAM Act, CASL (Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation)

attributes.name: parental_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether verifiable parental consent has been obtained for players under the age of 13 (COPPA) or under 16 (GDPR Article 8). Required for data collection and processing of minors.

attributes.name: password_last_changed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player last changed their account password. Used for security audits, password expiration policies, and breach response.

attributes.name: platform_of_origin
attributes.description: The platform through which the player originally registered their account. Used for platform-specific analytics, cross-platform progression tracking, and attribution analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: steam|psn|xbox_live|nintendo_switch|epic_games|mobile_ios|mobile_android|web — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Platform SDK Standards (Steamworks, PSN, Xbox Live, Nintendo, Epic Games Store)

attributes.name: preferred_language
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code representing the player's preferred language for UI, communications, and in-game content. Used for localization and content delivery.

attributes.name: profile_visibility
attributes.description: Privacy setting controlling who can view the player's profile information. Public profiles are visible to all; friends_only profiles are visible to approved connections; private profiles are visible only to the player.
attributes.references: Privacy Policy, GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design)

attributes.name: referral_code
attributes.description: Unique referral code used by the player during registration, linking them to the referring player for viral growth tracking and K-Factor (Viral Coefficient) calculation.
attributes.references: Viral Marketing Framework, Player Acquisition Strategy

attributes.name: registration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player account was first created in the system. Used for cohort analysis, retention calculations, and LTV (Lifetime Value) modeling.

attributes.name: reputation_score
attributes.description: Community reputation score based on player behavior, reports, commendations, and moderation actions. Used for matchmaking, trust scoring, and identifying toxic players. Negative scores indicate poor behavior.

attributes.name: suspension_expiry_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when a temporary account suspension will automatically expire and the account will be reactivated. Null for permanent bans.
attributes.references: Moderation Policy, Terms of Service Enforcement

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Detailed reason for account suspension or ban, referencing specific Terms of Service or Community Standards violations. Used for player communication, appeals processing, and moderation analytics.
attributes.references: Terms of Service, Community Standards, Moderation Policy

attributes.name: suspension_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the account was suspended or banned. Used for suspension duration tracking and appeals processing.
attributes.references: Moderation Policy, Terms of Service Enforcement

attributes.name: timezone
attributes.description: IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo) representing the player's local timezone. Used for scheduling live events, daily login rewards, and time-based game mechanics.

attributes.name: total_playtime_minutes
attributes.description: Cumulative total playtime across all sessions since account creation, measured in minutes. Used for engagement analysis, LTV (Lifetime Value) modeling, and player segmentation.

attributes.name: two_factor_auth_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has enabled two-factor authentication (2FA) for enhanced account security. Recommended for high-value accounts and required for certain privileged operations.
attributes.references: Account Security Best Practices, PCI DSS Requirement 8.3

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this player_account record was last modified in the data warehouse. Used for change tracking and incremental ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processing.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, ETL Processing Standards

attributes.name: username
attributes.description: Unique username chosen by the player during registration. Used for login and public identification across platforms. Must be unique system-wide.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Registration Standards (Steamworks, PSN, Xbox Live, Nintendo)

products.name: profile
products.description: Player-facing identity and demographic profile record linked to an account. Stores display name, avatar URL, bio, preferred language, locale, timezone, date of birth, gender identity (self-reported), country, region, profile visibility settings, and last profile update timestamp. Distinct from the account (authentication/identity) — the profile is the social and demographic layer. Supports GDPR right-to-erasure workflows by tracking consent-linked profile fields. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Contact object.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the player profile. Primary key. Distinct from account_id (authentication layer) — this is the social and demographic identity layer.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the player account (authentication/identity layer). Links this profile to the underlying authentication record.

attributes.name: accessibility_settings
attributes.description: JSON or delimited string capturing player's accessibility preferences (e.g., colorblind mode, subtitle size, controller remapping, audio cues). Used to personalize game experience for players with disabilities.
attributes.references: ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act), WCAG 2.1 (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)

attributes.name: avatar_url
attributes.description: URL to the player's profile avatar image stored in CDN (Content Delivery Network). Used for visual identity across platforms.

attributes.name: bio
attributes.description: Player-authored biography or profile description. Free-text field subject to content moderation. May be displayed on public profiles.

attributes.name: communication_language
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code for player support and marketing communications. May differ from preferred_language (UI language). Used for customer service routing and localized campaigns.

attributes.name: content_rating_preference
attributes.description: Player's preferred ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board) content rating level for game recommendations and parental controls. Values: E (Everyone), E10 (Everyone 10+), T (Teen), M (Mature 17+), AO (Adults Only 18+).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the player profile was first created. Used for player tenure analysis, cohort segmentation, and lifecycle tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: email_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player's email address has been verified through a confirmation link or code. Required for account recovery and secure communications.

attributes.name: external_profile_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier from the source system (e.g., Salesforce Contact ID, Steam ID, Epic Account ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: gdpr_erasure_completed_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Erasure Completed Timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when GDPR erasure request was completed and PII (Personally Identifiable Information) was anonymized or deleted. Null if no erasure has been performed. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: gdpr_erasure_requested
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Erasure Requested
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player has requested data erasure under GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure). Triggers anonymization workflow and profile soft-deletion.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: Locale identifier combining language and region (e.g., en_US, es_MX, fr_FR, de_DE, ja_JP). Used for localization of content, currency, and regional settings.

attributes.name: parental_consent_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether verifiable parental consent has been obtained for players under 13 (COPPA) or under 16 (GDPR Article 8). Required for minors to access online features.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act), GDPR Article 8

attributes.name: phone_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player's phone number has been verified through SMS or voice call. Used for two-factor authentication (2FA) and account security.

attributes.name: platform_preference
attributes.description: Player's preferred gaming platform. Used for personalized content recommendations, platform-specific events, and cross-platform analytics. Values: console, pc, mobile, vr (Virtual Reality), cross_platform.

attributes.name: player_segment
attributes.description: Marketing or behavioral segment assigned to this player (e.g., whale, casual, hardcore, lapsed, at_risk_churn). Used for targeted campaigns, personalized offers, and retention strategies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: whale|casual|hardcore|lapsed|at_risk_churn|new_player|returning_player — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code of the player's location. Used for regional analytics, tax compliance, and geo-targeted marketing. May be required for payment processing.
attributes.references: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard), GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: preferred_language
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code representing the player's preferred language for UI (User Interface) and communications (e.g., en, es, fr, de, ja, zh).

attributes.name: profile_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the player profile. Values: active (normal operation), suspended (temporary restriction), banned (permanent restriction), deleted (soft-deleted per GDPR right-to-erasure), pending_verification (awaiting age/identity verification).
attributes.references: Internal Moderation Policy, GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure)

attributes.name: referral_code
attributes.description: Unique referral code assigned to this player for viral marketing and K-Factor (Viral Coefficient) tracking. Used when this player refers new players to earn rewards.

attributes.name: referred_by_code
attributes.description: Referral code of the player who referred this player. Used for attribution tracking, referral reward distribution, and viral growth analysis.

attributes.name: region
attributes.description: Sub-national region, state, or province (e.g., California, Ontario, Bavaria). Used for regional analytics, localized events, and compliance with regional regulations.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record that originated this profile record. Values: salesforce_crm (Salesforce CRM Contact object), unity_player_services, epic_games_services, steam, console_sdk, mobile_sdk. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: timezone
attributes.description: IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo). Used for scheduling live events, daily rewards, and time-based features.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent profile update (any field change). Used for tracking profile activity and data freshness. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: vip_tier
attributes.description: Player's VIP tier based on spending, engagement, or loyalty. Used for tiered rewards, exclusive content access, and premium support. Values: none, bronze, silver, gold, platinum, diamond.

products.name: platform_identity
products.description: Tracks a player's linked external platform identities (PSN ID, Xbox Gamertag, Nintendo Account, Steam ID, Epic Games ID, Apple Game Center, Google Play Games). Each row represents one platform-to-account linkage, storing the external platform type, external platform user ID, platform display name, link status, link timestamp, and last verified timestamp. Enables cross-platform identity resolution and single sign-on federation. Sourced from Steamworks, Console SDKs, and Epic Games Store SDK integrations.

attributes.name: platform_identity_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the platform identity linkage record. Primary key.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal player account that owns this platform identity linkage. Links to the authoritative player account record in the Player domain.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this platform identity linkage record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: cross_platform_play_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the player has opted in to cross-platform play (crossplay) using this platform identity. True indicates the player allows matchmaking and interaction with players on other platforms; false indicates platform-exclusive play only.

attributes.name: external_platform_user_code
attributes.description: The unique user identifier assigned by the external platform (e.g., PSN ID, Xbox Gamertag, Steam ID, Epic Account ID). This is the authoritative identifier used by the platform provider to identify the player on their ecosystem.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Documentation (PSN, Xbox Live, Steam, Epic Games Store, Apple Game Center, Google Play Games)

attributes.name: fraud_risk_score
attributes.description: A calculated risk score (0.00 to 100.00) indicating the likelihood that this platform identity linkage is fraudulent or suspicious. Higher scores indicate higher risk. Derived from fraud detection algorithms analyzing linkage patterns, device fingerprints, and platform reputation signals.
attributes.references: Internal Fraud Detection Framework, PCI DSS 3.2.1 Requirement 11.4

attributes.name: last_activity_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the player last used this platform identity to authenticate or play. Used for identity staleness detection and account security monitoring.

attributes.name: last_verified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the platform identity linkage was most recently verified or re-authenticated. Used to track OAuth token refresh cycles and ensure the link remains valid.

attributes.name: link_device_type
attributes.description: The type of device from which the platform identity linkage was performed. Used for device-based analytics and cross-device identity resolution.

attributes.name: link_ip_address
attributes.description: The IP address from which the platform identity linkage request originated. Used for fraud detection, geolocation verification, and security auditing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4 (Personal Data Definition), ISO 27001 A.12.4.1 (Event Logging)

attributes.name: link_method
attributes.description: The technical method or flow used to establish the platform identity linkage. OAuth indicates standard OAuth 2.0 authorization flow; sdk_native indicates platform SDK native sign-in; manual_entry indicates player manually entered credentials; platform_sso indicates single sign-on federation; account_merge indicates linkage created during account merge operation.
attributes.references: OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749, Platform SDK Integration Guides

attributes.name: link_source
attributes.description: The application or channel through which the platform identity linkage was initiated. Game_client indicates in-game linking; web_portal indicates account management website; mobile_app indicates companion app; customer_support indicates manual linking by support agent; account_migration indicates bulk migration; platform_auto_link indicates automatic linkage by platform SDK.

attributes.name: link_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the platform identity linkage. Active indicates the link is valid and operational; inactive indicates the player has disconnected the link; suspended indicates temporary restriction; revoked indicates permanent removal; pending_verification indicates awaiting platform OAuth confirmation; expired indicates the OAuth token or link has lapsed.

attributes.name: linked_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the platform identity was first successfully linked to the player account. Represents the initial OAuth authorization or SDK linkage event.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, customer support annotations, or special handling instructions related to this platform identity linkage. Used for documenting manual interventions, escalations, or account-specific context.

attributes.name: oauth_access_token_hash
attributes.description: One-way cryptographic hash of the OAuth 2.0 access token issued by the platform provider. Stored for audit and token rotation tracking; the actual token is stored in a secure vault. Hash enables token lifecycle management without exposing the credential.

attributes.name: oauth_refresh_token_hash
attributes.description: One-way cryptographic hash of the OAuth 2.0 refresh token issued by the platform provider. Stored for audit and token rotation tracking; the actual token is stored in a secure vault.

attributes.name: platform_account_creation_date
attributes.description: The date when the player originally created their account on the external platform (e.g., when they first registered for PSN, Xbox Live, or Steam). Sourced from platform API profile data where available.

attributes.name: platform_account_tier
attributes.description: The subscription or membership tier of the players account on the external platform (e.g., PlayStation Plus, Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, Nintendo Switch Online). Indicates premium service level and entitlements on the platform.

attributes.name: platform_achievement_count
attributes.description: The total number of achievements, trophies, or gamerscore points the player has earned on the external platform. Sourced from platform achievements API. Used for player engagement and skill segmentation.

attributes.name: platform_age_verified_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the players age has been verified by the external platform provider. True indicates the platform has confirmed the player meets age requirements; false indicates unverified. Critical for COPPA and GDPR compliance.
attributes.references: COPPA 16 CFR Part 312, GDPR Article 8, Platform SDK Documentation

attributes.name: platform_communication_consent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the player has granted consent for the game publisher to communicate with them via the external platform (e.g., platform notifications, messages). True indicates consent granted; false indicates opt-out.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing), CAN-SPAM Act, Platform SDK Messaging Documentation

attributes.name: platform_data_sharing_consent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the player has granted consent for the game publisher to receive and process their platform profile data (e.g., friends list, achievements, playtime). True indicates consent granted; false indicates opt-out.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing), Platform SDK Data Sharing Documentation

attributes.name: platform_display_name
attributes.description: The human-readable display name or gamertag shown on the external platform (e.g., Xbox Gamertag, PSN Online ID, Steam Profile Name). This is the public-facing identity the player uses on that platform.

attributes.name: platform_email_verified_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the players email address has been verified by the external platform provider. True indicates the platform has confirmed email ownership; false indicates unverified. Used for trust scoring and fraud prevention.
attributes.references: Platform API Documentation, OpenID Connect Core 1.0

attributes.name: platform_friend_count
attributes.description: The total number of friends or connections the player has on the external platform. Sourced from platform social graph API. Used for social feature enablement and viral coefficient (K-Factor) analysis.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Social Graph API Documentation

attributes.name: platform_language_code
attributes.description: The two-letter ISO 639-1 language code representing the players preferred language setting on the external platform. Used for localized content delivery and communication.

attributes.name: platform_parental_control_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether parental controls are enabled on the players external platform account. True indicates the account is subject to parental restrictions (e.g., content filtering, spending limits, communication restrictions); false indicates no parental controls.
attributes.references: COPPA 16 CFR Part 312, Platform SDK Parental Control Documentation

attributes.name: platform_privacy_level
attributes.description: The privacy setting configured by the player on the external platform for their profile and activity visibility. Public allows all users to view; friends_only restricts to approved connections; private hides from all users.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Privacy Settings Documentation, GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design)

attributes.name: platform_region_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country or region code associated with the players account on the external platform. Determines regional content availability, pricing, and compliance requirements (e.g., GDPR for EU, COPPA for USA).
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, Platform SDK Region Documentation

attributes.name: platform_total_playtime_hours
attributes.description: The cumulative total playtime (in hours) the player has logged on the external platform across all games. Sourced from platform activity API where available. Used for player engagement profiling and LTV (Lifetime Value) modeling.

attributes.name: platform_type

attributes.description: Timezone offset from UTC for the device's location (e.g., +00:00, -08:00). Used for scheduling live events and time-based content delivery.

attributes.name: total_memory_mb
attributes.description: Total system memory (RAM) available on the device in megabytes. Used for performance optimization and minimum spec enforcement.

attributes.name: trust_score
attributes.description: Calculated trust score (0.00 to 100.00) indicating the device's trustworthiness based on behavior patterns, fraud signals, and usage history. Used for fraud detection and risk assessment.

products.name: segment
products.description: Defines player segmentation classifications used for live-ops targeting, personalization, and lifecycle management in GaaS operations. Stores segment name, segment type (behavioral, demographic, LTV-based, engagement-based, acquisition-source, churn-risk), definition criteria (rule-based or ML-assigned), segment owner (marketing, product, live-ops), effective date range, and is_active flag. Standard segments: Whale/Dolphin/Minnow (spend tiers), D1/D7/D30 retained cohorts, F2P converter, churned, lapsed, FTUE incomplete, high-churn-risk. This is the authoritative player classification taxonomy consumed by marketing and live-ops for campaign targeting and intervention workflows.

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the player segment. Primary key.

attributes.name: ml_model_registry_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the ML model used for segment assignment, if assignment_method is ml_model or hybrid. Null for rule-based segments.

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Player segments are created and maintained by analytics or marketing employees. The existing segment_owner text field should be normalized to a proper FK for accountability, access control (only owner

attributes.name: parent_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to a parent segment if this segment is a sub-segment or refinement of a broader segment. Null for top-level segments. Enables hierarchical segment taxonomies.

attributes.name: acquisition_channel
attributes.description: Marketing channel or source for acquisition-source segments (e.g., 'organic', 'facebook_ads', 'influencer', 'app_store_feature'). Null for non-acquisition segments.

attributes.name: age_range_max
attributes.description: Maximum age for demographic age-based segments. Null for open-ended or non-age segments.

attributes.name: age_range_min
attributes.description: Minimum age for demographic age-based segments. Null for non-age segments. Used for COPPA compliance and age-gated content targeting.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Workflow approval state for segment definition: draft (being created), pending_review (submitted for approval), approved (ready for use), rejected (not approved).

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the business user who approved this segment for production use. Null if not yet approved.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment was approved for production use. Null if not yet approved.

attributes.name: assignment_method
attributes.description: How players are assigned to this segment: rule_based (deterministic business rules), ml_model (machine learning classification), manual (analyst-curated), or hybrid (combination).

attributes.name: churn_risk_score_max
attributes.description: Maximum churn risk probability score (0.0000 to 1.0000) for churn-risk segments. Null for non-churn segments.

attributes.name: churn_risk_score_min
attributes.description: Minimum churn risk probability score (0.0000 to 1.0000) for churn-risk segments. Null for non-churn segments.

attributes.name: coppa_safe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Safe Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment is safe for targeting players under 13 years old per COPPA requirements (True) or restricted to 13+ audiences (False).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: definition_criteria
attributes.description: Business rule or logic defining segment membership (e.g., 'Players with LTV > $500', 'Retained on Day 7', 'No login in 30 days'). May reference rule engine or ML model.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this segment definition was retired or superseded. Null for currently active segments.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this segment definition became active and players began being assigned to it.

attributes.name: engagement_tier
attributes.description: Engagement level classification for engagement-based segments: high (daily active), medium (weekly active), low (monthly active), inactive (lapsed). Null for non-engagement segments.

attributes.name: gdpr_compliant
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment definition complies with GDPR requirements for player data processing and consent (True) or requires review (False). Critical for EU player targeting.

attributes.name: geo_filter
attributes.description: Geographic restriction for this segment using ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g., 'USA', 'JPN', 'DEU') or region codes. Null for global segments.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment is currently active and being used for player assignment and targeting (True) or has been retired (False).

attributes.name: is_standard_segment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a standard, enterprise-wide segment (True) used across all games and teams, or a custom segment (False) created for specific campaigns or experiments.

attributes.name: last_refresh_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent segment membership recalculation run.

attributes.name: max_ltv_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum LTV value for segment membership, applicable to LTV-based segments (e.g., Minnow tier upper bound). Null for open-ended or non-LTV segments.

attributes.name: min_ltv_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum LTV value required for segment membership, applicable to LTV-based segments (e.g., Whale tier). Null for non-LTV segments.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the business user who last modified this segment definition.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment record was last modified.

attributes.name: platform_filter
attributes.description: Platform restriction for this segment (e.g., 'console', 'pc', 'mobile', 'all'). Used when segment is platform-specific.

attributes.name: player_count
attributes.description: Current number of players assigned to this segment as of last_refresh_timestamp. Snapshot metric for segment size monitoring.

attributes.name: priority_rank
attributes.description: Priority ranking for segment assignment when a player qualifies for multiple segments. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used for conflict resolution in targeting logic.

attributes.name: refresh_frequency
attributes.description: How often player membership in this segment is recalculated: real_time (streaming), hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or on_demand (manual trigger).

attributes.name: retention_day_threshold
attributes.description: Day number used for retention-based segments (e.g., 1 for D1 retained, 7 for D7 retained, 30 for D30 retained). Null for non-retention segments.

attributes.name: segment_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code for the segment used in system integrations and reporting (e.g., WHALE_01, D7_RET, CHURN_HIGH).

attributes.name: segment_description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the segment purpose, membership criteria, and intended use cases. Provides context for analysts and marketers.

attributes.name: segment_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the player segment (e.g., Whale, Dolphin, Minnow, D7 Retained, High Churn Risk, FTUE Incomplete).

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the segment methodology: behavioral (play patterns), demographic (age, geo), LTV-based (spend tiers), engagement_based (DAU/MAU/WAU), acquisition_source (organic, paid), or churn_risk (predictive).

attributes.name: spend_tier
attributes.description: Monetization tier classification for spend-based segments: whale (high spenders), dolphin (medium spenders), minnow (low spenders), non_payer (F2P only). Null for non-spend segments.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of business tags for segment categorization and search (e.g., 'monetization', 'retention', 'high_value', 'experimental'). Used for segment discovery and filtering.

attributes.name: target_use_case
attributes.description: Primary business use case for this segment (e.g., 'Live-ops event targeting', 'Personalized offers', 'Churn prevention campaign', 'A/B test cohort', 'Retention analysis').

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the business user who created this segment definition.

products.name: segment_membership
products.description: Association table recording which players belong to which segments at any point in time. Stores player account reference, segment reference, assignment method (rule-based, manual, ML-model), assignment timestamp, expiry timestamp, and is_current flag. Enables point-in-time segment membership queries for cohort analysis, live-ops targeting, and retention campaign execution. Tracks segment transitions (e.g., player moved from 'active' to 'lapsed' segment) as separate rows for historical accuracy.

attributes.name: segment_membership_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the segment membership record. Primary key for tracking individual player-segment associations over time.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific game title for which this segment membership applies. Null indicates a cross-game or account-level segment. Enables game-specific player segmentation and title-level retention strategies.

attributes.name: marketing_campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the marketing or retention campaign that this segment membership supports. Null if the segment is not campaign-specific. Links segment membership to campaign performance tracking and ROI analysis.

attributes.name: marketing_player_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.player_segment. Business justification: Segment_membership assigns players to marketing-defined segments for CRM campaigns, email/push targeting, and lifecycle marketing automation. Marketing.player_segment represents marketing team's segme

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player account that is assigned to this segment. Links to the authoritative player identity in the Player domain.

attributes.name: primary_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the segment definition that this player is assigned to. Links to the segment configuration and rules.

attributes.name: assignment_batch_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the batch processing run that created this segment membership record, if applicable. Null for real-time or manual assignments. Used for troubleshooting, reprocessing, and audit trail of bulk segment updates.

attributes.name: assignment_method
attributes.description: The mechanism by which the player was assigned to this segment. Rule-based assignments use predefined business logic, manual assignments are curator-driven, ML-model assignments use predictive algorithms, API-trigger assignments come from external systems, batch-process assignments occur during scheduled ETL runs, and real-time-event assignments happen during live gameplay or transaction events.

attributes.name: assignment_reason
attributes.description: Business justification or rule description explaining why the player was assigned to this segment. May contain rule identifiers, campaign names, or free-text explanations for manual assignments. Supports transparency and auditability of segmentation decisions.

attributes.name: assignment_source
attributes.description: The system, process, or user that initiated this segment assignment. Examples include system names (GameAnalytics, Amplitude, internal segmentation engine), batch job identifiers, or user IDs for manual assignments. Provides audit trail for segment membership origin.

attributes.name: assignment_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the player was assigned to this segment. Critical for point-in-time segment membership queries, cohort analysis, and retention campaign execution. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: churn_risk_score
attributes.description: Predicted probability (0.0000 to 1.0000) that the player will churn within the next 30 days, calculated at the time of segment assignment. Higher scores indicate higher churn risk. Used for proactive retention targeting and at-risk player segments.

attributes.name: confidence_score
attributes.description: Confidence or probability score (0.0000 to 1.0000) assigned by ML models or rule engines indicating the certainty of this segment assignment. Higher scores indicate stronger confidence. Null for manual or deterministic assignments. Used for segment quality assessment and threshold-based filtering.

attributes.name: consent_status
attributes.description: Player consent status for being included in this segment and receiving segment-targeted communications or offers. Granted indicates explicit consent, denied indicates opt-out, not_required indicates consent is not needed for this segment type, pending indicates consent request is outstanding. Critical for GDPR and COPPA compliance.

attributes.name: consent_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player granted or denied consent for this segment membership. Null if consent is not required. Required for regulatory audit trails under GDPR and COPPA. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this segment membership record was first created in the data platform. Distinct from assignment_timestamp which reflects the business event time. Used for data lineage and audit purposes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: days_since_last_session
attributes.description: Number of days since the players last gameplay session at the time of segment assignment. Captured as a snapshot to understand recency patterns within segments. Critical for lapsed player segments and reactivation campaigns.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this segment membership ceases to be active for business purposes. Null indicates an ongoing membership. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this segment membership becomes active for business purposes. May differ from assignment_timestamp if the segment is scheduled to activate in the future. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: engagement_score
attributes.description: Composite engagement score (0.00 to 100.00) calculated at the time of segment assignment. Combines metrics such as DAU, session length, feature usage, and social interactions. Provides a snapshot of player engagement level for segment quality validation.

attributes.name: exclusion_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this player should be excluded from segment-targeted campaigns despite meeting segment criteria. True indicates exclusion (e.g., VIP player, employee account, test account, player request). Used to override automated segment assignments for special cases.

attributes.name: exclusion_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why the player is excluded from segment-targeted activities when exclusion_flag is True. Examples include VIP status, employee account, test account, player opt-out request, regulatory restriction. Null when exclusion_flag is False.

attributes.name: expiry_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this segment membership expires or was terminated. Null indicates an active, ongoing membership. Used to track segment transitions and historical membership periods. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: geo_region
attributes.description: Geographic region or market for which this segment membership is relevant. Uses 3-letter ISO country codes (USA, GBR, JPN) or regional groupings. Null indicates global segment. Supports geo-targeted campaigns and regional player behavior analysis.

attributes.name: is_current
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is the current active segment membership record for this player-segment combination. True for active memberships, False for historical records. Enables efficient queries for current segment state without date filtering.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this segment membership record was last updated. Used to track changes to membership status, expiry dates, or other mutable fields. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: ltv_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated lifetime value of the player in USD at the time of segment assignment. Captured as a snapshot to track how LTV estimates evolve as players move between segments. Used for high-value player identification and retention investment decisions.

attributes.name: membership_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this segment membership. Active memberships are in effect, expired memberships have passed their end date, suspended memberships are temporarily inactive, revoked memberships were manually terminated, and pending memberships are scheduled for future activation.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the ML model used for assignment, if assignment_method is ml_model. Null for non-ML assignments. Enables tracking of model performance and segment quality over time as models are retrained and updated.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, comments, or metadata about this segment membership. Used by analysts and campaign managers to document special circumstances, manual overrides, or observations about segment behavior.

attributes.name: priority_rank
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking when a player belongs to multiple segments simultaneously. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used by live-ops and marketing systems to determine which segment-specific content or offers to present when conflicts arise.

attributes.name: segment_entry_event
attributes.description: The specific player behavior, transaction, or milestone event that triggered entry into this segment. Examples include first_purchase, 7_day_inactive, level_50_reached, high_spender_threshold_crossed. Provides behavioral context for segment transitions.

attributes.name: segment_exit_event
attributes.description: The specific player behavior, transaction, or milestone event that triggered exit from this segment. Examples include returned_to_active, subscription_cancelled, moved_to_whale_segment. Null for active memberships. Tracks segment transition patterns.

attributes.name: segment_tenure_days
attributes.description: Number of days the player has been continuously assigned to this segment. Calculated as the difference between current date and effective_start_date. Used to identify long-term segment residents and track segment stability.

attributes.name: target_platform
attributes.description: The gaming platform for which this segment membership is relevant. Console includes PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo; PC includes Steam, Epic Games Store; mobile includes iOS and Android; cross-platform indicates segment applies across all platforms. Enables platform-specific segmentation strategies.

attributes.name: total_spend_to_date
attributes.description: Cumulative amount in USD that the player has spent across all in-app purchases, microtransactions, and subscriptions at the time of segment assignment. Snapshot value used for spend-based segmentation (whale, dolphin, minnow, free-to-play).

products.name: session
products.description: Records individual player gameplay sessions as discrete business events. Stores session start timestamp, session end timestamp, session duration (seconds), platform, game title reference, game version, session type (matchmaking, solo, co-op, tutorial, FTUE), device reference, IP geolocation (country/region), CCU bucket at session start, disconnect reason, and session quality indicators (average FPS, latency ms). The foundational event entity for DAU/WAU/MAU calculations, D1/D7/D30 retention, and session length KPIs. Sourced from GameAnalytics/Amplitude event streams.

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the gameplay session. Primary key.

attributes.name: device_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific device used for this session.

attributes.name: game_server_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.game_server. Business justification: Player sessions occur on specific game servers. This is a fundamental operational link for session tracking, performance analysis, and incident correlation. Enables answering questions like 'which ser

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title played during this session.

attributes.name: network_region_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.network_region. Business justification: Sessions are hosted in specific network regions for latency optimization, data residency compliance, and capacity planning. Operations teams analyze session distribution across regions to balance load

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player who initiated this session. Links to the player master entity.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the platform on which the session was played (console, PC, mobile).

attributes.name: tester_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: QA and development teams conduct playtesting sessions that must be distinguished from organic player sessions for analytics accuracy. Linking sessions to the testing employee enables bug attribution,

attributes.name: ab_test_variant
attributes.description: The A/B test or experiment variant assigned to the player during this session. Used for feature testing and optimization analysis.

attributes.name: attribution_source
attributes.description: The marketing attribution source that led to this players acquisition (e.g., organic, paid ad campaign, influencer). Sourced from AppsFlyer or Adjust. Used for CPI (Cost Per Install) and ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) analysis.

attributes.name: average_fps
attributes.description: The average frames per second experienced during the session. FPS is a key performance indicator for game rendering quality and player experience. Low FPS indicates performance issues.

attributes.name: average_latency_ms
attributes.description: The average network latency in milliseconds experienced during the session. High latency negatively impacts player experience, especially in real-time multiplayer games.

attributes.name: ccu_bucket
attributes.description: The concurrent user count bucket at the time this session started. CCU represents the number of players actively playing at the same time. Used for server capacity planning and peak load analysis.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this session record was first created in the analytics system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: The source system that captured and transmitted this session event (GameAnalytics, Amplitude, Unity Analytics, Unreal Engine telemetry, or custom instrumentation). Used for data quality and reconciliation.

attributes.name: disconnect_reason
attributes.description: The reason the session ended. Normal indicates player-initiated logout. Other values indicate technical or administrative disconnections. Used for quality assurance and player experience analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: normal|timeout|crash|network_error|kicked|banned|server_shutdown — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total duration of the gameplay session measured in seconds. Calculated as the difference between session end and start timestamps. Key metric for session length KPI (Key Performance Indicator) and engagement analysis.

attributes.name: end_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the player ended or disconnected from the gameplay session. Null if session is still active.

attributes.name: event_count
attributes.description: Total number of tracked in-game events (achievements, level completions, item pickups, etc.) that occurred during this session. Used for engagement depth analysis.

attributes.name: game_version
attributes.description: The specific version or build number of the game title that was active during this session. Used for version-based analytics and quality assurance tracking.

attributes.name: ip_address
attributes.description: The IP address from which the player connected to the game session. Used for geolocation analysis and security monitoring.

attributes.name: is_cross_platform
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this session involved players from multiple platforms (cross-play). Used for cross-platform engagement analysis.

attributes.name: is_first_session
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is the players first-ever session with this game title. Used for FTUE (First-Time User Experience) analysis and D1 (Day 1) retention tracking.

attributes.name: is_tutorial_completed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player completed the tutorial during this session. Used for onboarding funnel analysis.

attributes.name: matchmaking_wait_seconds
attributes.description: The time in seconds the player waited in matchmaking queue before the session started. Null for non-matchmaking sessions. Used for matchmaking efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: mtx_transaction_count
attributes.description: The number of microtransaction purchases made during this session. Used for conversion rate and monetization funnel analysis.

attributes.name: party_size
attributes.description: The number of players in the party or group at session start. 1 indicates solo play. Used for social play pattern analysis.

attributes.name: quality_score
attributes.description: A composite quality score (0-100) calculated from FPS, latency, and other technical metrics. Used to assess overall session experience quality.

attributes.name: revenue_usd
attributes.description: Total revenue generated during this session from MTX (Microtransactions), IAP (In-App Purchases), or other monetization events. Measured in US dollars. Used for ARPU (Average Revenue Per User) and ARPPU (Average Revenue Per Paying User) calculations.

attributes.name: sdk_version
attributes.description: The version of the game SDK or analytics SDK used to capture this session data. Used for data quality and version compatibility tracking.

attributes.name: session_type
attributes.description: The gameplay mode or type of session. FTUE (First-Time User Experience) indicates onboarding sessions. PvP (Player versus Player) and PvE (Player versus Environment) indicate competitive modes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: matchmaking|solo|co-op|pvp|pve|tutorial|ftue|practice|ranked|casual — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the player initiated the gameplay session. Primary business event timestamp for session lifecycle. Used for DAU (Daily Active Users), WAU (Weekly Active Users), and MAU (Monthly Active Users) calculations.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this session record was last updated in the analytics system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

products.name: engagement_metric
products.description: Daily/weekly/monthly pre-aggregated engagement metric snapshots per player, serving as the Silver Layer operational record for retention and engagement tracking. Stores metric date, metric grain (daily/weekly/monthly), DAU flag, WAU flag, MAU flag, session count, total playtime minutes, days_since_last_session, D1/D7/D30 retention flags, login streak, and game titles played count. This is NOT an analytics product — it is the operational engagement record that feeds live-ops, player support, and lifecycle management workflows. Sourced from GameAnalytics/Amplitude cohort outputs.

attributes.name: engagement_metric_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the engagement metric record. Primary key for this operational engagement snapshot.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player for whom this engagement metric snapshot was recorded. Links to the authoritative player identity in the Player domain.

attributes.name: achievement_unlock_count
attributes.description: Number of achievements or trophies the player unlocked during the metric period. Measures progression and goal-oriented engagement.

attributes.name: average_session_length_minutes
attributes.description: Mean duration of gameplay sessions in minutes during the metric period. Calculated as total playtime divided by session count.

attributes.name: churn_risk_score
attributes.description: Predictive score (0-100) indicating the likelihood of player churn within the next 7 days. Calculated from engagement patterns, session frequency, and days since last session.

attributes.name: cohort_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier for the player cohort to which this player belongs, typically based on registration date or acquisition campaign. Used for cohort-based retention and LTV analysis.

attributes.name: days_since_last_session
attributes.description: Number of calendar days elapsed since the players most recent session prior to this metric date. Used for churn risk assessment and re-engagement targeting.

attributes.name: engagement_score
attributes.description: Composite engagement score calculated from session frequency, playtime, and retention metrics. Normalized 0-100 scale for player segmentation and lifecycle management.

attributes.name: engagement_tier
attributes.description: Categorical segmentation of player engagement level. Whale = high-value highly engaged; Core = regular engaged; Casual = occasional; Dormant = at-risk; Churned = inactive; New = first-time.

attributes.name: first_session_date
attributes.description: The date of the players very first session across all platforms and titles. Anchors all retention calculations (D1, D7, D30).

attributes.name: ftue_completed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player has completed the First-Time User Experience tutorial or onboarding flow. Critical for retention analysis.

attributes.name: game_titles_played_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct game titles the player engaged with during the metric period. Measures cross-title engagement for multi-game publishers.

attributes.name: in_game_event_participation_count
attributes.description: Number of live in-game events (seasonal events, limited-time modes, tournaments) the player participated in during the metric period. Measures live-ops engagement.

attributes.name: is_d1_retained
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player returned on the day after their first session (D1 retention). Critical metric for First-Time User Experience (FTUE) effectiveness.

attributes.name: is_d30_retained
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player was active 30 days after their first session (D30 retention). Measures long-term player retention and game stickiness.

attributes.name: is_d7_retained
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player was active 7 days after their first session (D7 retention). Key indicator of early player lifecycle health.

attributes.name: is_dau
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player was active on this metric date. True if the player had at least one session during the day.

attributes.name: is_mau
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player was active during the month containing this metric date. True if the player had at least one session during the 30-day period.

attributes.name: is_wau
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player was active during the week containing this metric date. True if the player had at least one session during the 7-day period.

attributes.name: last_session_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the players most recent session end as of this metric date. Used for real-time churn prediction and re-engagement workflows.

attributes.name: lifecycle_stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the player lifecycle journey. Onboarding = new player in FTUE; Active = regular player; Engaged = highly active; At-risk = declining engagement; Churned = inactive; Reactivated = returned after churn.

attributes.name: login_streak_days
attributes.description: Number of consecutive days the player has logged in as of this metric date. Used for streak-based rewards and engagement incentives.

attributes.name: metric_date
attributes.description: The calendar date for which this engagement metric snapshot was calculated. Represents the business event date for the engagement measurement period.

attributes.name: metric_grain
attributes.description: The aggregation period for this engagement metric snapshot. Indicates whether this record represents daily, weekly, or monthly engagement data.

attributes.name: peak_ccu_contribution
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player was online during the peak concurrent user period for this metric date. Used for capacity planning and live-ops scheduling.

attributes.name: primary_platform
attributes.description: The platform on which the player spent the majority of their playtime during the metric period. Used for platform-specific engagement analysis.

attributes.name: pve_session_count
attributes.description: Number of PvE cooperative or solo gameplay sessions the player completed during the metric period. Measures single-player or co-op engagement.

attributes.name: pvp_match_count
attributes.description: Number of PvP competitive matches the player participated in during the metric period. Measures competitive engagement.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this engagement metric record was first created in the lakehouse. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this engagement metric record was last updated in the lakehouse. Used for change tracking and data freshness monitoring.

attributes.name: session_count
attributes.description: Total number of distinct gameplay sessions the player initiated during the metric period. A session is defined as a continuous period of player activity.

attributes.name: social_interaction_count
attributes.description: Number of social interactions (friend invites, guild joins, chat messages, co-op sessions) the player initiated during the metric period. Measures social engagement.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The analytics platform or system of record from which this engagement metric snapshot was sourced (e.g., GameAnalytics, Amplitude, internal telemetry).

attributes.name: total_playtime_minutes
attributes.description: Cumulative playtime in minutes across all sessions during the metric period. Measures total player engagement duration.

attributes.name: ugc_contribution_count
attributes.description: Number of user-generated content items (levels, mods, skins, replays) the player created or published during the metric period. Measures creative engagement.

products.name: dlc_purchase
products.description: This association product represents the transactional event between player_account and dlc_bundle. It captures the monetization relationship where players purchase downloadable content. Each record links one player_account to one dlc_bundle with transaction-specific attributes including purchase price, timestamp, platform, entitlement status, and activation details. This is the SSOT for revenue recognition, content access control, refund processing, and cross-platform entitlement management.. Existence Justification: In the gaming industry, players purchase multiple DLC bundles over their account lifetime, and each DLC bundle is purchased by thousands or millions of players. This is a core monetization relationship where the business actively manages individual purchase transactions with transaction-specific data (price paid, timestamp, platform, entitlement status, activation). The relationship is not derivable—it is the operational source of truth for revenue recognition, content access control, and refund processing.

attributes.name: dlc_purchase_id

attributes.name: activation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player first activated or downloaded the DLC content after purchase. Nullable if purchased but not yet activated. Used for engagement analytics and to distinguish purchased-but-unused content.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the purchase_price_paid. Supports multi-currency transactions and regional pricing strategies.

attributes.name: discount_applied
attributes.description: Total discount amount applied to this purchase in the transaction currency. Nullable if no discount. Used for promotional campaign effectiveness analysis.

attributes.name: entitlement_status
attributes.description: Current status of the players entitlement to access this DLC content. Active means player has access, revoked indicates access removed (e.g., chargeback), refunded means purchase was refunded, pending indicates payment processing, expired for time-limited content. Drives content access control systems.

attributes.name: payment_method

attributes.name: platform_code
attributes.description: The platform through which the purchase was made (PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Mobile). Critical for cross-platform entitlement management and platform-specific revenue sharing calculations.

attributes.name: purchase_price_paid
attributes.description: The actual amount paid by the player for this DLC bundle at the time of purchase. May differ from base_price_usd due to regional pricing, discounts, sales, or promotional offers. Critical for revenue recognition and refund calculations.

attributes.name: purchase_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player completed the purchase transaction. Used for revenue recognition timing, refund eligibility windows, and purchase history tracking.

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: Amount refunded to the player. Nullable if never refunded. May differ from purchase_price_paid due to partial refunds or platform fees.

attributes.name: refund_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the purchase was refunded. Nullable if never refunded. Triggers entitlement_status change to refunded and revenue reversal.

The authoritative SSOT for WHAT the business offers across all storefronts.

Each record captures milestone type, event date, approving authority, associated build or release reference, affected platforms, and event metadata. For end-of-life events: player notification method, refund policy, data retention policy, and regulatory compliance notes. The SSOT for lifecycle reporting, milestone tracking, and formal title retirement decisions.

products.name: leaderboard_entry
products.description: This association product represents the competitive ranking entry between a player account and a leaderboard. It captures each player's participation and performance on a specific leaderboard, including their rank position, score achieved, timestamp of achievement, season context, platform, rank tier, and percentile. Each record links one player_account to one leaderboard with attributes that exist only in the context of this competitive participation. This is the operational record used for rewards distribution, competitive matchmaking, player recognition, and leaderboard display.. Existence Justification: In gaming platforms, players compete on multiple leaderboards simultaneously (global, seasonal, mode-specific, regional, event-based), and each leaderboard ranks thousands to millions of players. The business actively manages leaderboard entries as operational records with lifecycle states (active, under review, disqualified, expired), tracks rank changes in real-time, enforces eligibility criteria, distributes rewards based on rank tiers, and uses entries for competitive matchmaking. Leaderboard entries are not derived analytics—they are operational business entities that players and game systems create, update, and query continuously.

attributes.name: leaderboard_entry_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this leaderboard entry. Primary key.

attributes.name: leaderboard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the leaderboard on which this entry appears

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the player account who achieved this leaderboard entry

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game season during which this leaderboard entry was achieved. Null for non-seasonal leaderboards. Critical for seasonal rewards and historical competitive tracking.

attributes.name: entry_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this leaderboard entry. Active entries are displayed on the leaderboard. Under_review entries are pending anti-cheat validation. Disqualified entries are removed due to cheating. Expired entries are from past seasons/resets.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this leaderboard entry was last updated (rank change, score improvement, status change). Used for change tracking and real-time leaderboard updates.

attributes.name: percentile
attributes.description: The player's percentile ranking on this leaderboard (e.g., 95.5 means top 4.5%). Calculated based on total ranked players. Used for player feedback and competitive context.

attributes.name: platform_code
attributes.description: The platform on which the player achieved this score (console, PC, mobile, or specific platform). Used for platform-specific leaderboards and cross-platform competitive analysis.

attributes.name: rank_position
attributes.description: The player's current rank position on this leaderboard (1 = top rank). Changes as other players submit scores. Used for rewards distribution and competitive display.

attributes.name: rank_tier
attributes.description: The competitive tier or bracket the player belongs to based on their rank position (e.g., top 10 = grandmaster, top 100 = master). Used for rewards distribution and player recognition.

attributes.name: reward_claimed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has claimed their reward for this leaderboard placement. Used for rewards distribution workflows and preventing duplicate claims.

attributes.name: score_value
attributes.description: The player's score or metric value that determines their rank on this leaderboard. Could be kills, win rate, completion time, points, etc., depending on the leaderboard's ranking_metric.

attributes.name: submission_count
attributes.description: Number of times the player has submitted a score to this leaderboard. Used to enforce min_matches_played eligibility criteria and track player engagement.

attributes.name: timestamp_achieved
attributes.description: Date and time when the player achieved this score or rank. Used for tie-breaking, historical tracking, and determining eligibility for time-bound rewards.

products.name: sku_deployment
products.description: This association product represents the deployment event between build_artifact and sku. It captures the operational process of deploying a specific build artifact to a specific SKU, including certification, rollout strategy, and lifecycle management. Each record links one build_artifact to one sku with attributes that exist only in the context of this deployment relationship. This is the authoritative record of what build is live on which SKU at any point in time.. Existence Justification: In game publishing operations, a single build artifact can be deployed to multiple SKUs (e.g., the same build deployed to PS5 Standard Edition, PS5 Deluxe Edition, and Xbox Series X Standard Edition), and a single SKU receives multiple build artifacts over its lifecycle (patches, hotfixes, content updates). Release engineering teams actively manage each deployment as a distinct operational event with its own certification workflow, phased rollout strategy, approval process, and potential rollback. This is not a reference lookup—it is a managed business process.

attributes.name: sku_deployment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this deployment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: build_artifact_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the build artifact being deployed

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or system account that initiated this deployment. Critical for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: title_sku_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the SKU receiving the deployment

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this deployment was approved by release management. Part of the deployment workflow and governance process.

attributes.name: certification_status
attributes.description: Platform certification status for this specific build-SKU deployment. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Different from build-level certification as each SKU may require separate platform approval.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this deployment record was created in the system.

attributes.name: deployment_date
attributes.description: The date and time when this build artifact was deployed to this SKU. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: deployment_notes
attributes.description: Internal notes about this specific deployment, including special considerations, dependencies, or operational context.

attributes.name: phased_rollout_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of users receiving this build in a phased rollout strategy. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Ranges from 0.00 to 100.00, enabling gradual deployment to mitigate risk.

attributes.name: rollback_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this deployment was rolled back due to issues. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Critical for incident tracking and deployment history.

attributes.name: rollback_reason

attributes.name: rollback_timestamp
