attributes.name: affected_region
attributes.description: Geographic region or data center location affected by the problem. Uses 3-letter region codes (e.g., USE, EUW, APS).

attributes.name: affected_service
attributes.description: Name of the game service or infrastructure component affected by this problem. Examples: matchmaking, authentication, CDN, game servers.

attributes.name: assigned_engineer
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the engineer currently assigned to investigate and resolve the problem.

attributes.name: assigned_team
attributes.description: Engineering team or group responsible for investigating and resolving the problem. Examples: DevOps, Network Engineering, Platform Engineering.

attributes.name: change_request_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the change request created to implement the permanent solution for this problem. Links problem to change management process.

attributes.name: closed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the problem record was formally closed after verification. Final lifecycle timestamp for the problem.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this problem record was created in the system. Audit field for record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the problem including symptoms, impact, and context. Provides comprehensive information for root cause analysis.

attributes.name: detected_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the problem was first detected or identified. Used for timeline analysis and response time measurement.

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: Method by which the problem was detected. Used to measure effectiveness of monitoring and proactive problem management.

attributes.name: downtime_minutes
attributes.description: Total service downtime in minutes caused by this problem. Used for SLA tracking and availability reporting.

attributes.name: incident_count
attributes.description: Number of incidents linked to this problem. Used to measure problem impact and prioritize resolution efforts.

attributes.name: investigation_started_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when formal investigation of the problem began. Used to track time-to-investigation metrics.

attributes.name: is_known_error
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this problem has been classified as a known error with documented workaround. True when root cause is identified but permanent fix is pending.

attributes.name: is_recurring
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this is a recurring problem that has occurred multiple times. Used to identify systemic issues requiring architectural changes.

attributes.name: permanent_solution
attributes.description: Description of the permanent fix or solution implemented to resolve the problem. Documents the final resolution approach.

attributes.name: player_impact_count
attributes.description: Estimated number of players affected by this problem. Critical metric for prioritization and business impact assessment.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level for problem resolution based on severity and business impact. P1 is highest priority requiring immediate action.

attributes.name: problem_number
attributes.description: Human-readable unique problem ticket number used for external reference and tracking. Format: PRB-YYYYMMDD.

attributes.name: problem_type
attributes.description: Classification of the problem by technical domain. Used for routing to appropriate engineering teams and trend analysis.

attributes.name: related_problem_id
attributes.description: Reference to another problem record that is related or linked to this problem. Enables tracking of problem dependencies and patterns.

attributes.name: resolved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the problem was resolved with a permanent solution. Used for resolution time tracking and SLA compliance.

attributes.name: root_cause
attributes.description: Identified root cause of the problem after investigation. Documents the underlying technical or process issue causing incidents.

attributes.name: root_cause_identified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the root cause was successfully identified. Used to measure investigation effectiveness and time-to-diagnosis.

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Severity level indicating the business impact and urgency of the problem. Critical problems affect core game services and require immediate attention.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the problem record. Tracks progression from identification through resolution and closure.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Short descriptive title summarizing the problem for quick identification and reporting.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last updated this problem record. Audit field for change accountability.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this problem record was last modified. Audit field for change tracking and data freshness.

attributes.name: workaround
attributes.description: Temporary workaround or mitigation steps to reduce impact while permanent fix is developed. Used for known error management.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who created this problem record. Audit field for accountability and traceability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: last_activation_timestamp

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this suppression rule record was last modified.

attributes.name: notification_override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this suppression rule also prevents notification delivery or only suppresses alert visibility.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Priority classification of the suppression rule determining its precedence when multiple rules apply to the same alert.

attributes.name: recurrence_pattern
attributes.description: Cron expression or schedule pattern defining recurring time windows when the suppression rule is active.

attributes.name: rule_code

attributes.name: rule_name

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the suppression rule based on its triggering mechanism and operational purpose.

attributes.name: scope

attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; Perforce Helix Core Version Control

attributes.name: has_waiver
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal risk-acceptance waiver has been granted for this defect, allowing the game to ship with the known issue. True = waiver approved. Critical for release governance and post-launch accountability.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; IGDA QA Best Practices; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: is_certification_blocker
attributes.description: Indicates whether this defect will block platform certification submission (e.g., fails a TRC or TCR requirement for PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo). True = certification cannot proceed until resolved. Critical for release gate management.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: is_escalated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this defect has been escalated beyond the standard triage process, typically due to severity, compliance impact, or executive visibility. True = escalated. Triggers additional reporting and stakeholder notification workflows.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: is_regression
attributes.description: Indicates whether this defect is a regression — a previously fixed issue that has reappeared in a newer build. True = confirmed regression. Used to track regression rate as a key release quality KPI and to flag CI/CD pipeline failures.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices; CI/CD Best Practices

attributes.name: jira_issue_key
attributes.description: The externally-known Jira issue key (e.g., GAME-1234) that uniquely identifies this defect in the source system of record. Used for cross-referencing with Jira dashboards, sprint boards, and release planning. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: linked_jira_issue_keys
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of related Jira issue keys (e.g., duplicate of, blocks, is blocked by, relates to). Preserves the Jira issue link graph in denormalized form for Silver layer analytics without requiring a separate junction table at this stage.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Business urgency level indicating how quickly the defect must be addressed relative to release schedules and player impact. Blocker = must fix before release; High = fix in current sprint; Medium = fix in near-term sprint; Low = fix when capacity allows. Distinct from severity — a cosmetic defect on the main menu may be low severity but high priority.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: regression_introduced_version
attributes.description: The build version in which the regression was reintroduced, if is_regression is True. Used to identify the offending code change or asset update via Perforce Helix Core history. Null if not a regression.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: reported_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the defect was first reported and logged in Jira. Serves as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this transaction. Used to calculate defect age, SLA compliance, and time-to-triage metrics.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: reproducibility
attributes.description: Indicates how consistently the defect can be reproduced following the documented reproduction steps. Always = 100% reproducible; Intermittent = occurs sometimes; Rare = very infrequent; Unable to Reproduce = cannot be replicated. Affects triage priority and fix confidence.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: reproduction_steps
attributes.description: Step-by-step instructions required to reliably reproduce the defect. Critical for developers to diagnose and fix the issue. Sourced from the Jira 'Steps to Reproduce' field.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: resolved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the defect was marked as resolved or fixed in Jira. Used to calculate time-to-fix, fix cycle time, and release readiness metrics. Null if the defect is not yet resolved.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the underlying cause of the defect used for trend analysis and process improvement. Examples: code logic error, asset pipeline issue, configuration error, third-party SDK defect, design specification gap, environment mismatch. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: code_logic|asset_pipeline|configuration|third_party_sdk|design_spec|environment|data_corruption|race_condition — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Technical impact level of the defect on game functionality or player experience. Critical = game crash or data loss; Major = significant feature broken; Minor = partial feature degradation; Trivial = cosmetic or negligible impact. Assigned during triage and may be updated post-triage.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this defect record originated. Jira is the primary source; Zendesk player support tickets, GameAnalytics crash reports, or manual playtesting logs may also feed defects. Used for data lineage and ETL audit.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; Zendesk; GameAnalytics/Amplitude

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Short, human-readable summary of the defect as entered in Jira. Used in dashboards, triage meetings, and release notes to identify the issue at a glance.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: triage_date
attributes.description: The date on which the defect was formally triaged by the QA lead and development team. Captures the most recent triage event date. Used to measure time-to-triage SLA compliance.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: triage_outcome
attributes.description: The formal decision reached during the most recent triage session. Accepted = will be fixed; Deferred = moved to a future release; Rejected = not a valid defect; Duplicate = already tracked under another issue; Won't Fix = known issue accepted as-is.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: triage_participants
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of workforce member names or IDs who participated in the triage session. Provides accountability and audit trail for triage decisions. Stored as a denormalized string for Silver layer simplicity.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this defect record was last modified in the data product. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field. Used to detect stale records and track synchronization lag from Jira.

attributes.name: waiver_approver
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized individual (e.g., QA Director, Studio Head, Legal) who approved the non-certification waiver. Provides accountability for risk-acceptance decisions.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; IGDA QA Best Practices; SOC 2

attributes.name: waiver_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the non-certification waiver expires and must be reviewed or renewed. Ensures waivers do not persist indefinitely and are re-evaluated at each release cycle. Null if no waiver exists.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; IGDA QA Best Practices; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: waiver_justification
attributes.description: Formal written justification for the risk-acceptance waiver, documenting why the defect is acceptable to ship. Required for audit and compliance purposes. Populated only when has_waiver is True.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; IGDA QA Best Practices; ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2

products.name: test_case
products.description: Master catalog of all test cases used across QA, UAT, performance, regression, and certification testing. Captures test case name, description, test type (functional, regression, performance, compliance, certification), preconditions, test steps, expected results, platform applicability, associated game component, automation flag, and ownership. Serves as the authoritative test case library for all QA activities.
products.reference: Jira Test Case / QA Test Library

String-level test coverage for localization quality a

attributes.name: test_suite_id

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or username of the QA lead or manager who approved this test case for active use in the test library. Provides governance accountability for test case quality and completeness.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this test case was formally approved by the QA lead and transitioned to active status. Supports audit trails for test case governance and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: automation_framework
attributes.description: Name of the automated testing framework or tool used to execute this test case when is_automated is True (e.g., 'Selenium', 'Appium', 'Unity Test Framework', 'Unreal Automation Tool', 'pytest', 'Robot Framework'). Null when the test case is manual.
attributes.references: CI/CD Pipeline Standards; Unity Test Framework; Unreal Automation Tool

attributes.name: automation_script_path
attributes.description: File path or repository reference (Perforce Helix Core depot path or Git URL) to the automation script that implements this test case. Enables traceability between the test case catalog and the version-controlled test code.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; CI/CD Pipeline Standards

attributes.name: build_version_introduced
attributes.description: The game build version or software version in which this test case was first introduced into the test library (e.g., '1.0.0', '2.3.1-beta'). Enables historical analysis of test coverage growth across build versions.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: certification_standard
attributes.description: The regulatory or platform certification standard that this test case validates compliance against. TRC/TCR are console manufacturer technical requirements; ESRB/PEGI/USK/CERO/GRAC are content rating body requirements; GDPR/COPPA are data privacy regulations; PCI DSS covers payment processing; WCAG covers accessibility. None indicates a non-compliance test case. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: TRC|TCR|ESRB|PEGI|USK|CERO|GRAC|GDPR|COPPA|PCI_DSS|WCAG|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ESRB; PEGI; USK; CERO; GRAC; GDPR Supervisory Authorities; COPPA Enforcement (FTC); PCI SSC; TRC/TCR; WCAG 2.1

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this test case record was first created in the QA system of record (Jira). Serves as the authoritative record creation audit timestamp for data lineage and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119-3; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability); ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: defect_count
attributes.description: The total number of active defects (Jira bugs) currently linked to this test case. Provides a quick indicator of the test case's defect discovery effectiveness and the current quality health of the associated game component. Not a calculated aggregate — sourced directly from Jira linkage metadata.

attributes.name: estimated_execution_mins
attributes.description: The estimated time in minutes required to execute this test case manually or via automation. Used for test planning, sprint capacity estimation, and QA resource allocation. Supports release timeline forecasting.

attributes.name: execution_environment
attributes.description: The target environment in which this test case is designed to be executed. Dev is the development sandbox; QA is the dedicated testing environment; staging mirrors production for pre-release validation; cert is the platform certification environment; production is for live-service monitoring tests.

attributes.name: expected_result
attributes.description: The precise, observable outcome that must occur for the test case to be considered passed. Defines the acceptance criterion against which actual test execution results are compared. Essential for pass/fail determination in both manual and automated QA runs.

attributes.name: game_component
attributes.description: The specific game system, module, or feature area that this test case targets (e.g., 'In-Game Store', 'Matchmaking', 'Player Inventory', 'FTUE', 'Anti-Cheat', 'Physics Engine', 'NPC AI'). Enables component-level quality reporting and defect trend analysis across the game title.
attributes.references: Unity/Unreal Engine Asset Pipeline; Jira Component Field

attributes.name: is_automated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test case is executed by an automated testing framework (True) or requires manual execution by a QA engineer (False). Drives CI/CD pipeline integration decisions and automation coverage reporting.
attributes.references: CI/CD Pipeline Standards; ISO/IEC 29119-5 Keyword-Driven Testing

attributes.name: is_certification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test case must pass as a mandatory requirement for platform certification submission (True). Certification-required tests are blocking for console, PC storefront, or mobile store submissions and must achieve a pass result before Gold Master sign-off.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: is_regression_candidate
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test case should be included in the standard regression test pack (True) for every build or patch release. Regression candidates are high-value tests that protect core game functionality and are executed as part of every CI/CD pipeline run.

attributes.name: jira_epic_key
attributes.description: Reference to the parent Jira Epic that this test case is associated with, enabling traceability from test coverage back to feature epics and OKRs. Supports release readiness reporting at the epic level.

attributes.name: jira_issue_key
attributes.description: The externally-known unique identifier for this test case as tracked in Jira (e.g., QA-1042). Serves as the business-facing reference across QA, development, and release management teams. Maps to the Jira Test issue type in the project management system of record.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Test Issue Type

attributes.name: last_executed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this test case was most recently executed. Used to identify stale test cases that have not been run recently and to track test execution cadence across QA cycles.

attributes.name: last_execution_result
attributes.description: The outcome of the most recent execution of this test case. Pass indicates the expected result was achieved; fail indicates a defect was found; blocked indicates execution was prevented by a dependency or environment issue; skipped indicates intentional exclusion; not_run indicates no execution has occurred yet.

attributes.name: last_passed_build
attributes.description: The most recent game build version in which this test case achieved a pass result. Used to identify stale or flaky tests and to assess the current health of test coverage relative to the active build.

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current state of the test case within its authoring and maintenance lifecycle. Draft indicates the test case is being authored and not yet approved for execution; active indicates it is approved and available for test runs; deprecated indicates it has been superseded by a newer version; archived indicates it is retained for historical reference only; under_review indicates it is pending QA lead approval.

attributes.name: owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the QA engineer, lead, or team responsible for authoring, maintaining, and reviewing this test case. Provides accountability and a point of contact for test case clarifications and updates.

attributes.name: owner_team
attributes.description: The QA team or functional group responsible for this test case (e.g., 'Core Gameplay QA', 'Platform Certification Team', 'Performance QA', 'Compliance QA', 'UAT Team'). Enables team-level quality metrics and workload distribution reporting.
attributes.references: IGDA QA Standards; Jira Team Field

attributes.name: pass_rate_pct
attributes.description: The historical pass rate of this test case expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00), calculated as the ratio of pass executions to total executions over the test case's lifetime. Identifies flaky or consistently failing tests for prioritized maintenance. Sourced from execution history aggregation in the QA system.

attributes.name: platform_applicability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of target platforms for which this test case is applicable (e.g., 'PC,PS5,Xbox Series X,iOS,Android,Switch'). Determines which platform-specific test runs should include this test case. Aligns with Steamworks, Console SDKs, and mobile store certification requirements.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies; TRC/TCR

attributes.name: preconditions
attributes.description: Describes the required system state, environment configuration, player account state, or data setup that must exist before the test case can be executed (e.g., 'Player must be logged in with a level 10 character and have 500 in-game currency'). Critical for reproducibility and automation setup.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Business-assigned priority level indicating the importance of executing this test case relative to others. Critical tests must pass before any release gate; high-priority tests cover core gameplay loops and monetization flows; medium covers secondary features; low covers edge cases and cosmetic validations. Drives test execution ordering and triage decisions.

attributes.name: release_milestone
attributes.description: The game release milestone or sprint to which this test case is associated (e.g., 'Alpha', 'Beta', 'Gold Master', 'Patch 1.2', 'DLC Drop 3'). Links test coverage to the release planning lifecycle and quality gate checkpoints.
attributes.references: Jira Release Planning; Gold Master Release Standards

attributes.name: requirement_reference
attributes.description: Identifier or reference to the business or technical requirement that this test case validates (e.g., a Jira story key, a GDD section reference, or a platform TRC/TCR requirement ID). Ensures full traceability from requirements through test coverage to defects.

attributes.name: review_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes added by the QA lead or reviewer during the test case review and approval process. Captures feedback, clarifications, or conditions for approval that are not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Indicates the potential impact on the game or platform if this test case fails. Blocker failures prevent release; major failures impact core gameplay or monetization; minor failures affect non-critical features; trivial failures are cosmetic or low-impact. Used in release quality gate assessments.

attributes.name: test_case_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the purpose, scope, and intent of the test case. Provides context for QA engineers and stakeholders on what business functionality or technical behavior is being validated.

attributes.name: test_case_name
attributes.description: Human-readable title of the test case that clearly identifies the scenario being validated (e.g., 'Verify player inventory persists after server restart'). Used as the primary display label in QA dashboards and test reports.

attributes.name: test_category
attributes.description: Secondary classification of the test case by its scope and coverage level within the QA process. Smoke tests validate basic build stability; integration tests verify cross-system interactions; localization tests validate regional language and cultural content; security tests verify DRM and anti-cheat integrity; accessibility tests validate compliance with platform accessibility guidelines. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: smoke|sanity|integration|unit|end_to_end|localization|security|accessibility — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119-1; IGDA QA Standards; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: test_steps
attributes.description: Step-by-step instructions for executing the test case, written in a numbered or structured format. Each step describes a discrete action the tester or automation script must perform. Sourced from Jira test management fields and serves as the authoritative execution guide.

attributes.name: test_type
attributes.description: Classification of the test case by its testing methodology and objective. Functional tests validate game features; regression tests ensure existing functionality is not broken by new changes; performance tests measure FPS, load times, and stability benchmarks; compliance tests verify ESRB/PEGI/GDPR/COPPA adherence; certification tests validate platform TRC/TCR requirements for console submission.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119-1; ESRB; PEGI; TRC/TCR Platform Certification

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this test case record was most recently modified. Tracks the recency of test case maintenance and supports change detection in ETL pipelines from Jira to the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version number of the test case following semantic versioning conventions (e.g., '1.0', '2.3', '1.0.1'). Incremented when test steps, expected results, or preconditions are materially changed. Supports change management and audit traceability.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119-3; Perforce Helix Core Version Control

attributes.description: The specific game build version being tested in the current active cycle. May differ from target_build_version if a hotfix build was submitted mid-cycle. Sourced from Perforce Helix Core.

attributes.name: current_cycle_number
attributes.description: The ordinal number of the currently active or most recently completed test cycle within this plan (e.g., 1 = first cycle, 2 = re-test cycle). Tracks iteration progression.

attributes.name: current_cycle_status
attributes.description: Execution status of the currently active test cycle. Values: planned (not yet started), active (execution in progress), completed (cycle finished), aborted (cycle terminated early due to blocking defects or build failure).
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: cycle_count
attributes.description: Total number of test execution cycles (iterations) defined under this test plan. Each cycle targets a specific build and has its own start/end dates, pass/fail results, and defect counts.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: defect_count_critical
attributes.description: Number of open or unresolved defects classified as Critical (P1) severity in the current cycle. Critical defects are showstoppers that block release. Sourced from Jira bug tracking.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal Defect Severity Classification Standard

attributes.name: defect_count_major
attributes.description: Number of open or unresolved defects classified as Major (P2) severity in the current cycle. Major defects significantly impact gameplay or platform certification. Sourced from Jira bug tracking.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal Defect Severity Classification Standard

attributes.name: defect_count_minor
attributes.description: Number of open or unresolved defects classified as Minor (P3) severity in the current cycle. Minor defects have limited gameplay impact and may be deferred post-launch. Sourced from Jira bug tracking.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal Defect Severity Classification Standard

attributes.name: defect_count_trivial
attributes.description: Number of open or unresolved defects classified as Trivial (P4) severity in the current cycle. Cosmetic or negligible issues typically deferred to a future patch. Sourced from Jira bug tracking.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal Defect Severity Classification Standard

attributes.name: entry_criteria
attributes.description: Conditions that must be met before test execution can begin (e.g., 'Build deployed to cert environment, smoke test passed, no P1 blockers open'). Enforces release gate discipline.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal Release Gate Standard

attributes.name: esrb_compliance_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) Compliance Verified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the game content tested in this plan has been verified as compliant with ESRB rating requirements for North American distribution. Required for all titles targeting North American retail and digital storefronts.
attributes.references: ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board); FTC Consumer Protection Standards

attributes.name: exit_criteria
attributes.description: Conditions that must be satisfied to declare the test plan complete and approve progression to the next release gate (e.g., '100% critical test cases executed, pass rate ≥ 95%, zero P1 defects open').
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal Release Gate Standard

attributes.name: jira_epic_key
attributes.description: The Jira epic key (e.g., QA-1042) that anchors this test plan within the project management system. Enables bidirectional traceability between the QA test plan and Jira sprint/backlog planning.

attributes.name: objectives
attributes.description: Stated quality objectives for this test plan (e.g., 'Validate all critical gameplay paths on PS5 prior to Gold Master submission'). Drives prioritization of test cases and defect triage decisions.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: pass_rate_pct
attributes.description: Current observed pass rate across all executed test cases in the active or most recently completed cycle (e.g., 97.50%). Compared against pass_threshold_pct to determine release gate eligibility.
attributes.references: Internal QA KPI Reporting Standard; ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing

attributes.name: pass_threshold_pct
attributes.description: Minimum required pass rate (as a percentage, e.g., 95.00) for this test plan to satisfy its exit criteria and unlock the associated release gate. Defined at plan authoring time.
attributes.references: Internal Release Gate Standard; ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing

attributes.name: pegi_compliance_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pan European Game Information (PEGI) Compliance Verified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the game content tested in this plan has been verified as compliant with PEGI rating requirements for European distribution. Required for all titles targeting European storefronts.
attributes.references: PEGI (Pan European Game Information); European Commission Digital Services Act

attributes.name: performance_fps_target
attributes.description: The minimum acceptable frames per second (FPS) performance benchmark that the game build must sustain during performance testing within this plan (e.g., 60.00 FPS for console, 30.00 FPS for mobile). Drives performance test pass/fail determination.
attributes.references: Internal Performance Testing Standard; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Guidelines

attributes.name: plan_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this test plan across QA tooling, Jira, and release management systems (e.g., TP-GAME2401). Serves as the business identifier for cross-system reference.

attributes.name: plan_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the QA test plan (e.g., 'PC Gold Master Regression — v2.4.1'). Used as the primary display label in QA dashboards and release gate reports.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the test plan. Controls workflow transitions and visibility in release gate dashboards. Values: draft (being authored), active (execution in progress), on_hold (paused), completed (all cycles finished), cancelled (abandoned).
attributes.references: Internal QA Process Standard; ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Classification of the test plan by testing methodology. Drives which test suites, entry/exit criteria templates, and reporting dashboards apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: regression|smoke|functional|performance|certification|uat|compliance|integration|localization|accessibility — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISTQB Software Testing Standard; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Guidelines

attributes.name: planned_end_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which test plan execution is planned to complete. Drives release gate scheduling and milestone dependency management.
attributes.references: Jira Sprint Planning; Internal Release Calendar Standard

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which test plan execution is planned to begin. Used for QA capacity planning, sprint scheduling in Jira, and release milestone alignment.
attributes.references: Jira Sprint Planning; Internal Release Calendar Standard

attributes.name: platform_scope
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of target platforms covered by this test plan (e.g., 'PC,PS5,XSX,iOS,Android'). Determines which platform-specific TRC/TCR certification checklists apply. Sourced from Steamworks/Console SDK certification requirements.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs Platform Certification; TRC/TCR Guidelines

attributes.name: qa_team_name
attributes.description: Name of the QA team or squad assigned to execute this test plan (e.g., 'Console Cert Team', 'Mobile QA Squad', 'Performance Lab'). Supports capacity planning and team-level reporting.

attributes.name: release_gate_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test plan has satisfied all exit criteria and the associated release gate has been formally approved (True) or not yet approved (False). Drives downstream build promotion workflows.
attributes.references: Internal Release Gate Standard; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Guidelines

attributes.name: scope_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of what is in scope and out of scope for this test plan. Captures game features, systems, and platforms explicitly included or excluded from testing coverage.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: target_build_version
attributes.description: The specific game build version string targeted by this test plan (e.g., '2.4.1.8823'). Sourced from Perforce Helix Core version control labels. Ensures QA results are traceable to an exact build artifact.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; Internal Build Management Standard

attributes.name: test_environment
attributes.description: The infrastructure environment in which testing is executed. Determines data isolation, build deployment pipeline, and certification validity. Values: dev, staging, cert (certification), production, sandbox.
attributes.references: Internal Infrastructure and QA Environment Standard; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: total_test_case_count
attributes.description: Total number of test cases included in this test plan across all test suites. Baseline denominator for pass rate, coverage, and execution progress calculations.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing; Internal QA Metrics Standard

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this test plan record was most recently modified. Supports incremental ETL processing, audit trails, and change detection in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

products.name: quality_test_execution
products.description: Transactional record capturing each individual execution of a test case within a test plan or test cycle. Records execution timestamp, tester identity, build version tested, platform, environment, execution result (pass, fail, blocked, skipped, not run), actual result notes, defect references raised, execution duration, and automation run flag. Primary source of QA execution evidence for release gates.
products.reference: Jira Test Execution / Test Run Record

attributes.name: quality_test_execution_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual test execution record within the QA system. Primary key for the test_execution data product.

attributes.name: ab_experiment_id

attributes.name: asset_id

attributes.name: asset_version_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.asset_version. Business justification: Test runs validate specific asset versions in build pipeline (automated asset validation on commit). Version-specific test results enable CI/CD quality gates and promotion decisions.

attributes.name: build_id

attributes.name: build_submission_id

attributes.name: drm_entitlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.drm_entitlement. Business justification: Test runs validate specific entitlement configurations; DRM test results required for cert submission and platform holder approval.

attributes.name: employee_id

attributes.name: game_server_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.game_server. Business justification: Test executions (automated and manual) run on specific game servers. Test result validation requires correlation with server build version, configuration, and performance metrics (FPS, latency) for ac

attributes.name: iap_transaction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to monetization.iap_transaction. Business justification: Test executions for IAP flows generate real or sandbox transactions (test purchases, refund flows, receipt validation) that must be traceable for validation, debugging, and platform certification evid

attributes.name: level_map_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.level_map. Business justification: Test runs target individual levels for validation (playthrough testing, performance profiling, accessibility checks). Level-specific test results enable per-level quality gates and release readiness a

attributes.name: ml_model_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.ml_model_registry. Business justification: ML models predict test outcomes or prioritize test cases; test executions validate model predictions and provide training data for model improvement and test optimization.

attributes.name: network_region_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.network_region. Business justification: Test executions target specific regions for geo-specific validation (latency SLAs, content availability, compliance). Certification testing requires regional execution tracking for platform-holder and

attributes.name: parent_execution_quality_test_execution_id

attributes.name: sprint_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to studio.sprint. Business justification: Test executions performed within sprint boundaries; QA velocity and sprint health metrics require sprint-level aggregation. Sprint retrospectives analyze test execution pass rates. Creating new sprint

attributes.name: storefront_id

attributes.name: telemetry_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.telemetry_event. Business justification: Automated test runs generate telemetry events; linking enables correlation of test failures with specific telemetry patterns for root cause analysis and test result validation.

attributes.name: test_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific test case that was executed in this run. Links to the test case definition containing expected results, preconditions, and test steps.

attributes.name: test_cycle_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.test_cycle. Business justification: Test executions occur within test cycles. test_execution has test_cycle_name (STRING) but no FK to test_cycle. Adding test_cycle_id FK allows joining to get cycle details. Cardinality: N test_executio

attributes.name: test_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the test plan or test cycle under which this execution was performed. Organises executions into release-gate or sprint-level QA campaigns.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Software Testing Standard; Jira Test Management

attributes.name: test_suite_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.test_suite. Business justification: quality_test_execution currently has test_suite_name as STRING (denormalized). Normalizing by adding test_suite_id FK to test_suite master reference table. The test_suite_name STRING column becomes re

attributes.name: tester_player_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to player.player_account. Business justification: When players participate in beta testing or crowdsourced QA programs (increasingly common in gaming), test executions performed by players (not employees) need player_account link for access control (

attributes.name: actual_result_notes
attributes.description: Free-text description of the actual observed outcome during test execution, contrasted against the expected result defined in the test case. Primary evidence field for defect reproduction and release gate review.

attributes.name: automation_framework
attributes.description: Name of the automated testing framework or tool used to execute this test (e.g., 'Selenium', 'Appium', 'Unity Test Framework', 'Unreal Automation Tool', 'pytest'). Populated only when is_automated is True.

attributes.name: automation_run_reference
attributes.description: External identifier of the CI/CD pipeline run or automated test job that triggered this execution (e.g., Jenkins build number, GitHub Actions run ID). Enables traceability from execution record back to the pipeline run.
attributes.references: CI/CD Pipeline Standards; Perforce Helix Core

attributes.name: build_version
attributes.description: Human-readable version string of the game build under test (e.g., 1.4.2.8731-rc1). Captured directly on the execution record for traceability without requiring a join to the build table in release gate reports.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core; Steamworks/Console SDK Certification

attributes.name: crash_occurred
attributes.description: Indicates whether the game application crashed during this test execution (True). A crash is a certification-blocking event on all first-party platforms and triggers mandatory defect creation and escalation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this test execution record was first persisted in the system. Distinct from execution_timestamp which captures the real-world event time.

attributes.name: device_model
attributes.description: Hardware model or device identifier of the machine used for this execution (e.g., 'PS5 DevKit CFI-7000', 'iPhone 15 Pro', 'Xbox Series X Dev Mode'). Supports hardware-specific defect reproduction and certification evidence.

attributes.name: evidence_attachment_url
attributes.description: URL or path to supporting evidence artefacts for this execution such as screenshots, video captures, log files, or crash dumps stored in the asset management system. Required for defect reproduction and certification submission packages.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119-3 Test Documentation; Platform Certification Submission Requirements

attributes.name: execution_duration_sec
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in seconds from execution start to completion. Used for performance benchmarking of test suites, identifying slow automated tests, and estimating QA cycle time for release planning.

attributes.name: execution_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this test execution was completed or terminated. Used in conjunction with execution_timestamp to derive execution duration for performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: execution_key
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally referenceable identifier for this execution record (e.g., QE-0001234). Used in QA reports, release notes, and cross-team communication as the business-facing execution reference.

attributes.name: execution_status
attributes.description: Current outcome or lifecycle state of this test execution. 'pass' indicates all assertions met; 'fail' indicates one or more assertions failed; 'blocked' indicates a prerequisite prevented execution; 'skipped' indicates intentional omission; 'not_run' indicates pending execution; 'in_progress' indicates active execution.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119-3 Test Documentation; Jira Test Management

attributes.name: execution_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which this test execution was initiated. Represents the real-world business event time and is the primary temporal anchor for release gate evidence and QA audit trails.

attributes.name: execution_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this execution was performed manually by a QA engineer or playtester, executed by an automated test framework (e.g., CI/CD pipeline), or a hybrid semi-automated approach requiring human validation steps.

attributes.name: fps_observed
attributes.description: Frames per second (FPS) recorded during this execution, applicable to performance and stability test cases. Used to validate performance benchmarks against target FPS thresholds defined in release quality gates.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Performance Testing; Platform TRC/TCR Performance Requirements

attributes.name: game_title_code
attributes.description: Short code identifying the game title under test (e.g., 'GAME_ALPHA', 'TITLE_X'). Enables cross-title QA reporting and defect density benchmarking across the studio portfolio.
attributes.references: Internal Game Title Registry; Steamworks/Console SDK

attributes.name: is_automated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test execution was triggered and run by an automated test framework (True) or performed manually by a QA engineer or playtester (False). Key metric for automation coverage reporting.

attributes.name: is_cert_blocking
attributes.description: Indicates whether a failure in this execution constitutes a platform certification blocker (True) per TRC/TCR requirements from first-party console manufacturers (Sony, Microsoft, Nintendo). Drives escalation workflows for certification readiness.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Console SDK TRC/TCR Certification Requirements; First-Party Certification Guidelines

attributes.name: is_regression
attributes.description: Indicates whether this execution is part of a regression test pass (True) verifying that previously passing functionality has not been broken by new changes, versus a new feature test (False).

attributes.name: jira_issue_key
attributes.description: The Jira ticket key of the defect or task raised as a result of this execution (e.g., 'GAME-4521'). Provides a direct cross-system link to the bug tracking system for defect lifecycle management.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking and Project Management

attributes.name: locale_code
attributes.description: IETF BCP 47 locale code representing the language and region setting active during this execution (e.g., 'en-US', 'ja-JP', 'de-DE'). Required for localisation QA tracking and PEGI/ESRB/USK/CERO regional compliance testing.
attributes.references: IETF BCP 47; PEGI; ESRB; USK; CERO; GRAC

attributes.name: memory_usage_mb
attributes.description: Peak memory consumption in megabytes observed during this execution, applicable to performance test cases. Validated against platform memory budget thresholds for certification readiness.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 29119 Performance Testing; Platform TRC/TCR Requirements

attributes.name: os_version
attributes.description: Version of the operating system or firmware on the test device at the time of execution (e.g., 'Windows 11 22H2', 'iOS 17.2', 'PS5 FW 7.00'). Critical for platform compatibility defect triage and certification evidence.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level of the test case at the time of execution, inherited from the test case definition. Drives triage ordering for blocked or failed executions and determines release gate blocking criteria.

attributes.name: release_version
attributes.description: The game release or patch version this execution is qualifying (e.g., 'v2.5.0', 'Patch 1.4.2'). Used to aggregate execution evidence per release for go/no-go release gate decisions.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core; Steamworks/Console SDK Certification

attributes.name: rerun_count
attributes.description: Number of times this specific test case has been re-executed within the same test cycle or plan. A high rerun count on a failing test indicates a persistent defect or flaky automated test requiring investigation.

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the defect or failure identified during this execution. 'blocker' indicates a showstopper preventing release; 'critical' indicates a severe functional failure. Nullable when execution result is pass or skipped.

attributes.name: steps_executed_count
attributes.description: Number of individual test steps executed within this test case run. Used to identify partial executions (e.g., blocked mid-step) and to calculate step-level pass rates for detailed QA reporting.

attributes.name: steps_passed_count
attributes.description: Number of individual test steps within this execution that produced a passing result. Enables granular step-level pass rate calculation alongside steps_executed_count.

attributes.name: test_category
attributes.description: Classification of the test type executed. 'certification' maps to TRC/TCR platform compliance tests; 'playtesting' captures structured player experience QA; 'uat' denotes User Acceptance Testing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: functional|regression|smoke|performance|certification|uat|playtesting|security|localization|accessibility|compatibility — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: test_environment
attributes.description: The deployment environment in which the test was executed. 'cert' denotes a platform certification environment (e.g., Sony DevKit, Xbox Dev Mode). Determines the validity of execution evidence for release gates.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this test execution record, such as a status update, defect linkage, or result note amendment.

products.name: test_cycle
products.description: Master record representing a planned and executed iteration of testing activity (e.g., sprint QA cycle, regression cycle, certification cycle, UAT cycle). Captures plan scope, objectives, entry/exit criteria, test environment, assigned QA team, start/end dates, target build, platform scope, total test cases assigned, pass rate, defect count by severity, pass/fail thresholds, release gate linkage, and cycle status (planned, active, completed, aborted). Serves as both the planning artifact and execution container for all QA testing iterations.
products.reference: Jira Test Cycle / QA Sprint Cycle

attributes.name: test_cycle_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the test cycle record. Primary key for the test_cycle data product in the quality domain.

attributes.name: content_release_id

attributes.references: Internal Workforce Master Data; ISTQB Test Manager Role Definition

attributes.name: game_studio_id
attributes.description: Reference to the development studio responsible for the build under test. Enables studio-level QA performance reporting and accountability tracking.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title (IP) that this test cycle is scoped to. Links the cycle to the specific game product under test.

attributes.name: jira_sprint_id
attributes.description: The Jira sprint identifier associated with this test cycle, linking QA execution to the development sprint cadence. Enables sprint-level quality reporting and velocity correlation.

attributes.name: platform_cert_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.cert_submission. Business justification: Test cycles validate cert submission candidates; cycle completion gates submission approval and provides evidence for platform holder certification.

attributes.name: release_gate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the formal release gate or milestone record that this test cycle is linked to. Connects the test cycle execution results to the release decision workflow.
attributes.references: Internal Release Management Process; TRC/TCR Platform Certification

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.storefront. Business justification: Test cycles organized per platform for certification readiness; each platform has separate gold master approval workflows. Replaces string platform_scope with proper FK.

attributes.name: test_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.test_plan. Business justification: Test cycles execute test plans. test_cycle has cycle_type, cycle_objective but no FK to test_plan. Cycles are iterations of plan execution. Cardinality: N test_cycles : 1 test_plan. Adding test_plan_i

attributes.name: tournament_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to esports.tournament. Business justification: Tournament-specific test cycles (pre-event regression, patch validation, LAN environment testing) must reference the tournament for scheduling coordination, gate approval, and competitive readiness si

attributes.name: abort_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason this test cycle was aborted before completion (e.g., 'Critical P1 blocker in build rendering all test cases invalid — new build required'). Populated only when status = 'aborted'. Supports root cause analysis and process improvement.
attributes.references: Internal QA Incident Management; Jira Bug Tracking

attributes.name: actual_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when test cycle execution actually concluded (completed or aborted). Used to calculate cycle duration and compare against planned schedule.
attributes.references: Internal QA Execution Tracking; ISTQB Test Execution Metrics

attributes.name: actual_pass_rate_pct
attributes.description: The actual pass rate percentage achieved in this test cycle, calculated as (test_cases_passed / test_cases_executed) * 100. Compared against pass_rate_threshold_pct to determine release gate pass/fail status.
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Effectiveness Metrics; Internal QA Release Gate Policy

attributes.name: actual_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when test cycle execution actually commenced. Compared against planned_start_date to measure schedule adherence and QA process efficiency.
attributes.references: Internal QA Execution Tracking; ISTQB Test Execution Metrics

attributes.name: certification_body
attributes.description: The external certification or rating authority whose requirements are being validated in this test cycle (e.g., ESRB, PEGI, Sony TRC, Microsoft TCR). attributes.name: compliance_framework

attributes.references: GDPR Supervisory Authorities; COPPA (FTC); PCI SSC; ISO/IEC 27001; ESRB; PEGI

attributes.name: created_timestamp
