attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability); ISO/IEC 27001 Audit Trail Requirements; SOC 2

attributes.name: cycle_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title of the test cycle (e.g., 'Sprint 42 QA Regression', 'Platform Certification Cycle — PS5 v2.1.0', 'UAT Cycle — Season 3 Launch'). Used for identification in dashboards and reports.

attributes.name: cycle_objective
attributes.description: Free-text description of the primary business and quality objectives for this test cycle (e.g., 'Validate all P1/P2 regression scenarios for Season 3 content drop prior to live ops deployment'). Provides context for stakeholders reviewing cycle results.
attributes.references: Internal QA Process Standard; ISTQB Test Plan Objective Definition

attributes.name: cycle_type
attributes.description: Classification of the test cycle by its testing methodology and purpose. Drives which test suites, entry/exit criteria, and reporting templates apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: regression|certification|uat|smoke|performance|compliance|playtesting — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Cycle Classification; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: defect_count_p1
attributes.description: Number of open or total P1 (Critical/Blocker) severity defects identified during this test cycle. P1 defects represent game-breaking issues that prevent core functionality and are hard blockers for release. Tracked separately per severity for release gate assessment.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Priority/Severity Model; Internal Defect Severity Classification; TRC/TCR Platform Certification

attributes.name: defect_count_p2
attributes.description: Number of open or total P2 (Major) severity defects identified during this test cycle. P2 defects represent significant functional issues that degrade player experience but have workarounds. Tracked for release gate threshold evaluation.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Priority/Severity Model; Internal Defect Severity Classification

attributes.name: defect_count_p3
attributes.description: Number of open or total P3 (Minor) severity defects identified during this test cycle. P3 defects represent low-impact issues that do not block release but are tracked for quality trending and backlog management.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Priority/Severity Model; Internal Defect Severity Classification

attributes.name: entry_criteria
attributes.description: Defined conditions that must be met before the test cycle can begin execution (e.g., 'Build deployed to QA environment, smoke test passed, all P0 blockers resolved'). Enforces quality gates at cycle initiation.
attributes.references: ISTQB Entry Criteria Definition; Internal QA Gate Policy

attributes.name: exit_criteria
attributes.description: Defined conditions that must be satisfied for the test cycle to be declared complete and eligible for release gate sign-off (e.g., '95% pass rate, zero open P1 defects, all certification test cases executed'). Drives release readiness decisions.
attributes.references: ISTQB Exit Criteria Definition; TRC/TCR Platform Certification; Internal Release Gate Policy

attributes.name: gate_waiver_justification
attributes.description: Documented business justification for overriding a failed release gate (populated only when release_gate_status = 'waived'). Records the rationale, risk acceptance, and authorizing stakeholder for audit and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: Internal Release Gate Waiver Policy; SOC 2 Change Management Controls; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: is_gold_master_candidate
attributes.description: Indicates whether the build under test in this cycle is a Gold Master (GM) candidate — the final release-ready build submitted for platform certification and manufacturing. Flags cycles that are part of the final pre-launch quality gate process.
attributes.references: Internal Gold Master Release Process; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: is_regression_baseline
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test cycle has been designated as the official regression baseline for the associated game title and build version. Baseline cycles serve as the reference point for future regression comparisons and stability benchmarking.
attributes.references: Internal QA Regression Baseline Policy; ISTQB Regression Testing Standard

attributes.name: jira_cycle_key
attributes.description: The externally-known Jira issue or sprint key that uniquely identifies this test cycle in the Jira project management system (e.g., QA-1042). Serves as the cross-system business identifier linking the test cycle to its Jira sprint or epic.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Sprint/Epic Key Convention

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for QA leads to capture additional context, observations, or stakeholder communications relevant to this test cycle that are not captured in structured fields (e.g., environment anomalies, scope changes, external dependency impacts).

attributes.name: pass_rate_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The minimum required pass rate percentage (e.g., 95.00) that must be achieved for this test cycle to satisfy the release quality gate. Defined at cycle planning time based on cycle type and platform requirements.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Gate Policy; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: planned_end_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which test cycle execution is planned to conclude. Used for release gate scheduling and QA timeline commitments.
attributes.references: Internal QA Planning Standard; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which test cycle execution is planned to begin. Used for capacity planning, resource scheduling, and release timeline management.
attributes.references: Internal QA Planning Standard; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: qa_team_size
attributes.description: Number of QA testers assigned to execute this test cycle. Used for capacity planning, workload distribution analysis, and QA resource utilization reporting.
attributes.references: Internal QA Resource Management; ISTQB Test Team Composition

attributes.name: release_gate_status
attributes.description: The outcome of the release quality gate assessment for this test cycle. 'pending' = gate evaluation not yet performed; 'passed' = all exit criteria and thresholds met; 'failed' = one or more exit criteria not met; 'waived' = gate failure acknowledged and overridden by authorized stakeholder with documented justification.
attributes.references: Internal Release Gate Policy; TRC/TCR Platform Certification; PEGI/ESRB Compliance Readiness

attributes.name: target_build_version
attributes.description: The specific game build version (e.g., '2.1.0.4521') that this test cycle is scoped to test. Aligns with the build label in Perforce Helix Core version control. Critical for traceability between defects and the build under test.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Build Labeling Convention; Semantic Versioning (SemVer) 2.0

attributes.name: test_cases_blocked
attributes.description: Number of test cases that could not be executed due to a blocking defect, environment issue, or dependency. Blocked cases are excluded from pass rate calculations and flagged for root cause analysis.
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Execution Status; Internal QA Blocked Case Policy

attributes.name: test_cases_executed
attributes.description: Number of test cases that have been executed (run) within this test cycle as of the latest update. Tracks execution progress against the total assigned scope.
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Execution Progress Metrics; Internal QA Reporting

attributes.name: test_cases_failed
attributes.description: Number of executed test cases that have resulted in a failure within this test cycle. Drives defect creation workflows and release gate blocking decisions.
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Result Metrics; Internal QA Defect Management Policy

attributes.name: test_cases_passed
attributes.description: Number of executed test cases that have achieved a passing result within this test cycle. Used as the numerator for pass rate calculation and release gate assessment.
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Result Metrics; Internal QA Release Gate Policy

attributes.name: test_cycle_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the test cycle. Drives workflow routing, reporting visibility, and release gate eligibility. 'planned' = scheduled but not started; 'active' = execution in progress; 'completed' = all test cases executed and results recorded; 'aborted' = terminated before completion; 'on_hold' = paused pending external dependency.
attributes.references: Internal QA Lifecycle Governance; Jira Sprint State Model

attributes.name: test_environment
attributes.description: Name or description of the QA environment configuration used for this test cycle (e.g., 'QA-ENV-03 — PS5 DevKit Firmware 8.0, Build Server B'). Ensures reproducibility and traceability of test results to a specific environment state.
attributes.references: Internal QA Environment Management Standard; ISO/IEC 29119 Test Environment

attributes.name: total_test_cases
attributes.description: Total number of test cases assigned to this test cycle at the time of planning. Represents the full scope of testing work planned for the cycle. Used for capacity planning and pass rate denominator calculations.
attributes.references: ISTQB Test Coverage Metrics; Internal QA Capacity Planning

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this test cycle record was most recently modified. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability); ISO/IEC 27001 Audit Trail Requirements; SOC 2

products.name: defect_triage
products.description: Transactional record capturing the formal triage event for a defect, including triage date, triage outcome (accepted, rejected, deferred, duplicate, by-design), assigned severity and priority post-triage, triage participants, target fix version, and escalation flag. Tracks the decision-making lifecycle of defects from discovery through disposition. Sourced from Jira workflow transitions and triage meeting records.

attributes.name: defect_triage_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the defect triage event record in the quality domain Silver layer.

attributes.name: compliance_incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_incident. Business justification: Triage sessions can identify defects that constitute compliance incidents (privacy breach, age-gate failure). Real business process: compliance escalation during defect triage.

attributes.name: defect_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent defect record that this triage event is associated with. Maps to the defect entity in the quality domain.

attributes.name: experiment_assignment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.experiment_assignment. Business justification: Triage teams need to know if defect reporters were in experiments to assess if bug is experiment-induced; critical for determining root cause and experiment safety.

attributes.name: game_studio_id
attributes.description: Reference to the development studio responsible for the game title associated with this defect. Enables studio-level quality KPI reporting.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title against which this defect triage is recorded. Enables cross-title defect quality benchmarking and release readiness reporting.

attributes.name: primary_defect_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or QA lead who chaired the triage session and is accountable for the triage outcome decision. Maps to the workforce/employee entity.
attributes.references: Jira Triage Meeting Record; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: tertiary_defect_reporter_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the QA tester, player support agent, or community manager who originally reported the defect. Maps to the workforce/employee entity. Corresponds to the Jira 'Reporter' field.

attributes.name: affected_game_area
attributes.description: The functional area or system of the game affected by the defect (e.g., 'FTUE', 'PvP Matchmaking', 'In-Game Store/MTX', 'NPC AI', 'Audio', 'UI/HUD', 'Save System'). Sourced from Jira component field. Enables area-level defect density analysis.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Component Field; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: affected_game_version
attributes.description: The game build version string in which the defect was first observed (e.g., 1.4.2.1087). Aligns with the version label tracked in Perforce Helix Core and Jira fix version fields.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core — Changelist/Label; Jira Fix Version

attributes.name: affected_platform
attributes.description: The target platform(s) on which the defect is reproducible (e.g., PS5, Xbox Series X, PC, iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch). Sourced from Jira custom field aligned to Steamworks/Console SDK platform identifiers. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PC|PS5|Xbox_Series_X|Xbox_Series_S|Nintendo_Switch|iOS|Android|PS4|Xbox_One — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs — Platform Certification; TRC/TCR

attributes.name: certification_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this defect poses a risk to platform certification submission (TRC/TCR compliance for console platforms such as PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo). True = certification risk identified during triage.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Console SDK TRC; TCR; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this triage record was first created in the system, corresponding to the Jira workflow transition that initiated the triage state. Audit trail field for data lineage.
attributes.references: Jira Workflow Transition Log; ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2

attributes.name: duplicate_of_jira_key
attributes.description: When triage_outcome is 'duplicate', this field records the Jira issue key of the canonical (master) defect that this issue duplicates. Enables duplicate chain analysis and defect deduplication reporting.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Duplicate Link Type

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this defect has been escalated beyond the standard triage process (e.g., to executive leadership, platform holder, or external certification body). True = escalated; False = standard triage path.
attributes.references: Jira Escalation Workflow; Steamworks/Console SDK TRC

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of why the defect was escalated, such as platform certification risk, player safety concern, legal/regulatory exposure, or executive visibility requirement. Populated only when escalation_flag is True.
attributes.references: Jira Escalation Workflow; ESRB; PEGI; GDPR Supervisory Authorities

attributes.name: estimated_fix_effort
attributes.description: T-shirt size estimate of the engineering effort required to resolve the defect, as assessed during triage. Used for sprint capacity planning in Jira and release schedule risk assessment.
attributes.references: Jira Sprint Planning — Story Points / Effort Estimation; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: jira_epic_key
attributes.description: The Jira epic key to which this defect is linked, enabling roll-up of defect counts by feature area or release milestone epic.

attributes.name: jira_issue_key
attributes.description: The externally-known Jira issue key (e.g., QA-1042) that uniquely identifies the defect in the Jira project management system. Serves as the business-facing identifier for cross-team communication and triage meeting references.

attributes.name: live_ops_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the defect affects live service operations such as GaaS event scheduling, in-game store/MTX transactions, matchmaking, or DAU/MAU tracking. True = live ops team must be notified. Critical for games operating under a Game-as-a-Service (GaaS) model.
attributes.references: GameAnalytics/Amplitude — Live Ops Events; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: monetization_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the defect directly impacts in-game monetization flows including IAP, MTX, virtual currency, or the in-game store. True = revenue risk; requires immediate escalation to monetization and finance teams.
attributes.references: PCI SSC — PCI DSS; IGDA QA Best Practices; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

attributes.name: player_facing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the defect is visible or impactful to end players (True) versus being an internal/backend-only issue (False). Influences prioritization, player communication decisions, and NPS/CSAT risk assessment.
attributes.references: IGDA QA Best Practices; Zendesk Player Support

attributes.name: post_triage_priority
attributes.description: The official fix priority assigned during triage, reflecting urgency relative to release schedule and business impact. 'blocker' indicates the defect must be resolved before any release can proceed; used to drive sprint backlog ordering in Jira.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Priority Field; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: post_triage_severity
attributes.description: The official defect severity level confirmed or reassigned by the triage panel after deliberation. Severity reflects the impact of the defect on game functionality, player experience, or platform certification compliance (e.g., critical = game-breaking crash or TRC/TCR failure).
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Severity Field; Steamworks/Console SDK TRC; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: pre_triage_severity
attributes.description: The defect severity level assigned by the reporter or QA engineer prior to the formal triage session. Captured to enable comparison with post-triage severity and measure triage calibration accuracy.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Severity Field; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this defect has regulatory or legal compliance implications (e.g., GDPR data handling, COPPA age-gating, ESRB/PEGI rating content, PCI DSS payment flow). True = compliance review required.
attributes.references: GDPR Supervisory Authorities; COPPA (FTC); ESRB; PEGI; PCI SSC; FTC

attributes.name: release_gate_impact
attributes.description: Classification of how this defect impacts the release quality gate decision. 'blocks_release' means the defect must be fixed before any release; 'blocks_certification' means it prevents platform submission; 'watch_list' means it is monitored but does not block; 'no_impact' means it does not affect release readiness.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Console SDK TRC; TCR; IGDA QA Best Practices; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: reproduction_rate
attributes.description: The frequency with which the defect can be reproduced under the documented steps, as assessed during triage. Informs fix prioritization and test case design.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Reproducibility Field; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level categorization of the defect root cause as determined during triage. 'third_party_sdk' covers issues originating from Unity, Unreal Engine, or platform SDKs. 'platform_specific' covers hardware/OS-level issues. Drives root cause trend analysis for process improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: code_defect|asset_error|design_issue|environment|third_party_sdk|platform_specific|data_issue|unknown — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Root Cause Field; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: target_fix_sprint
attributes.description: The Jira sprint name or identifier to which the defect fix has been assigned during triage (e.g., 'Sprint 42 - Gold Candidate'). Enables sprint-level defect burn-down reporting.

attributes.name: target_fix_version
attributes.description: The planned game release version in which the defect fix is scheduled to be delivered, as assigned during triage. Drives sprint planning in Jira and release readiness gate tracking.
attributes.references: Jira Fix Version Field; Perforce Helix Core — Release Label

attributes.name: triage_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the formal triage event occurred. Used for scheduling, SLA tracking, and release readiness reporting.
attributes.references: Jira Workflow Transition — Triage Meeting Record

attributes.name: triage_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes recorded during the triage session capturing discussion context, decision rationale, open questions, or conditions attached to the triage outcome. Sourced from Jira comment or triage meeting minutes.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Comment Field; Triage Meeting Record

attributes.name: triage_outcome
attributes.description: The formal disposition decision reached during triage. 'accepted' means the defect is confirmed and scheduled for fix; 'rejected' means it is not a valid defect; 'deferred' means fix is postponed to a future release; 'duplicate' means it duplicates an existing issue; 'by_design' means the behavior is intentional; 'needs_more_info' means additional reproduction data is required before a decision can be made.
attributes.references: Jira Workflow — Issue Resolution; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: triage_participant_count
attributes.description: The number of stakeholders who participated in the triage session for this defect (e.g., QA lead, producer, engineer, platform compliance officer). Supports governance and quorum validation for triage decisions.
attributes.references: Jira Triage Meeting Record; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: triage_participant_roles
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of functional roles represented in the triage session (e.g., 'QA Lead, Producer, Platform Engineer, Compliance Officer'). Captures governance breadth without storing individual PII.
attributes.references: Jira Triage Meeting Record; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: triage_sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the triage event occurred outside the defined SLA window for the defect's severity level (e.g., critical defects must be triaged within 4 hours). True = SLA was breached. Supports QA process compliance reporting.
attributes.references: IGDA QA Best Practices; Internal QA SLA Policy

attributes.name: triage_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the triage event itself. 'pending' indicates triage is scheduled but not yet conducted; 'in_progress' indicates the triage session is active; 'completed' indicates a final disposition has been recorded; 'cancelled' indicates the triage was abandoned.

attributes.name: triage_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the triage decision was recorded in Jira. Distinct from triage_date which captures day-level scheduling; this field captures the exact workflow transition moment.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this triage record was last modified, capturing any post-triage updates such as severity reassignment, escalation changes, or fix version updates. Audit trail field for data lineage.
attributes.references: Jira Workflow Transition Log; ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2

attributes.name: workaround_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether a player-facing or operational workaround exists for the defect, as determined during triage. True = a workaround has been identified and documented, which may influence deferral decisions.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Workaround Field; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: workaround_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the available workaround for the defect. Populated only when workaround_available is True. Used by player support (Zendesk) and community management teams to communicate interim guidance.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Workaround Field; Zendesk Knowledge Base

products.name: playtest_session
products.description: Transactional record for each formal playtesting session conducted during game development. Captures session date, type (internal, external, focus group, blind test, accessibility), game title/build, platform, participant count, duration, facilitator, objectives, key findings summary, usability issues, FTUE feedback flags, and satisfaction scores (NPS/CSAT). SSOT for playtesting activity scheduling and aggregate session outcomes.

attributes.name: playtest_session_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each formal playtesting session record in the quality domain. Primary key for this transactional entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: ab_experiment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.ab_experiment. Business justification: Playtests often evaluate experimental features; linking enables analysis of playtest feedback by experiment variant to inform rollout decisions and variant selection.

attributes.name: age_verification_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.age_verification_event. Business justification: Playtests with minors require age verification events for COPPA compliance. Real business process: minor participant compliance and parental consent tracking.

attributes.name: build_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.build_submission. Business justification: Playtests validate specific cert submission candidates; feedback determines submission readiness and identifies blocking issues before platform holder review.

attributes.name: certification_checklist_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.certification_checklist. Business justification: Playtests validate TRC/TCR compliance (age ratings, accessibility features); findings map to checklist requirements for cert readiness assessment.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the QA lead or researcher who facilitated and was responsible for conducting this playtesting session. The primary party reference for this transaction.
attributes.references: Internal Workforce Master Data; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: finance_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget. Business justification: Playtest sessions incur direct costs (participant compensation, facilities, equipment) charged to marketing or research budgets. Finance tracks playtest spend for cost control and capitalization decis

attributes.name: game_mode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to title.game_mode. Business justification: Playtest sessions evaluate specific game modes (multiplayer, campaign, battle royale) for balance, fun, and retention. Mode-level feedback aggregation drives design iteration. Replaces string game_mod

attributes.name: game_server_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.game_server. Business justification: Playtest sessions run on dedicated game servers. Session feedback (fun rating, usability issues) must be correlated with server performance metrics (FPS, latency, crash count) for build quality assess

attributes.name: game_studio_id
attributes.description: Reference to the development studio responsible for the game build under test. Enables quality benchmarking and defect trend analysis across studios within the enterprise.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title under playtesting. Links the session to the specific intellectual property (IP) being evaluated, enabling quality trend analysis by game title.

attributes.name: milestone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to studio.milestone. Business justification: Playtests scheduled around milestone reviews (vertical slice, alpha, beta); studios track which milestone a playtest validates. Milestone sign-off requires playtest feedback incorporation. Creating ne

attributes.name: network_region_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.network_region. Business justification: Playtest sessions target specific regions for player experience validation. Regional performance benchmarking and certification readiness assessment require region context for latency, content availab

attributes.name: participant_player_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to player.player_account. Business justification: Playtest sessions recruit specific player accounts (often from targeted segments like high-engagement or VIP players) to participate in closed alpha/beta tests. Recruitment tracking, NDA enforcement,

attributes.name: platform_sku_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.platform_sku. Business justification: Playtests validate specific SKU configurations (edition features, regional content); feedback is SKU-specific for edition differentiation validation.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the target platform on which the game build was tested (e.g., PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, PC, iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch). Platform-specific quality metrics and TRC/TCR compliance are tracked at this level.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs — Platform Certification; TRC (Technical Requirements Checklist)

attributes.name: tournament_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to esports.tournament. Business justification: Tournament patch playtests (pre-event validation with pro players, balance testing for competitive meta) must reference the tournament for feedback routing, patch approval decisions, and competitive r

attributes.name: accessibility_evaluated
attributes.description: Indicates whether accessibility features (e.g., colorblind modes, subtitle options, motor accessibility controls) were formally evaluated during this session. Supports compliance with platform holder accessibility requirements and IGDA accessibility guidelines.
attributes.references: IGDA Accessibility SIG Guidelines; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: avg_fps_recorded
attributes.description: Average frames per second (FPS) measured across the session when performance_evaluated is true. A primary technical quality metric for game stability and player experience. Compared against platform-specific FPS targets (e.g., 30 FPS, 60 FPS).
attributes.references: FPS (Frames Per Second) Technical Standard; TRC (Technical Requirements Checklist); Console SDK Performance Requirements

attributes.name: bugs_logged_count
attributes.description: Total number of defects and bugs formally logged in Jira as a direct result of this playtesting session. Provides a quantitative measure of session productivity and build quality.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Issue Count; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: build_label
attributes.description: Human-readable label or codename assigned to the game build in Perforce Helix Core (e.g., 'Alpha-Sprint-42', 'RC1-Candidate', 'Gold-Master-Candidate'). Complements build_version with a descriptive milestone identifier used in QA communications.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core — Label Management; Gold Master Release Convention

attributes.name: build_version
attributes.description: Specific software build version of the game tested during this session (e.g., 1.4.2.1087). Sourced from Perforce Helix Core version control. Critical for correlating defects and findings to a precise code baseline and for regression tracking.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core — Changelist/Label Convention; Semantic Versioning (SemVer) 2.0

attributes.name: certification_readiness_status
attributes.description: Assessment of the build's readiness for submission to platform holder certification (TRC/TCR compliance for PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Apple, Google). Distinct from general release readiness — specifically tracks platform certification gate status.
attributes.references: TRC (Technical Requirements Checklist); TCR (Technical Certification Requirements); Steamworks/Console SDK Certification; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: consent_collected
attributes.description: Indicates whether informed consent was collected from all participants prior to the session, including consent for data recording, observation, and use of feedback. Mandatory for GDPR and COPPA compliance when participant data is collected.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent); COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) — FTC Enforcement; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: crash_count
attributes.description: Total number of game crashes or critical application failures observed across all participants during the session. A key stability metric for release readiness gates and platform certification (TRC/TCR) compliance.
attributes.references: TRC (Technical Requirements Checklist); TCR (Technical Certification Requirements); Steamworks/Console SDK Certification

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this playtesting session record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: critical_bugs_count
attributes.description: Number of bugs logged from this session classified as Critical or Blocker severity in Jira. Critical bugs are blockers for release and are tracked separately for executive QA dashboards and release quality gates.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking — Priority/Severity Classification; Release Quality Gate Standards

attributes.name: csat_score
attributes.description: Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT) collected from session participants, typically on a 1–5 or 1–10 scale. Measures overall satisfaction with the game experience during the session. Complements NPS with a direct satisfaction measure.
attributes.references: CSAT (Customer Satisfaction Score) Industry Standard; GameAnalytics/Amplitude Player Satisfaction Metrics

attributes.name: difficulty_rating
attributes.description: Participant-reported perceived difficulty rating for the game content tested, typically on a 1–10 scale. Used to calibrate game balance, difficulty curves, and onboarding design. Critical input for game design iteration.
attributes.references: IGDA Playtesting Best Practices; Game Balance Design Standards

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Actual elapsed duration of the playtesting session in minutes, derived from start and end timestamps and stored for direct reporting use. Key metric for QA capacity planning and session effectiveness analysis.

attributes.name: end_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the playtesting session concluded. Combined with start_timestamp to derive actual session duration for QA reporting and capacity planning.

attributes.name: esrb_content_flags
attributes.description: Content descriptors or flags identified during the session that are relevant to ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board) or PEGI content rating compliance (e.g., 'Violence', 'Language', 'In-Game Purchases'). Supports rating submission accuracy and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board) Content Descriptor Standards; PEGI (Pan European Game Information) Content Descriptors; FTC Advertising Standards

attributes.name: ftue_evaluated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the First-Time User Experience (FTUE) flow was a specific evaluation objective of this playtesting session. FTUE quality is a critical KPI for player acquisition and D1 retention.
attributes.references: FTUE (First-Time User Experience) Industry Standard; D1 Retention KPI

attributes.name: fun_rating
attributes.description: Participant-reported fun/enjoyment rating for the game experience, typically on a 1–10 scale collected via post-session survey. A game-industry-specific satisfaction metric distinct from CSAT, capturing the core entertainment value proposition.
attributes.references: IGDA Playtesting Best Practices; GameAnalytics Player Experience Metrics

attributes.name: jira_epic_key
attributes.description: Jira Epic identifier linking this playtesting session to the overarching QA epic or release milestone in the project management system (e.g., 'QA-1042'). Enables traceability between playtesting activity and sprint/release planning.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Epic Key Convention

attributes.name: key_findings_summary
attributes.description: Structured narrative summary of the most significant findings, observations, and insights from the playtesting session. Authored by the facilitator and reviewed by the QA lead. This is the primary qualitative output of the session record.
attributes.references: IGDA QA Standards; Internal QA Report Template

attributes.name: location_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the playtesting session was conducted on-site at a studio facility, fully remote (participants at home), hybrid, or at a third-party testing lab. Affects logistics, data collection methods, and NDA compliance requirements.
attributes.references: IGDA QA Standards; GDPR Article 13 (Remote Data Collection)

attributes.name: minor_participants_present
attributes.description: Indicates whether any participants under the age of 18 (or 13 for COPPA) were present in the session. Triggers enhanced data protection protocols, parental consent requirements, and COPPA compliance procedures.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) — FTC Enforcement; GDPR Article 8 (Child Consent); PEGI Age Rating Standards

attributes.name: nda_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether participants in this session were required to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) prior to participation. Relevant for pre-release builds and external/focus group sessions where IP protection is required.
attributes.references: IP (Intellectual Property) Protection Standards; GDPR Article 13 (Participant Information)

attributes.name: nps_score
attributes.description: Net Promoter Score (NPS) collected from session participants via post-session survey, ranging from -100 to 100. Measures participant likelihood to recommend the game. A key player satisfaction KPI tracked from playtesting through live operations.
attributes.references: NPS (Net Promoter Score) Industry Standard; Bain & Company NPS Methodology

attributes.name: participant_count_actual
attributes.description: Number of participants who actually attended and completed the playtesting session. Compared against participant_count_planned to assess session execution quality and statistical validity of findings.
attributes.references: Internal QA Reporting Standards; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: participant_count_planned
attributes.description: Number of participants originally scheduled to attend the playtesting session. Used to measure session fill rate and plan QA resource capacity.

attributes.name: performance_evaluated
attributes.description: Indicates whether performance metrics (FPS, load times, memory usage) were formally measured and evaluated during this playtesting session. Distinguishes performance-focused sessions from pure gameplay/usability sessions.
attributes.references: FPS (Frames Per Second) Performance Standard; TRC (Technical Requirements Checklist)

attributes.name: recommendations
attributes.description: Actionable recommendations generated from the session findings, intended for the development team. Includes suggested design changes, bug fix priorities, and areas requiring follow-up testing. Feeds into Jira backlog grooming.
attributes.references: Jira Backlog Management; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: release_readiness_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator set by the QA facilitator or lead indicating whether the build tested in this session meets the quality gate criteria for progression to the next release milestone (e.g., Alpha to Beta, RC to Gold Master). A critical input to the release quality gate process.
attributes.references: Gold Master Release Quality Gate Standard; TRC (Technical Requirements Checklist); TCR (Technical Certification Requirements)

attributes.name: scheduled_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the playtesting session is planned to occur. Used for QA scheduling, resource allocation, and milestone tracking against the game development roadmap.

attributes.name: session_code
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known business identifier for the playtesting session (e.g., PLT-2024-000123). Used in Jira tickets, QA reports, and cross-team communications to reference a specific session without exposing the surrogate key.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Issue Key Convention

attributes.name: session_objectives
attributes.description: Structured description of the primary goals and test objectives for this playtesting session (e.g., evaluate FTUE flow, test PvP balance, assess accessibility features, validate performance on target hardware). Sourced from the Jira epic or QA test plan.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Epic Description; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: session_recording_url
attributes.description: Secure URL to the recorded video or screen capture of the playtesting session stored in the digital asset management system. Confidential as it may contain unreleased game footage and participant interactions. Access controlled per IP protection policy.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core — Digital Asset Management; IP (Intellectual Property) Protection; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: session_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the playtesting session, tracking its workflow from scheduling through completion or cancellation. Drives QA pipeline reporting and release readiness dashboards.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Issue Status Workflow

attributes.name: session_type
attributes.description: Classification of the playtesting session by methodology and participant profile. Internal sessions use studio staff; external sessions use recruited players; focus groups target specific demographics; blind tests exclude prior game knowledge; accessibility sessions evaluate inclusive design; UAT (User Acceptance Testing) validates release criteria; regression sessions verify bug fixes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: internal|external|focus_group|blind_test|accessibility|uat|regression — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IGDA Quality Assurance Standards; UAT (User Acceptance Testing) Industry Practice

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the playtesting session actually began. The principal real-world business event timestamp for this transaction. Used to calculate actual session duration and compare against scheduled time.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this playtesting session record was most recently modified. Supports incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: usability_issues_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct usability issues identified during the session, separate from technical bugs. Usability issues relate to UI/UX clarity, control intuitiveness, and player comprehension failures that impact player experience without being code defects.
attributes.references: IGDA QA Standards; FTUE (First-Time User Experience) Evaluation Framework

products.name: playtest_feedback
products.description: Transactional record capturing individual feedback items collected during a playtesting session. Records participant identifier (anonymized), feedback category (gameplay, UI/UX, FTUE, difficulty, performance, audio, visual, narrative), verbatim feedback text, sentiment classification, severity rating, associated game component or level, and whether the feedback was actioned. Enables granular analysis of player experience issues pre-launch.

attributes.name: playtest_feedback_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual playtest feedback record captured during a playtesting session. Primary key for this entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.asset. Business justification: Playtesters report issues with specific assets (broken texture on character model, missing audio cue, low-res icon). Direct asset feedback loop for content quality improvement.

attributes.name: battle_pass_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to monetization.battle_pass. Business justification: Playtest feedback on battle pass UX (progression pacing, reward satisfaction, tier skip pricing, premium value perception) must reference the specific pass instance being evaluated for design iteratio

attributes.name: build_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific game build version under test at the time of feedback collection. Critical for correlating feedback to a specific code and asset state in version control (Perforce Helix Core).
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control Standard

attributes.name: compliance_incident_id

attributes.description: Reference to the game title under test when this feedback was collected. Enables cross-title quality benchmarking and release readiness tracking.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to monetization.iap_transaction. attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.level_map. Business justification: Playtesters report level-specific issues (stuck spots, confusing layout, performance drops, unclear objectives, visual glitches). Direct level feedback loop for environment quality improvement and pla

attributes.name: licensed_ip_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to licensing.licensed_ip. Business justification: Playtest feedback on licensed characters, brands, or middleware features is tracked per IP asset for licensor reporting, brand compliance validation, and quality assurance. Real business need for bran

attributes.name: localization_string_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.localization_string. Business justification: Playtesters report translation errors, cultural inappropriateness, text overflow in UI, or confusing phrasing. Direct string feedback loop for localization quality improvement and cultural adaptation.

attributes.name: ml_model_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.ml_model_registry. Business justification: ML models analyze sentiment or predict feedback impact; linking enables model validation against actual feedback and automated feedback prioritization for QA action.

attributes.name: npc_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.npc_definition. Business justification: Playtesters report NPC issues (broken AI, missing dialogue, incorrect loot, unbalanced combat, poor pathfinding). Direct NPC feedback loop for AI tuning and gameplay balance improvement.

attributes.description: Anonymized identifier for the playtesting participant who submitted this feedback item. Anonymized to comply with GDPR and COPPA requirements; no direct PII is stored at this level.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.player_behavior_segment. Business justification: Playtest feedback from different behavioral segments has different business weight; segment context enables prioritized action on feedback from high-value or at-risk segments.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.playtest_session. Business justification: Playtest feedback is collected during playtest sessions. playtest_feedback currently has session_id pointing to player.session (wrong domain). This feedback is specifically from quality.playtest_sessi

attributes.name: seasonal_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.seasonal_event. Business justification: Playtesters report event issues (broken mechanics, unclear rules, reward bugs, poor balance, confusing UI). Direct event feedback loop for live ops quality improvement and player engagement optimizati

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: Reference to the playtesting session during which this feedback item was collected. Links feedback to its parent session context including date, build, and test plan.

attributes.name: telemetry_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.telemetry_event. Business justification: Playtest feedback references specific gameplay moments captured in telemetry; analysts link feedback to telemetry to validate player claims and measure impact of reported issues.

attributes.name: accessibility_concern
attributes.description: Indicates whether this feedback item identifies an accessibility issue (e.g., colorblind mode, subtitle readability, motor accessibility). Supports compliance with accessibility standards and inclusive design commitments.
attributes.references: IGDA Accessibility Special Interest Group Standards; Internal Accessibility Policy

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: The disposition or resolution action taken on this feedback item by the QA or development team. Captures the outcome of the triage process and aligns with Jira resolution types used in bug tracking workflows.
attributes.references: Jira Resolution Type Standard; Internal QA Triage Policy

attributes.name: actioned_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this feedback item was first actioned (triaged, assigned, or converted to a Jira issue) by the QA team. Used to measure triage cycle time and QA team responsiveness.
attributes.references: Internal QA SLA and Triage Cycle Time Standard

attributes.name: content_rating_concern
attributes.description: Indicates whether this feedback item raises a concern related to game content rating compliance (e.g., unexpected mature content, violence level, language). Flags items for review by the compliance team against ESRB, PEGI, USK, CERO, and GRAC rating standards.
attributes.references: ESRB Rating Standards; PEGI Rating Standards; USK Rating Standards; CERO Rating Standards; GRAC Rating Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this playtest feedback record was first created in the data platform. Audit trail timestamp for data lineage and GDPR data subject request processing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (accountability); ISO/IEC 27001 Audit Trail Requirements; SOC 2 Type II

attributes.name: device_model
attributes.description: The specific hardware device model used during the playtesting session (e.g., PlayStation 5 Standard, iPhone 15 Pro, NVIDIA RTX 4090 PC). Enables hardware-specific performance and compatibility analysis.
attributes.references: Internal QA Device Matrix; Platform Certification Requirements

attributes.name: feedback_category
attributes.description: Primary classification of the feedback item by game experience domain. Drives routing to the appropriate development team and enables category-level quality trend analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gameplay|ui_ux|ftue|difficulty|performance|audio|visual|narrative|controls|accessibility — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Internal QA Taxonomy; IGDA Quality Standards

attributes.name: feedback_reference_code
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally referenceable business identifier for this feedback item (e.g., PF-20240101). Used in QA reports, stakeholder communications, and cross-system traceability. Distinct from the surrogate PK.

attributes.name: feedback_source_type
attributes.description: The method or channel through which the feedback was collected during the playtesting session (e.g., written form, verbal debrief, in-game feedback tool, structured survey, facilitator observation).

attributes.name: feedback_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of this feedback item within the QA workflow, from initial capture through triage, actioning, resolution, and closure. Drives QA team workqueue management and release readiness reporting.
attributes.references: Internal QA Workflow State Machine; Jira Issue Status Standard

attributes.name: feedback_subcategory
attributes.description: Secondary classification providing finer granularity within the feedback category (e.g., within 'gameplay': combat_mechanics, progression_system, economy_balance). Enables detailed root-cause analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: varies by category — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: feedback_text
attributes.description: The raw, verbatim feedback text as provided by the playtesting participant. Captures unstructured qualitative input for NLP analysis, sentiment classification, and QA team review. Classified confidential as it may contain unreleased game content details.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (data minimisation); Internal QA Data Handling Policy

attributes.name: feedback_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone) when this feedback item was recorded during the playtesting session. The principal business event timestamp for this transaction record.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Date/Time Standard; Internal QA Session Logging Standard

attributes.name: fps_at_event
attributes.description: The measured Frames Per Second (FPS) recorded on the test device at the moment the feedback event occurred. Key performance metric for identifying frame rate drops correlated with player experience complaints.
attributes.references: Internal Performance Benchmarking Standard; Platform TRC/TCR Performance Requirements

attributes.name: game_component
attributes.description: The specific game system, feature, or module associated with this feedback item (e.g., inventory_system, matchmaking, character_controller, hud, tutorial_flow). Maps to development team ownership for routing and accountability.
attributes.references: Internal Game Architecture Component Registry; Jira Component Taxonomy

attributes.name: is_actioned
attributes.description: Indicates whether this feedback item has been reviewed and actioned by the development or QA team (e.g., converted to a Jira ticket, acknowledged, or formally deferred). Core operational flag for feedback triage workflow management.

attributes.name: is_ftue_related
attributes.description: Indicates whether this feedback item is specifically related to the First-Time User Experience (FTUE) flow. FTUE feedback is prioritized for pre-launch analysis as it directly impacts Day 1 (D1) retention metrics.
attributes.references: Internal FTUE Quality Gate Policy; D1 Retention KPI Framework

attributes.name: is_release_blocker
attributes.description: Indicates whether this feedback item has been classified as a release blocker that must be resolved before the game can pass the release quality gate. Directly feeds into the release readiness dashboard.
attributes.references: Internal Release Quality Gate Policy; Platform TRC/TCR Certification Requirements

attributes.name: jira_issue_key
attributes.description: The Jira issue key (e.g., QA-1234) linked to this feedback item when it has been converted into a tracked defect, task, or story in the Jira project management system. Null if not yet actioned into Jira.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management Standard; Internal QA Bug Tracking Process

attributes.name: level_or_area
attributes.description: The specific game level, map, zone, or area within the game where the feedback event occurred (e.g., level_01_tutorial, zone_darkwood_forest, hub_main_menu). Enables spatial analysis of player experience issues.
attributes.references: Internal Level Design Registry; Unity/Unreal Engine Asset Pipeline

attributes.name: milestone_target
attributes.description: The release milestone by which this feedback item must be resolved (e.g., Alpha, Beta, Gold Master, Day-One Patch). Directly supports release quality gate management and Gold Master readiness tracking.
attributes.references: Internal Release Milestone Framework; Gold Master Release Policy

attributes.name: os_version
attributes.description: The operating system version running on the test device at the time of feedback collection (e.g., Windows 11 23H2, iOS 17.2, Android 14). Used for OS-level compatibility and regression analysis.
attributes.references: Internal QA Device Matrix; Platform Certification Requirements

attributes.name: participant_skill_level
attributes.description: Self-reported or assessed skill level of the playtesting participant. Enables difficulty calibration analysis by correlating feedback sentiment and severity with player skill level, particularly for difficulty tuning.

attributes.name: platform
attributes.description: The gaming platform on which the playtesting session was conducted when this feedback was collected. Critical for platform-specific QA analysis and Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) / Technical Certification Requirements (TCR) compliance tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pc|ps5|xbox_series|nintendo_switch|ios|android|vr — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs Certification Standard; TRC/TCR Platform Requirements

attributes.name: priority_rating
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to this feedback item by the QA lead or product owner, indicating urgency of resolution relative to the release schedule. Distinct from severity: a cosmetic bug may be low severity but high priority near launch.
attributes.references: Jira Priority Standard; Internal Release Management Policy

attributes.name: qa_analyst_notes
attributes.description: Internal notes added by the QA analyst during triage or review of this feedback item. May include reproduction steps, environmental context, or cross-reference to related defects. Confidential internal working notes.

attributes.name: reproducibility
attributes.description: Assessment of how consistently the issue or experience described in the feedback can be reproduced by the QA team. Critical for defect prioritization: always-reproducible issues are prioritized for immediate investigation.
attributes.references: Internal QA Defect Management Standard; IGDA QA Best Practices

attributes.name: resolved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the issue raised by this feedback item was confirmed as resolved by the QA team. Used to calculate resolution cycle time and track quality improvement velocity across sprints.
attributes.references: Internal QA Resolution Tracking Standard; Jira Resolution Workflow

attributes.name: sentiment
attributes.description: Sentiment classification of the feedback item as determined by QA analyst review or automated NLP processing. Indicates the emotional tone of the participant's response to the game experience.
attributes.references: Internal QA Sentiment Analysis Framework; GameAnalytics/Amplitude Analytics Standard

attributes.name: sentiment_confidence_score
attributes.description: Confidence score (0.0000 to 1.0000) associated with the automated sentiment classification, indicating the reliability of the NLP model's prediction. Used to flag low-confidence classifications for manual QA analyst review.

attributes.name: session_elapsed_minutes
attributes.description: The elapsed time in minutes from the start of the playtesting session to the moment this feedback item was recorded. Enables temporal analysis of when in a session players encounter issues, particularly for First-Time User Experience (FTUE) analysis.
attributes.references: Internal QA Session Tracking Standard; FTUE Analysis Framework

attributes.name: severity_rating
attributes.description: Severity classification of the feedback item indicating the impact on player experience and release readiness. Critical and major items are escalated as release blockers. Aligned with Jira severity taxonomy used in QA bug tracking.

attributes.name: sprint_target
attributes.description: The Jira sprint identifier in which the resolution of this feedback item is planned (e.g., Sprint_42). Enables sprint-level quality planning and velocity tracking for QA-driven development work.
attributes.references: Jira Sprint Management Standard; Internal Agile Development Process

attributes.name: suggested_fix
attributes.description: Optional free-text field capturing the participant's or QA analyst's suggested resolution or improvement for the identified issue. Provides actionable input to the development team during sprint planning.
attributes.references: Internal QA Feedback Capture Standard; Jira Sprint Planning Process

attributes.name: target_audience_segment
attributes.description: The player audience segment that the playtesting participant represents. Enables segmented analysis of feedback to understand how different player demographics experience the game, informing targeted design decisions.
attributes.references: Internal Player Segmentation Framework; Marketing Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: test_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of playtesting activity during which this feedback was collected. Distinguishes internal QA, external beta, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), focus groups, alpha testing, and platform certification testing.
