attributes.description: Free-text field for supplementary context, workaround descriptions, platform holder correspondence summaries, or internal release committee commentary that does not fit structured fields. Supports QA team collaboration and audit documentation.

attributes.name: performance_metric_threshold
attributes.description: The minimum or maximum required threshold value for the performance metric as defined by the platform certification standard or internal quality gate (e.g., minimum 30 FPS, maximum 5 seconds load time). Null for non-performance findings.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Standards; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs

attributes.name: performance_metric_type
attributes.description: For performance-related findings, identifies the specific performance metric that failed the certification or quality gate threshold (e.g., FPS below minimum, load time exceeding limit, crash rate above threshold). 'none' for non-performance findings.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Standards; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Unity/Unreal Engine

attributes.name: performance_metric_value
attributes.description: The observed numeric value of the performance metric at the time the finding was identified (e.g., 24.3 FPS, 8.7 seconds load time, 0.023 crash rate). Null for non-performance findings. Paired with performance_metric_type for full context.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Standards; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Unity/Unreal Engine

attributes.name: platform
attributes.description: The distribution platform or console hardware for which this certification finding applies. Determines which first-party Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) or Technical Certification Requirements (TCR) standard governs the finding. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PlayStation|Xbox|Nintendo_Switch|PC_Steam|PC_Epic|iOS|Android|PC_GOG|PC_Microsoft — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: platform_reviewer_ref
attributes.description: The first-party platform holder's internal case or reviewer reference number associated with this finding (e.g., Sony Lotcheck case ID, Microsoft CERT ticket number). Enables direct correspondence tracking with platform certification teams.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: post_launch_monitoring
attributes.description: Formal description of the post-launch monitoring plan committed to as a condition of waiver approval, specifying metrics to be tracked (e.g., crash rate thresholds, player complaint volume, telemetry alerts) and the monitoring duration. Required for all approved waivers.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; IGDA Quality Standards; GameAnalytics/Amplitude

attributes.name: privacy_impact
attributes.description: Indicates whether this finding has potential impact on player data privacy compliance (GDPR, COPPA). True = finding may expose a privacy risk; False = no privacy impact. Triggers mandatory escalation to the Data Protection Officer when True.
attributes.references: GDPR Supervisory Authorities; COPPA Enforcement (FTC); FTC; European Commission (Digital Services Act)

attributes.name: reproduction_rate
attributes.description: Qualitative frequency with which the finding can be reproduced following the documented reproduction steps: always (100%), frequent (>50%), intermittent (10-50%), rare (<10%), unable_to_reproduce. Informs severity assessment and fix prioritization.
attributes.references: Jira; IGDA Quality Standards; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: reproduction_steps
attributes.description: Step-by-step instructions required to reliably reproduce the finding on the specified platform and build version. Critical for engineering triage, fix verification, and regression testing. Sourced from Jira defect records.

attributes.name: requirement_code
attributes.description: The specific platform certification requirement identifier (e.g., TRC R4000, TCR CERT-0123, App Store Guideline 4.2) that this finding violates. Provides direct traceability to the governing platform standard or internal quality gate rule.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: requirement_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the platform certification requirement or internal quality gate rule that was violated, as defined by the governing platform holder or internal QA standard. Provides context for engineers and release managers without requiring lookup of external documentation.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Standards; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs

attributes.name: resolution_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the finding's resolution workflow: open (newly identified), in_progress (fix underway), resolved (fix verified), waived (risk formally accepted), closed (cleared by platform or gate), deferred (pushed to future release). SSOT for release readiness dashboards.
attributes.references: Jira; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; SOC 2

attributes.name: resolved_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the finding was formally resolved, verified as fixed, or cleared by the platform holder. Null for open or in-progress findings. Used to calculate time-to-resolution KPIs and release gate compliance.
attributes.references: Jira; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; IGDA

attributes.name: risk_assessment
attributes.description: Formal risk level assigned to this finding as part of the waiver governance process, reflecting the potential player impact, regulatory exposure, or commercial risk if the finding ships unresolved: low, medium, high, critical. Informs waiver approval authority level.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; ESRB; PEGI; GDPR Supervisory Authorities; FTC

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the finding per platform certification and internal QA standards: critical (submission blocker, must fix before release), major (significant functional defect), minor (low-impact issue), advisory (informational, no fix required). Drives prioritization and release gate decisions.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Standards; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; IGDA Quality Standards

attributes.name: submission_round
attributes.description: The sequential certification submission attempt number (1, 2, 3…) during which this finding was raised. Tracks how many resubmission cycles a title has undergone, a key KPI for release efficiency and QA process maturity.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: target_release_date
attributes.description: The planned commercial release or patch launch date for the game title at the time this finding was logged. Provides business urgency context for prioritization — findings raised close to the target release date carry higher commercial risk.
attributes.references: Jira; Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; SAP S/4HANA

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The UTC timestamp when this certification finding record was most recently modified in the data platform. Supports incremental data pipeline processing, audit trails, and change detection for downstream analytics.

attributes.name: waiver_approved_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the waiver approver formally granted approval for the risk-acceptance waiver. Null when waiver is pending, denied, or not applicable.

attributes.name: waiver_expiry_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the approved waiver expires, after which the finding must be re-evaluated, fixed, or a new waiver requested. Enforces time-bounded risk acceptance and prevents indefinite deferral of quality issues.

attributes.name: waiver_justification
attributes.description: Formal written justification provided by the resolution owner explaining why the finding cannot be fixed prior to release and why the associated risk is acceptable. Required field for all waiver requests; subject to audit by release governance committees.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; IGDA Quality Standards; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: waiver_requested_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which a formal risk-acceptance waiver was requested for this finding, initiating the waiver governance workflow. Null when no waiver has been requested.

attributes.name: waiver_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the waiver governance process for this finding: not_requested, pending (submitted, awaiting approval), approved, denied, expired (approval period lapsed), withdrawn (requester cancelled). SSOT for waiver compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; IGDA Quality Standards; TRC/TCR Standards

products.name: release_gate
products.description: Master record for each formal release quality gate checkpoint in the game release pipeline (Alpha, Beta, Gold Master, Patch Release gates). Captures gate name, type, associated game title/build, target and actual review dates, gate owner, and full review event audit trail including review participants, criteria evaluated with pass/fail outcomes, blocking defect count by severity, defect waiver decisions, escalation items, final disposition (approve, reject, conditional approve), approver identities, and sign-off status. Supports multiple review iterations per gate. SSOT for release readiness decisions, their review evidence, and stakeholder approvals.
products.reference: Release Quality Gate / Gold Master Gate

attributes.name: release_gate_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each formal release quality gate checkpoint record in the game release pipeline.

attributes.name: approver_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee who formally approved or rejected this release gate, serving as the accountable sign-off authority.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; SOC 2

attributes.name: audit_engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_engagement. Business justification: Release gates are audited during regulatory/platform audits. Real business process: audit scope definition and release readiness verification.

attributes.name: build_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific game build version under review at this gate, sourced from Perforce Helix Core or the build pipeline.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Release gate approval determines go-live date, triggering capitalization-to-amortization transition. Finance depends on gate sign-off to start amortizing capitalized development costs and close asset-

attributes.name: content_release_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.content_release. Business justification: Release gates approve/reject specific content drops for production deployment. Gate-to-release linkage enables go/no-go decision tracking and release readiness reporting.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title associated with this release gate checkpoint.

attributes.name: kpi_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.kpi_definition. Business justification: Release gates include KPI thresholds (crash rate, performance benchmarks); linking formalizes which KPIs gate releases and enables automated gate evaluation against KPI targets.

attributes.name: platform_sku_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.platform_sku. Business justification: Release gates approve specific SKUs for launch; each edition/region has separate approval workflows and content validation requirements.

attributes.name: primary_release_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or team lead who owns and is accountable for this release gate checkpoint and its outcome.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; SAP S/4HANA HR

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Release gates enforce regulatory compliance checkpoints (GDPR, COPPA, age rating, platform TRCs). Real business process: go/no-go decision based on regulatory readiness.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the target platform (e.g., PlayStation, Xbox, PC, iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch) for which this release gate applies.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Platform Certification

attributes.name: actual_fps
attributes.description: The measured Frames Per Second (FPS) achieved by the build under review during performance testing, compared against target_fps to determine benchmark compliance.

attributes.name: actual_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the release gate review was actually conducted. Compared against target_review_date to measure schedule adherence.

attributes.name: blocking_defect_critical_count
attributes.description: Count of open Critical severity defects that are blocking release at the time of this gate review. Critical defects are showstoppers that prevent the game from functioning.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal QA Defect Severity Classification

attributes.name: blocking_defect_major_count
attributes.description: Count of open Major severity defects that are blocking release at the time of this gate review. Major defects significantly impair gameplay or platform compliance.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal QA Defect Severity Classification

attributes.name: blocking_defect_minor_count
attributes.description: Count of open Minor severity defects flagged as blocking at the time of this gate review.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal QA Defect Severity Classification

attributes.name: condition_resolution_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which all conditional approval conditions must be resolved and verified. Applicable only when gate disposition is Conditional Approve.

attributes.name: conditional_approval_conditions
attributes.description: Textual description of the mandatory conditions that must be fulfilled when the gate disposition is Conditional Approve. Null when disposition is not conditional.

attributes.name: coppa_compliance_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Compliance Verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether COPPA compliance requirements for children's privacy protection have been verified for this build at this gate. Required for titles accessible to players under 13 in the US.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this release gate record was first created in the system, providing the audit creation trail.

attributes.name: criteria_evaluated_count
attributes.description: Total number of release readiness criteria evaluated during this gate review, providing a completeness measure for the review process.

attributes.name: criteria_failed_count
attributes.description: Number of release readiness criteria that received a failing outcome during this gate review, directly informing the gate disposition decision.

attributes.name: criteria_passed_count
attributes.description: Number of release readiness criteria that received a passing outcome during this gate review.

attributes.name: disposition
attributes.description: The formal final decision outcome of the release gate review: Approve (release cleared), Reject (release blocked), Conditional Approve (release cleared with mandatory follow-up actions), Defer (gate postponed to a later iteration), Escalate (decision elevated to senior leadership).

attributes.name: disposition_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the final gate disposition decision was recorded, providing an authoritative audit timestamp for the release readiness decision.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: escalation_item_count
attributes.description: Number of items escalated to senior leadership or executive stakeholders during this gate review for decision-making beyond the gate owner's authority.

attributes.name: escalation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text description of escalation items raised during the gate review, capturing the nature of the escalation and any decisions made by senior stakeholders.

attributes.name: esrb_rating_confirmed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) Rating Confirmed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ESRB content rating has been confirmed and is consistent with the build under review at this gate. Required for North American distribution.

attributes.name: gate_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the release quality gate checkpoint (e.g., 'Alpha Gate', 'Beta Gate', 'Gold Master Gate', 'Day-1 Patch Gate').

attributes.name: gate_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing additional context, observations, or commentary from the gate review session not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: gate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the release gate review. Scheduled: gate is planned but not yet started. In Review: active review in progress. Approved: gate passed and release is cleared. Rejected: gate failed and release is blocked. Conditional Approved: gate passed with conditions that must be resolved. Cancelled: gate was voided.

attributes.name: gate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the release gate stage in the game release pipeline. Alpha indicates early feature-complete review; Beta indicates pre-launch stability review; Gold Master (GM) indicates final ship-ready certification; Patch Release and Hotfix indicate post-launch update gates; RC indicates Release Candidate. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: alpha|beta|gold_master|patch_release|hotfix|rc|uat|certification — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; Steamworks/Console SDK Certification

attributes.name: gdpr_compliance_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Compliance Verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether GDPR compliance requirements (data privacy, consent mechanisms, data subject rights) have been verified for this build at this gate. Required for EU distribution.
attributes.references: GDPR Supervisory Authorities; GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design)

attributes.name: jira_project_key
attributes.description: The Jira project key associated with this release gate, enabling traceability to the Jira release planning board and sprint backlog.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: next_review_target_date
attributes.description: The planned date for the next review iteration of this gate, applicable when the current disposition is Reject or Conditional Approve and a re-review is required.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: pci_dss_compliance_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) Compliance Verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether PCI DSS compliance for in-game payment processing and In-App Purchase (IAP) flows has been verified at this gate. Required for titles with real-money transactions.
attributes.references: PCI SSC (Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council); PCI DSS

attributes.name: pegi_rating_confirmed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pan European Game Information (PEGI) Rating Confirmed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the PEGI content rating has been confirmed and is consistent with the build under review at this gate. Required for European distribution.

attributes.name: performance_benchmark_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the build met all defined performance benchmarks (e.g., target Frames Per Second (FPS), load times, memory usage) at the time of this gate review.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Textual explanation of why the release gate was rejected. Populated only when gate disposition is Reject. Provides the formal rationale for blocking the release.

attributes.name: review_iteration_number
attributes.description: Sequential iteration count for this gate review, supporting multiple review cycles per gate (e.g., iteration 1 = initial review, iteration 2 = re-review after defect remediation).

attributes.name: review_participants
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of employee identifiers or names of stakeholders who participated in the gate review session, forming part of the review event audit trail.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; SOC 2

attributes.name: sign_off_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the required stakeholder sign-off for this gate has been completed. Pending: awaiting sign-off. Signed Off: all required approvals obtained. Waived: sign-off formally waived with justification. Not Required: gate type does not require formal sign-off.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; SOC 2

attributes.name: stability_crash_rate
attributes.description: The measured crash rate (crashes per session or per hour of play) for the build under review, used as a key stability benchmark for release readiness decisions.
attributes.references: Internal QA Stability Benchmark Standard; GameAnalytics/Amplitude

attributes.name: target_fps
attributes.description: The target Frames Per Second (FPS) performance threshold defined for this release gate, against which the actual build performance is evaluated.

attributes.name: target_review_date
attributes.description: The planned date on which the release gate review is scheduled to occur, used for release milestone tracking and project planning.
attributes.references: Jira Release Planning; Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard

attributes.name: trc_compliance_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the build has passed the platform manufacturer's Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) or Technical Certification Requirements (TCR) at the time of this gate. Compliant: all TRC/TCR items passed. Non-Compliant: one or more TRC/TCR items failed. Waived: non-compliance formally accepted. Not Applicable: TRC/TCR not required for this gate type.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Platform Certification; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this release gate record was last modified, supporting audit trail and change tracking requirements.

attributes.name: waived_defect_count
attributes.description: Number of defects that were formally waived (accepted risk) during this gate review, allowing the gate to proceed despite known issues.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Pipeline Standard; Jira Bug Tracking

products.name: release_gate_review
products.description: Transactional record capturing each formal review event conducted at a release gate checkpoint. Records review date, participants, gate criteria evaluated, criteria pass/fail outcomes, defect waiver decisions, escalation items, final recommendation (approve, reject, conditional approve), and sign-off status. Provides the audit trail for release gate decisions and stakeholder approvals.

attributes.name: release_gate_review_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each formal release gate review event. Primary key for this transactional record. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — captures a discrete quality gate decision event with its own lifecycle.

attributes.name: audit_engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_engagement. Business justification: Release gate reviews are subject to audit during regulatory engagements. Real business process: audit evidence collection and release readiness verification.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the QA lead or release manager who chaired and is accountable for this release gate review session. Serves as the primary party reference for this transaction.
attributes.references: Internal QA Governance; IGDA Quality Standards

attributes.name: game_studio_id
attributes.description: Reference to the development studio whose game build is under review at this release gate. Enables studio-level quality metrics aggregation and release readiness benchmarking.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title under review at this release gate. Links the review event to the specific game product being evaluated for release readiness.

attributes.name: milestone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to studio.milestone. Business justification: Release gate reviews are milestone-specific (alpha gate, beta gate, gold master); each milestone has defined gate criteria. Milestone progression requires gate review approval. Creating milestone_id F

attributes.name: release_gate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.release_gate. Business justification: Release gate reviews are conducted at release gates. release_gate_review has gate_type (STRING) but no FK to release_gate. Reviews are events that evaluate gates. Cardinality: N release_gate_reviews :

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the target distribution platform (e.g., PlayStation, Xbox, PC/Steam, iOS, Android) for which this release gate review is being conducted. Platform-specific certification requirements (TRC/TCR) vary by platform.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; ESRB; PEGI

attributes.name: actual_fps
attributes.description: The measured average Frames Per Second (FPS) achieved by the build during QA performance testing, recorded at the time of this gate review. Compared against target_fps to determine performance gate pass/fail.
attributes.references: Internal QA Performance Benchmark Standards; Unity/Unreal Engine Profiling

attributes.name: assigned_rating
attributes.description: The content rating assigned by the applicable rating body (e.g., ESRB: E, T, M, AO; PEGI: 3, 7, 12, 16, 18). Null if rating has not yet been assigned. Critical gate criterion for commercial release compliance.

attributes.name: build_version
attributes.description: The specific game build version string (e.g., 1.4.2.8831) submitted for this release gate review. Corresponds to the Perforce Helix Core changelist label or Unity/Unreal Engine build artifact version.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; Semantic Versioning 2.0.0

attributes.name: conditional_approval_conditions
attributes.description: Free-text description of the specific conditions that must be satisfied for a conditional_approve recommendation to convert to a full approval. Populated only when recommendation is conditional_approve. Conditions are tracked to closure before release.

attributes.name: content_rating_body
attributes.description: The regulatory body that issued or is processing the content rating for this release (e.g., ESRB, PEGI, USK, CERO, GRAC). Relevant to the target market(s) for this release. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ESRB|PEGI|USK|CERO|GRAC|IARC — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: content_rating_status
attributes.description: Status of the game's content rating submission and approval with applicable rating bodies (ESRB, PEGI, USK, CERO, GRAC) at the time of this gate review. A valid content rating is typically a hard gate requirement for commercial release.
attributes.references: ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board); PEGI (Pan European Game Information); USK; CERO; GRAC

attributes.name: coppa_compliance_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) compliance requirements have been verified as part of this release gate review. Mandatory gate criterion for games accessible to players under 13 in the US market.
attributes.references: COPPA Enforcement (FTC); FTC Consumer Protection Standards

attributes.name: crash_rate_pct
attributes.description: The measured crash rate of the build as a percentage of sessions, recorded at the time of this gate review. A key stability benchmark used to assess release readiness. Typically sourced from QA playtesting telemetry or GameAnalytics/Amplitude crash reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this release gate review record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and record provenance tracking.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: criteria_failed_count
attributes.description: The number of release gate criteria items that received a failing outcome during this review. Non-zero values typically trigger rejection or conditional approval outcomes.

attributes.name: criteria_passed_count
attributes.description: The number of release gate criteria items that received a passing outcome during this review. Used alongside total_criteria_evaluated to compute pass rate for release readiness reporting.

attributes.name: criteria_waived_count
attributes.description: The number of release gate criteria items that were formally waived (bypassed with documented justification) during this review. Waivers require explicit stakeholder sign-off and are tracked for audit and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: defect_waiver_count
attributes.description: The total number of individual defect waivers formally approved during this gate review session. Each waiver represents a documented risk acceptance decision allowing a known defect to ship.
attributes.references: Internal QA Waiver Policy; IGDA Quality Standards

attributes.name: escalation_item_count
attributes.description: The number of issues or decisions escalated to senior leadership or cross-functional stakeholders during this gate review. Escalations indicate items that could not be resolved within the standard review authority.

attributes.name: escalation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text description of items escalated to senior leadership or cross-functional stakeholders during this gate review. Documents the nature of each escalation, the escalation target, and expected resolution timeline. Populated when escalation_item_count > 0.

attributes.name: gdpr_compliance_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) compliance requirements for player data handling have been verified as part of this release gate review. Mandatory gate criterion for releases targeting EU markets.
attributes.references: GDPR Supervisory Authorities; GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design); European Commission Digital Services Act

attributes.name: jira_release_ticket
attributes.description: The Jira issue key (e.g., REL-4821) for the release epic or release planning ticket associated with this gate review. Provides traceability back to the Jira project management system of record for release planning.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: The date scheduled for the follow-up gate review, applicable when the current review results in a rejection or conditional approval requiring re-evaluation. Used for release milestone planning.
attributes.references: Jira Release Planning; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: open_critical_defect_count
attributes.description: The number of open critical-severity (P0/P1) defects in Jira at the time of this gate review. Critical defects are typically blocking for release approval and must be resolved or waived before gate passage.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal QA Severity Classification

attributes.name: open_major_defect_count
attributes.description: The number of open major-severity (P2) defects in Jira at the time of this gate review. Major defects may be conditionally waived with documented risk acceptance.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal QA Severity Classification

attributes.name: open_minor_defect_count
attributes.description: The number of open minor-severity (P3/P4) defects in Jira at the time of this gate review. Minor defects are typically tracked but do not block gate passage.
attributes.references: Jira Bug Tracking; Internal QA Severity Classification

attributes.name: participant_count
attributes.description: The total number of stakeholders who participated in this release gate review session. Includes QA leads, producers, studio directors, platform compliance officers, and any other attendees.

attributes.name: pci_dss_compliance_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) compliance requirements for in-game payment processing (IAP/MTX) have been verified as part of this release gate review. Required for titles with in-app purchase (IAP) or microtransaction (MTX) monetization.
attributes.references: PCI SSC (Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council); PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: performance_benchmark_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the build met all defined performance benchmarks (e.g., target FPS (Frames Per Second), load times, memory usage, crash rate thresholds) as evaluated during this gate review. Performance benchmarks are a standard gate criterion for release quality.
attributes.references: Internal QA Performance Benchmark Standards; Platform Certification Requirements

attributes.name: platform_cert_readiness
attributes.description: Assessment of the build's readiness for submission to first-party platform certification (e.g., Sony TRC, Microsoft TCR, Nintendo Lot Check). Tracks whether the build meets all Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) / Technical Certification Requirements (TCR) criteria required by the platform holder.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; Sony TRC; Microsoft TCR; Nintendo Lot Check

attributes.name: recommendation
attributes.description: The formal recommendation issued by the review lead at the conclusion of this gate review session. Approve indicates the build is cleared to proceed; reject indicates the build must be remediated and re-reviewed; conditional_approve indicates approval is granted subject to documented conditions being met.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Management Process; IGDA Quality Standards

attributes.name: regression_suite_pass_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of automated regression test suite cases that passed for this build at the time of the gate review. Sourced from CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) pipeline test results. A key quality gate metric.
attributes.references: Internal QA Automation Standards; CI/CD Pipeline

attributes.name: release_target_date
attributes.description: The planned commercial release date for the game title at the time of this gate review. Used to assess schedule risk and urgency of gate decisions. May differ from the actual release date if the gate results in a delay.
attributes.references: Internal Release Management; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: review_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this release gate review event, used in Jira, release management communications, and audit documentation (e.g., RGR-TITLE01-20240315). Aligns with Jira release planning ticket references.
attributes.references: Jira Release Planning; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The principal real-world timestamp when the formal release gate review session was conducted. This is the business event timestamp, distinct from record audit timestamps. Used for release timeline tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: review_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative notes captured during the gate review session, documenting key discussion points, risk observations, escalation context, and any decisions not captured in structured fields. Provides qualitative audit trail context.

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of this release gate review event. Approved indicates all gate criteria passed; rejected indicates blocking issues remain; conditional_approved indicates approval granted subject to specified conditions; deferred indicates the review has been postponed.

attributes.name: scheduled_review_date
attributes.description: The originally planned calendar date for this release gate review, as recorded in Jira release planning. Used to measure schedule adherence and release milestone tracking against planned dates.

attributes.name: sign_off_status
attributes.description: Current status of stakeholder sign-off collection for this gate review. Complete indicates all required approvers have signed off; partial indicates some approvers have signed but others are outstanding; pending indicates sign-off collection has not yet begun.

attributes.name: sign_off_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when all required stakeholder sign-offs were collected and the gate review was formally closed. Null if sign-off is not yet complete. Used for release timeline and audit trail.

attributes.name: target_fps
attributes.description: The target Frames Per Second (FPS) performance threshold defined for this release gate. Used as the benchmark against which actual build performance is measured during the review.
attributes.references: Internal QA Performance Benchmark Standards; Platform Certification Requirements

attributes.name: total_criteria_evaluated
attributes.description: The total count of release gate criteria items formally evaluated during this review session. Used to measure review scope and completeness of the gate assessment.

attributes.name: uat_completion_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of User Acceptance Testing (UAT) test cases that have been executed and closed at the time of this gate review. A key gate criterion indicating test coverage completeness before release.
attributes.references: Internal QA UAT Process; Jira Test Management

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this release gate review record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data freshness monitoring, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; Internal Data Governance Standard

products.name: perf_test_run
products.description: Transactional record for each performance test run executed against a game build. Captures run date, game title and build version, platform, test scenario (load test, stress test, soak test, FPS benchmark, latency test, CCU/PCU simulation), environment configuration, peak FPS, average FPS, frame time, CPU/GPU utilization, memory usage, network latency, CCU achieved, pass/fail against defined benchmarks, and regression flag vs. prior build. SSOT for game performance stability data.

attributes.name: perf_test_run_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each performance test run record. Primary key for the perf_test_run data product in the quality domain.

attributes.name: build_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to studio.build. Business justification: Performance test runs validate specific builds; studios track which build passed performance benchmarks for release gate decisions. Build certification requires perf test passage. Replaces denormalize

attributes.name: build_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.build_submission. Business justification: Performance tests validate cert submission builds against TRC benchmarks; results gate submission approval and identify performance regressions.

attributes.name: executed_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Performance test execution requires tracking which QA engineer ran the test for accountability, scheduling conflict resolution, and expertise matching. Critical for capacity planning and SLA complianc

attributes.name: game_mode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to title.game_mode. Business justification: Performance benchmarks (FPS, memory, latency) vary significantly by game mode (64-player vs 4-player). Mode-specific performance SLAs are required for certification and release gate approval. Critical

attributes.name: game_server_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.game_server. Business justification: Performance test runs execute on specific game servers. Benchmarking requires correlation with server hardware configuration, resource utilization (CPU, GPU, memory), and network conditions for accura

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the game title under test. Links this performance test run to the specific game IP being evaluated.
attributes.references: Internal Game Title Master Data Standard

attributes.name: kpi_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.kpi_definition. Business justification: Performance test runs measure specific KPIs (FPS, latency); linking enables tracking of KPI compliance over builds and automated performance regression detection.

attributes.name: level_map_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.level_map. Business justification: Performance tests measure FPS, memory usage, load times per level for benchmarking and optimization. Level-specific performance profiling enables targeted optimization and certification readiness vali

attributes.name: network_region_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.network_region. Business justification: Performance tests validate region-specific latency and throughput targets. Certification gate validation requires regional SLA compliance verification (max latency, target FPS) for platform-holder app

attributes.name: stability_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.stability_benchmark. Business justification: Performance test runs validate against stability benchmarks. perf_test_run has fps_benchmark_threshold and memory_budget_mb but no FK to stability_benchmark. Benchmarks define approved thresholds. Car

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the target platform on which the performance test was executed (e.g., PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, PC, iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch). Aligns with Steamworks/Console SDK platform taxonomy.
attributes.references: Steamworks SDK; Console SDK Platform Taxonomy; Internal Platform Reference Data

attributes.name: tournament_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to esports.tournament. Business justification: Performance benchmarking for tournament builds (LAN server capacity, spectator mode stability, broadcast delay testing) must reference the tournament for infrastructure planning, capacity validation,

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Username or display name of the QA lead or release manager who approved this performance test run result for the release gate. Null when release_gate_approved is False or approval is pending.
attributes.references: Internal Release Gate Policy; SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the release gate approval was granted for this performance test run. Null when release_gate_approved is False or approval is pending. Used for release timeline tracking and audit compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Internal Release Gate Policy; SOC 2 Type II

attributes.name: avg_cpu_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Mean CPU utilization percentage recorded across all active cores during the test run. Used to assess CPU headroom, identify bottlenecks, and validate that the build does not exceed platform CPU budget thresholds.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Console SDK CPU Budget Requirements; Internal Performance Benchmark Standard

attributes.name: avg_fps
attributes.description: The mean Frames Per Second (FPS) recorded across the full duration of the test run. Primary rendering performance KPI used in release gate pass/fail evaluation and regression comparison.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Internal FPS Benchmark Standard; Console SDK Performance Requirements

attributes.name: avg_frame_time_ms
attributes.description: The mean time in milliseconds to render a single frame during the test run. Complements FPS metrics by providing a direct measure of rendering latency. Target thresholds vary by platform (e.g., 16.67ms for 60 FPS, 33.33ms for 30 FPS).
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Unity/Unreal Engine Profiler Standards; Console SDK Performance Requirements

attributes.name: avg_gpu_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Mean GPU utilization percentage recorded during the test run. Used to assess GPU headroom and rendering pipeline efficiency. High GPU utilization with low FPS indicates a GPU bottleneck.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Console SDK GPU Budget Requirements; Internal Performance Benchmark Standard

attributes.name: avg_memory_usage_mb
attributes.description: Mean RAM consumption in megabytes across the full duration of the test run. Used alongside peak memory to assess memory stability and detect memory leaks during soak tests.
attributes.references: Console SDK TRC/TCR Memory Requirements; Internal Memory Budget Policy

attributes.name: avg_network_latency_ms
attributes.description: Mean round-trip network latency in milliseconds measured during the test run. Relevant for online multiplayer (PvP, MMO, GaaS) titles. High latency degrades player experience and is a key quality gate metric for live service games.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Internal Network Performance Standard; GaaS Quality Gate Policy

attributes.name: ccu_achieved
attributes.description: The actual number of Concurrent Users (CCU) successfully simulated or observed during the test run. For CCU/PCU simulation scenarios, this represents the peak concurrent load achieved before performance degradation or failure. Key metric for GaaS live operations capacity planning.
attributes.references: Internal GaaS Capacity Planning Standard; ISO/IEC 25010

attributes.name: ccu_target
attributes.description: The target number of Concurrent Users (CCU) defined for this test run scenario. Compared against ccu_achieved to determine if the build meets the required concurrency capacity for release.
attributes.references: Internal GaaS Capacity Planning Standard; ISO/IEC 25010

attributes.name: cert_readiness_status
attributes.description: Assessment of whether this build's performance results meet platform certification requirements (TRC/TCR). 'not_assessed' = certification review not yet performed; 'ready' = performance meets all TRC/TCR thresholds; 'not_ready' = performance fails one or more TRC/TCR requirements; 'waiver_pending' = exception waiver submitted to platform holder.
attributes.references: Console SDK TRC/TCR Certification Requirements; Steamworks Certification Guidelines; ESRB/PEGI Platform Compliance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this performance test run record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Internal Data Governance Audit Standard; SOC 2 Type II

attributes.name: game_mode_tested
attributes.description: The specific game mode or scenario exercised during the performance test (e.g., 'PvP_Arena_64Player', 'PvE_OpenWorld', 'MainMenu', 'FTUE_Tutorial', 'MMO_Hub_Zone'). Enables performance comparison across game modes.
attributes.references: Internal Game Design Documentation; QA Test Case Specification

attributes.name: hardware_config_profile
attributes.description: Label or identifier of the hardware configuration profile used during the test run (e.g., 'PS5-Standard', 'PC-MinSpec', 'PC-RecommendedSpec', 'iOS-iPhone14'). Captures the device/hardware tier to contextualize performance results.
attributes.references: Console SDK Hardware Specification Standards; Internal QA Hardware Profile Registry

attributes.name: is_automated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this performance test run was executed by an automated CI/CD pipeline (True) or manually triggered by a QA engineer (False). Used to segment automated regression suites from manual exploratory performance tests in reporting.
attributes.references: Internal CI/CD Quality Assurance Standard; Jira Automation Policy

attributes.name: is_regression
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test run detected a performance regression compared to the prior build's baseline results. True = regression detected (performance degraded vs. prior build); False = no regression detected. Triggers mandatory investigation before release gate approval.
attributes.references: Internal QA Regression Policy; Jira Bug Tracking Standard

attributes.name: jira_issue_key
attributes.description: The Jira issue key (e.g., QA-4821) associated with this performance test run. Enables traceability from the test run back to the Jira sprint, epic, or release planning ticket that initiated the test.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management Standard; Internal QA Traceability Policy

attributes.name: min_fps
attributes.description: The lowest Frames Per Second (FPS) value recorded during the test run. Critical for identifying frame rate drops, stutters, and worst-case rendering performance that impact player experience.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Internal FPS Benchmark Standard; Console SDK Performance Requirements

attributes.name: overall_result
attributes.description: The overall pass/fail determination for this performance test run against all defined benchmarks. 'pass' = all benchmarks met; 'fail' = one or more benchmarks not met; 'conditional_pass' = passed with documented exceptions approved by QA lead; 'inconclusive' = run completed but results are insufficient for a determination.
attributes.references: Internal QA Release Gate Policy; Console SDK TRC/TCR Certification Standards

attributes.name: p99_frame_time_ms
attributes.description: The 99th percentile frame time in milliseconds, representing worst-case frame rendering latency excluding the top 1% of outliers. Used to detect hitching and micro-stutter patterns that degrade player experience even when average FPS appears acceptable.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Internal Performance Benchmark Standard; Unity/Unreal Engine Profiler Standards

attributes.name: peak_cpu_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Maximum CPU utilization percentage observed at any point during the test run. Identifies CPU spike events that may cause frame drops or game freezes under peak load conditions.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Console SDK CPU Budget Requirements; Internal Performance Benchmark Standard

attributes.name: peak_fps
attributes.description: The highest Frames Per Second (FPS) value recorded during the test run. Used to assess maximum rendering throughput and identify performance ceiling for the build on the target platform.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Internal FPS Benchmark Standard; Console SDK Performance Requirements

attributes.name: peak_gpu_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Maximum GPU utilization percentage observed at any point during the test run. Identifies GPU saturation events that may cause rendering bottlenecks or thermal throttling on target hardware.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Console SDK GPU Budget Requirements; Internal Performance Benchmark Standard

attributes.name: peak_memory_usage_mb
attributes.description: Maximum RAM consumption in megabytes observed during the test run. Critical for platform certification compliance — console and mobile platforms enforce strict memory budgets (e.g., TRC/TCR memory limits). Exceeding this threshold is a certification blocker.
attributes.references: Console SDK TRC/TCR Memory Requirements; ESRB/PEGI Platform Certification Standards; Internal Memory Budget Policy

attributes.name: peak_network_latency_ms
attributes.description: Maximum round-trip network latency in milliseconds observed during the test run. Identifies worst-case latency spikes that may cause rubber-banding, desync, or disconnection events in online multiplayer scenarios.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010; Internal Network Performance Standard; GaaS Quality Gate Policy

attributes.name: prior_build_version
attributes.description: The build version used as the regression baseline for comparison in this test run. Populated when is_regression evaluation is performed. Enables direct traceability to the specific prior build whose metrics were used as the performance baseline.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Labeling Standard; Internal QA Regression Policy

attributes.name: regression_delta_fps
attributes.description: The difference in average FPS between this build and the prior build baseline (current avg_fps minus prior avg_fps). Negative values indicate FPS regression. Null when no prior baseline exists or regression comparison was not performed.
attributes.references: Internal QA Regression Policy; Internal FPS Benchmark Standard

attributes.name: release_gate_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether this performance test run result has been reviewed and approved as part of the release quality gate process. True = approved by QA lead/release manager; False = not yet approved or approval denied. Required before build promotion to certification or production.
attributes.references: Internal Release Gate Policy; Jira Release Planning Standard

attributes.name: run_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for QA engineers to document observations, anomalies, environmental conditions, or context relevant to this test run (e.g., 'Server under maintenance during run', 'Thermal throttling observed on device'). Supports qualitative analysis alongside quantitative metrics.

attributes.name: run_reference_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code assigned to this performance test run (e.g., PTR-FTUE-20240315-0042). Used in Jira tickets, QA reports, and release gate documentation to reference a specific run.
attributes.references: Jira QA Project Naming Convention; Internal QA Process Standard

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the performance test run. 'queued' = scheduled but not started; 'in_progress' = actively executing; 'completed' = finished with results captured; 'aborted' = terminated before completion; 'failed' = run encountered a fatal error preventing result capture.

attributes.name: run_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the performance test run was initiated. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction record.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Date/Time Standard; Internal QA Audit Policy

attributes.name: test_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in seconds from test run start to completion or abort. Used to validate that soak tests ran for the required duration and to normalize performance metrics across runs of different lengths.

attributes.name: test_environment
attributes.description: The deployment environment in which the performance test was executed. 'dev' = development; 'qa' = QA lab; 'staging' = staging/integration; 'pre_prod' = pre-production; 'cert' = platform certification environment (e.g., Sony TRC, Microsoft TCR).
attributes.references: Steamworks/Console SDK Certification Environment Standards; Internal Environment Management Policy

attributes.name: test_scenario_type
attributes.description: Classification of the performance test scenario executed. 'load_test' = normal expected load; 'stress_test' = beyond normal capacity; 'soak_test' = sustained load over time; 'fps_benchmark' = Frames Per Second (FPS) measurement; 'latency_test' = network latency measurement; 'ccu_simulation' = Concurrent Users (CCU)/Peak Concurrent Users (PCU) simulation.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 25010 Software Quality Standard; Internal QA Test Taxonomy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this performance test run record was last modified. Tracks post-run updates such as result annotation, pass/fail override, or regression flag changes.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Internal Data Governance Audit Standard; SOC 2 Type II

products.name: stability_benchmark
products.description: Master record defining the approved stability and performance benchmarks for a game title on a specific platform. Captures benchmark name, game title, platform, minimum acceptable FPS, maximum frame time, memory ceiling, crash rate threshold, load time SLA, network latency ceiling, CCU capacity target, benchmark version, approval date, and approving authority. Serves as the reference standard against which perf_test_run results are evaluated.

attributes.name: stability_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the stability benchmark record. Primary key for the stability_benchmark data product in the quality domain.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the individual or role (e.g., QA Director, Technical Director, Studio Head) who formally approved this benchmark as the accepted standard for release readiness evaluation.

attributes.name: game_mode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to title.game_mode. Business justification: Stability benchmarks define mode-specific performance targets (campaign vs multiplayer have different FPS/memory SLAs). Release gates and certification require mode-level benchmark compliance for appr

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title for which this stability benchmark is defined. Links the benchmark to the specific game product under evaluation.

attributes.name: kpi_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.kpi_definition. Business justification: Stability benchmarks ARE KPI definitions for technical metrics (crash rate, FPS); this is a definitional relationship linking quality standards to business KPIs.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the target platform (e.g., PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, PC, iOS, Android) for which this benchmark applies. A benchmark is platform-specific as performance thresholds differ by hardware.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: superseded_by_stability_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Reference to the newer stability_benchmark record that replaced this one when it was superseded. Enables version chain traceability. Null if this benchmark is the current active version.

attributes.name: applies_to_build_type
attributes.description: Specifies which build lifecycle stage(s) this benchmark applies to. 'gold_master' = final release build; 'release_candidate' = near-final candidate; 'beta' = public/closed beta; 'alpha' = early development; 'live_patch' = post-launch update; 'all' = applies universally.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal QA Release Standards; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which this benchmark was formally approved by the approving authority and became the active reference standard. Marks the transition from 'pending_approval' to 'active' status.

attributes.name: benchmark_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this benchmark within QA tooling and Jira project tracking (e.g., 'SB-PC-ULTRA-2024-V2'). Used as the business identifier in cross-system references.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management; Gaming Internal QA Governance Standards

attributes.name: benchmark_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name identifying this benchmark record (e.g., 'PC Ultra Settings Gold Master Benchmark v2.1', 'PS5 Launch Stability Baseline'). Serves as the primary identity label for QA teams and stakeholders.

attributes.name: benchmark_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the benchmark record. 'draft' = under construction; 'pending_approval' = awaiting sign-off; 'active' = approved and in use as the reference standard; 'superseded' = replaced by a newer version; 'retired' = no longer applicable.

attributes.name: benchmark_type
attributes.description: Classification of the benchmark by its primary quality concern. 'performance' = FPS/frame time/load time targets; 'stability' = crash rate/memory targets; 'compliance' = platform TRC/TCR requirements; 'certification' = first-party certification readiness; 'regression' = baseline for regression detection.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; ESRB; PEGI

attributes.name: benchmark_version
attributes.description: Semantic version number of this benchmark definition (e.g., '1.0', '2.3', '1.0.1'). Incremented when threshold values or scope are revised. Enables traceability of which version was active at any point in time.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal QA Governance Standards; Perforce Helix Core Version Control

attributes.name: ccu_capacity_target
attributes.description: Target number of Concurrent Users (CCU) the game server infrastructure must support without degradation. Used to validate server-side stability benchmarks for Game as a Service (GaaS) and online multiplayer titles.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Infrastructure Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this stability benchmark record was first created in the system. Audit trail field capturing the initial record creation event in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; Gaming Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: The date from which this benchmark version is binding and must be used as the reference standard for evaluating performance test runs. May differ from approval_date if a future effective date was specified.

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: The date on which this benchmark version ceases to be the active reference standard, typically when superseded by a newer version. Null indicates the benchmark is open-ended and currently active.

attributes.name: game_build_version
attributes.description: The game build version or milestone (e.g., 'Alpha', 'Beta', 'Gold Master', 'v1.2.0') against which this benchmark was defined. Anchors the benchmark to a specific development stage or release candidate.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; Gaming Internal QA Governance Standards

attributes.name: graphics_quality_preset
attributes.description: Graphics quality setting level at which this benchmark was defined and must be evaluated (e.g., 'ultra', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'platform_default'). PC titles may have multiple benchmarks per quality tier.

attributes.name: hardware_config
attributes.description: Description of the reference hardware configuration used to establish this benchmark (e.g., 'PS5 Retail Unit', 'PC - Intel i7-12700K / RTX 3080 / 16GB RAM', 'iPhone 14 Pro'). Ensures benchmark thresholds are interpreted in the correct hardware context.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: is_certification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether passing this benchmark is a mandatory prerequisite for first-party platform certification submission (e.g., Sony TRC, Microsoft TCR, Nintendo Lot Check). True = certification gate; False = internal quality gate only.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: is_release_gate
attributes.description: Indicates whether this benchmark constitutes a hard release quality gate that must be passed before a build can be promoted to Gold Master or submitted for distribution. True = blocking gate; False = advisory/informational benchmark.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal QA Release Standards; Jira Release Planning

attributes.name: jira_epic_key
attributes.description: The Jira Epic key associated with the QA initiative or release milestone that owns this benchmark (e.g., 'QA-1042'). Enables traceability between the benchmark definition and the project management backlog in Jira.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management and Bug Tracking

attributes.name: max_cpu_usage_pct
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable CPU utilization percentage during standard gameplay scenarios. Sustained CPU usage above this threshold may cause frame drops, audio glitches, or instability on target hardware.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: max_crash_rate_pct
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable crash rate expressed as a percentage of sessions (e.g., 0.5000 = 0.5%). Builds exceeding this threshold fail the stability gate and are blocked from release. A key Quality Assurance (QA) release readiness criterion.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Stability Standards; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: max_disk_io_mbps
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Disk I/O Throughput (Megabytes Per Second)
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable disk read/write throughput in megabytes per second during asset streaming and level loading. Critical for open-world titles and platforms with SSD-based streaming architectures (e.g., PS5 SSD).
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: max_frame_time_ms
attributes.description: Maximum allowable frame render time in milliseconds. Exceeding this threshold indicates frame drops or hitches that degrade player experience. Complementary to FPS as it captures frame time variance (e.g., 33.33ms for 30 FPS target).
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: max_gpu_usage_pct
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable GPU utilization percentage during standard gameplay scenarios. Sustained GPU usage above this threshold may indicate rendering inefficiency or thermal throttling risk on target hardware.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: max_hang_rate_pct
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable application hang or freeze rate expressed as a percentage of sessions. Hangs are distinct from crashes and represent unresponsive states that require player intervention. A key stability Quality Assurance (QA) gate.
attributes.references: Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: max_load_time_sec
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Load Time Service Level Agreement (SLA) (Seconds)
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable level load or initial boot time in seconds as defined by the Service Level Agreement (SLA). Exceeding this threshold constitutes a performance failure. Applies to the primary load scenario (e.g., main menu to gameplay).
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: max_memory_usage_mb
attributes.description: Maximum allowable RAM consumption in megabytes during gameplay. Builds exceeding this ceiling risk out-of-memory crashes on target hardware. Platform-specific as console and mobile hardware have fixed memory budgets.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: max_network_latency_ms
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable network round-trip latency in milliseconds for online/multiplayer game modes. Exceeding this ceiling degrades Player versus Player (PvP) and Massively Multiplayer Online (MMO) gameplay quality. Not applicable for offline-only titles.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal QA Network Standards; TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards

attributes.name: max_texture_memory_mb
attributes.description: Maximum allowable VRAM/texture memory consumption in megabytes. Exceeding this ceiling causes texture pop-in, Level of Detail (LOD) degradation, or out-of-memory crashes on GPU-constrained platforms.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: measurement_duration_sec
attributes.description: Duration in seconds over which performance metrics must be sustained to satisfy the benchmark. Ensures thresholds are evaluated over a representative gameplay window rather than a momentary snapshot (e.g., 300 seconds = 5-minute sustained test).

attributes.name: min_fps
attributes.description: The minimum acceptable Frames Per Second (FPS) threshold that a game build must sustain during performance testing. Builds falling below this value fail the benchmark. Measured in frames per second.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for QA engineers and technical directors to document rationale for threshold values, known exceptions, platform-specific caveats, or context about how this benchmark was derived.

attributes.name: percentile_threshold
attributes.description: Statistical percentile at which FPS and frame time thresholds must be met (e.g., 95.00 = 95th percentile, meaning 95% of frames must meet the FPS floor). Distinguishes between average-case and worst-case performance requirements.

attributes.name: resolution
attributes.description: Target display resolution at which this benchmark applies (e.g., '1920x1080', '2560x1440', '3840x2160', '1080p', '4K'). Performance thresholds vary significantly by resolution, particularly for GPU-bound scenarios.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: target_fps
attributes.description: The desired optimal Frames Per Second (FPS) target for the game on this platform (e.g., 30, 60, 120). Represents the intended player experience quality level, distinct from the minimum acceptable floor.
attributes.references: TRC/TCR Platform Certification Standards; Gaming Internal QA Performance Standards

attributes.name: test_scenario
attributes.description: Description of the specific gameplay scenario or test case used to measure performance against this benchmark (e.g., 'Open World Stress Test - 100 NPCs', 'PvP Match - 64 Players', 'Main Menu to Gameplay Load'). Ensures reproducibility of benchmark conditions.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal QA Test Standards; Jira Project Management

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this stability benchmark record. Updated on any change to threshold values, status, or metadata. Supports audit trail and change detection in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; SOC 2; Gaming Internal Data Governance Standards

products.name: crash_report
products.description: Transactional record for each crash event captured during QA testing, playtesting, or live operations monitoring. Records crash timestamp, game title and build version, platform, device/hardware profile, OS version, crash type (hard crash, soft crash, ANR, freeze), crash signature/stack trace hash, reproduction frequency, affected game component, severity, associated defect reference, and resolution status. Enables crash rate trending and stability regression detection.

attributes.name: crash_report_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each crash report record in the quality domain. Primary key for the crash_report data product.

attributes.name: asset_bundle_id

attributes.name: affected_game_component
attributes.description: The high-level game system or feature area where the crash occurred (e.g., Rendering, Physics, Networking, UI, Audio, AI/NPC, Matchmaking, In-App Purchase). Used for component-level crash rate dashboards and sprint planning in Jira.
