attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.drm_entitlement. Business justification: Experiment eligibility depends on entitlement status; assignments must verify player has required DLC/content entitlements before exposing experimental features. Critical for preventing feature leakag

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the internal user who performed the manual override. Null if is_override is false. Used for accountability and audit purposes.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific game title in which the experiment assignment occurred. Enables multi-game experiment tracking.

attributes.name: guild_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.guild. Business justification: Guild-level experiment assignments for testing social features (guild events, perks, tools). Common pattern for controlled rollouts of guild-specific functionality and measuring impact on guild retent

attributes.name: payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.payment. Business justification: Payment flow experiments (checkout UX, payment method presentation) need direct links to payment outcomes for conversion rate and payment success rate analysis.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player who was assigned to this experiment treatment. Unique player identifier used across the gaming platform.

attributes.name: subscription_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.subscription. Business justification: Subscription pricing, tier, and feature experiments require linking player assignments to their subscription records for LTV impact analysis and subscription conversion rate measurement.

attributes.name: treatment_arm_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific treatment variant assigned to the player (e.g., CONTROL, VARIANT_A, VARIANT_B). Used to segment cohorts for analysis.
attributes.references: A/B Testing Best Practices - Treatment Naming Convention

attributes.name: assignment_context
attributes.description: JSON string capturing additional context at assignment time (e.g., player level, session number, geographic region, device type). Used for stratification analysis and debugging.

attributes.name: assignment_hash_seed
attributes.description: Seed value used in deterministic hash assignment algorithm. Enables reproducibility and validation of assignment logic. Null for non-hash assignment methods.

attributes.name: assignment_method
attributes.description: Method used to assign the player to the treatment arm. Deterministic hash ensures consistent assignment across sessions; random provides true randomization; manual for QA testing; stratified for balanced cohorts; targeted for specific player segments.

attributes.name: assignment_priority
attributes.description: Priority level of this experiment assignment when multiple experiments overlap. Higher values indicate higher priority. Used to resolve experiment conflicts and ensure treatment integrity.

attributes.name: assignment_source
attributes.description: System component that performed the assignment. Client SDK for real-time in-game assignment; server API for backend assignment; batch backfill for historical assignment; manual override for QA testing.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the assignment. Active indicates the player is currently in the experiment; completed indicates the experiment ended; invalidated indicates the assignment was retroactively invalidated; excluded indicates the player was removed from analysis.

attributes.name: assignment_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the player was assigned to the treatment arm. Critical for time-based cohort analysis and calculating exposure duration.

attributes.name: bucketing_key
attributes.description: Identifier used for consistent bucketing across related experiments. Typically player_id but may be device_id or household_id for specific experiment designs.

attributes.name: build_number_at_assignment
attributes.description: Internal build number of the game client at assignment time. Used for precise version tracking and troubleshooting assignment issues.

attributes.name: created_by_system
attributes.description: Name of the system or service that created this assignment record (e.g., experiment-service, analytics-pipeline). Used for troubleshooting and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this assignment record was first created in the system. Immutable audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: device_type_at_assignment
attributes.description: Category of device the player was using at assignment time. Used for device-specific performance analysis and cross-device experiment validation.

attributes.name: experiment_layer
attributes.description: Logical layer or namespace of the experiment to enable orthogonal experiment execution. Players can be in one experiment per layer simultaneously without interaction effects.

attributes.name: exposure_count
attributes.description: Number of times the player encountered the treatment during the experiment period. Used for dose-response analysis and engagement measurement.

attributes.name: first_exposure_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player first encountered the treatment in-game. Null if is_exposed is false. Used to calculate time-to-exposure and actual treatment duration.

attributes.name: game_version_at_assignment
attributes.description: Semantic version of the game client at the time of assignment (e.g., 2.5.1). Critical for validating that players received the correct treatment implementation.

attributes.name: geographic_region_at_assignment
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code representing the players geographic location at assignment time. Used for region-specific analysis and regulatory compliance validation.

attributes.name: ineligibility_reason
attributes.description: Reason code or description explaining why a player was marked ineligible. Null if is_eligible is true. Used for quality control and Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) investigation.

attributes.name: invalidation_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the assignment was invalidated (e.g., bot detected, data quality issue, implementation bug). Null if not invalidated. Critical for experiment result validity.

attributes.name: invalidation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the assignment was invalidated. Null if assignment_status is not invalidated. Used for data quality tracking and Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) investigation.

attributes.name: is_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player met all eligibility criteria for the experiment at assignment time. False indicates the player was assigned but later found ineligible (e.g., bot detection, policy violation).

attributes.name: is_exposed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player actually encountered the treatment (true) or was assigned but never reached the experiment trigger point (false). Critical for intent-to-treat vs per-protocol analysis.

attributes.name: is_holdout
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this player is part of a global holdout group excluded from all experiments. Used for long-term cumulative impact measurement.

attributes.name: is_override
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this assignment was manually overridden (true) or followed standard assignment logic (false). Used to identify QA testing and special case assignments.

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the assignment was manually overridden. Null if is_override is false. Used for audit trail and quality assurance.

attributes.name: platform_at_assignment
attributes.description: Gaming platform the player was using when assigned to the experiment. Critical for platform-specific analysis and cross-platform experiment validation. attributes.name: player_segment_at_assignment
attributes.description: Player segment classification at the time of assignment (e.g., new_player, returning_player, whale, casual). Used for segment-specific experiment analysis and Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) checks.

attributes.name: session_id_at_assignment
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the game session during which the assignment occurred. Links to session telemetry for detailed behavioral analysis.

attributes.name: traffic_allocation_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of total eligible traffic allocated to this treatment arm at the time of assignment. Used for power analysis and Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) validation.

attributes.name: treatment_arm_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the treatment variant for reporting and analysis (e.g., Increased Reward Rate, New Onboarding Flow).

attributes.name: reassignment_experiment_assignment_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on experiment_assignment (reassignment_experiment_assignment_id)

products.name: experiment_result
products.description: Transactional record capturing the computed statistical outcome of a concluded or interim-analyzed A/B experiment. Stores experiment reference, analysis run timestamp, analysis type (interim, final, post-hoc), metric name, control arm mean, treatment arm mean, relative lift percentage, absolute delta, p-value, confidence interval lower/upper bounds, statistical power achieved, sample size per arm, SRM flag, and analyst decision (ship, rollback, iterate, inconclusive). One record per metric per analysis run. Enables experiment result auditability and decision traceability.

attributes.name: experiment_result_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the experiment result record. Primary key.

attributes.name: ab_experiment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent A/B experiment that this result belongs to.

attributes.name: approver_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the manager or stakeholder who approved or rejected the analyst decision.

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.asset. Business justification: Experiment results track performance metrics for specific asset variants tested (weapon win rate deltas, cosmetic purchase lift, map engagement changes). Essential for asset balance decisions and cont

attributes.name: kpi_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.kpi_definition. Business justification: experiment_result captures statistical outcomes for specific metrics. Each result measures one defined KPI. Adding kpi_definition_id FK normalizes metric definitions, ensuring experiment results refer

attributes.name: primary_experiment_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the data analyst or data scientist who performed this analysis and made the decision.

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Billing Revenue Recognition Event Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.revenue_recognition. Business justification: Revenue-focused experiment results must link to revenue recognition events for accurate financial impact measurement, especially for subscription and deferred revenue experiments requiring GAAP-compli

attributes.name: absolute_delta
attributes.description: The absolute difference between treatment and control arm means (treatment_mean - control_mean).

attributes.name: analysis_run_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this statistical analysis was executed. Represents the principal business event time for this result record.

attributes.name: analysis_type
attributes.description: The type of statistical analysis performed: interim (mid-experiment check), final (experiment concluded), or post-hoc (retrospective analysis after conclusion).

attributes.name: analysis_window_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the data window used for this analysis.

attributes.name: analysis_window_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the data window used for this analysis.

attributes.name: analyst_decision
attributes.description: The decision made by the analyst based on this result: ship (deploy treatment to all users), rollback (revert to control), iterate (modify and re-test), inconclusive (insufficient evidence), or monitor (continue observation).

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The approval status of the analyst decision: pending (awaiting review), approved (decision confirmed), rejected (decision overturned), or escalated (sent to higher authority).

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the decision was approved or rejected.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_lower
attributes.description: The lower bound of the confidence interval for the treatment effect estimate.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_upper
attributes.description: The upper bound of the confidence interval for the treatment effect estimate.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: The confidence level used for the confidence interval calculation, typically expressed as a percentage (e.g., 95.00, 99.00).

attributes.name: control_arm_mean
attributes.description: The computed mean value of the metric for the control (baseline) arm of the experiment.

attributes.name: control_sample_size
attributes.description: The number of observations (players, sessions, or events) in the control arm for this metric analysis.

attributes.name: control_standard_deviation
attributes.description: The standard deviation of the metric in the control arm, indicating variability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this experiment result record was first created in the system. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: decision_rationale
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of the reasoning behind the analyst decision, including business context and trade-offs considered.

attributes.name: effect_size
attributes.description: Standardized measure of the magnitude of the treatment effect (e.g., Cohen's d, Hedges' g), independent of sample size.

attributes.name: is_primary_metric
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this metric is the primary (decision-making) metric for the experiment, as opposed to a secondary or guardrail metric.

attributes.name: metric_category
attributes.description: The business category of the metric: engagement (DAU, session length), monetization (ARPU, IAP), retention (D1/D7/D30), acquisition (CPI, installs), performance (FPS, load time), or quality (crash rate, bug reports).

attributes.name: minimum_detectable_effect
attributes.description: The smallest effect size that the experiment was designed to detect with the target statistical power.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this experiment result record was last modified. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: multiple_testing_correction
attributes.description: The method used to correct for multiple comparisons, if any (e.g., Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR). None if no correction applied.

attributes.name: p_value
attributes.description: The statistical p-value indicating the probability that the observed difference occurred by chance. Lower values indicate higher statistical significance.

attributes.name: relative_lift_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage change of the treatment arm relative to the control arm. Calculated as ((treatment_mean - control_mean) / control_mean) * 100.

attributes.name: srm_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a Sample Ratio Mismatch was detected, which suggests potential bias in the experiment randomization or data collection.
attributes.references: A/B Testing Best Practices - Sample Ratio Mismatch Detection

attributes.name: srm_p_value
attributes.description: The p-value from the chi-square test for Sample Ratio Mismatch detection. Low values indicate significant deviation from expected sample ratios.
attributes.references: A/B Testing Best Practices - Sample Ratio Mismatch Detection

attributes.name: statistical_power
attributes.description: The achieved statistical power of the test, representing the probability of detecting a true effect. Typically expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8000 for 80% power).

attributes.name: statistical_test_method
attributes.description: The statistical test method used to compute this result (e.g., t-test, z-test, Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, Bayesian analysis, bootstrap).

attributes.name: treatment_arm_mean
attributes.description: The computed mean value of the metric for the treatment (variant) arm of the experiment.

attributes.name: treatment_sample_size
attributes.description: The number of observations (players, sessions, or events) in the treatment arm for this metric analysis.

attributes.name: treatment_standard_deviation
attributes.description: The standard deviation of the metric in the treatment arm, indicating variability.

attributes.name: prior_analysis_experiment_result_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on experiment_result (prior_analysis_experiment_result_id)

products.name: funnel_definition
products.description: Master catalog of player behavior conversion funnels defined and owned by the analytics domain. Each record defines a funnel name, owning game title, funnel type (onboarding, monetization, feature adoption, PvP engagement, battle pass progression), ordered list of funnel steps (stored as JSON array of event type references), attribution window in hours, player population filter criteria, and funnel version. Funnels are versioned to support historical comparison. Used by product managers and data analysts to standardize conversion analysis across titles.

attributes.name: funnel_definition_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the funnel definition record. Primary key.

attributes.name: content_release_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.content_release. Business justification: Funnels measure content drop adoption (download → install → first play → D7 retention). Funnel definitions scope to specific releases for launch performance tracking and content strategy optimization.

attributes.name: dev_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to studio.dev_project. Business justification: Funnel definitions are created during development to measure player progression through features/content. Links analytics measurement design to the project that owns the feature, enabling project-spec

attributes.name: game_mode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to title.game_mode. Business justification: Conversion funnels are often mode-specific: tutorial completion in campaign, first match completion in multiplayer, ranked placement matches. Mode context is essential for accurate funnel analysis and

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title that owns this funnel definition. Each funnel is scoped to a specific game.

attributes.name: ip_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to licensing.ip_agreement. Business justification: Funnels track licensed content conversion (e.g., "IP character trial → purchase"). Agreement context needed for royalty attribution on funnel conversions and IP monetization analysis. Real business pr

attributes.name: licensed_ip_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to licensing.licensed_ip. Business justification: Funnels measure IP-specific conversion paths (awareness → trial → purchase). Links IP catalog to funnel analytics for IP performance measurement and licensing value assessment.

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Funnel definitions are owned by product analysts or game economists who define conversion metrics. Business process: funnel design governance, metric ownership, business reporting accountability. Crit

attributes.name: parent_funnel_definition_id
attributes.description: Reference to the previous version of this funnel definition. Null for version 1. Used to trace funnel evolution and compare conversion rates across versions.

attributes.name: storefront_listing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.storefront_listing. Business justification: Conversion funnels track storefront listing views → add-to-cart → purchase. Funnel definitions must reference the specific listing being analyzed for ASO optimization, listing A/B tests, and cross-sto

attributes.name: support_ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.support_ticket. Business justification: Support resolution funnels track ticket lifecycle stages (opened → first response → resolved → closed). Standard customer service analytics for SLA monitoring and support efficiency measurement.

attributes.name: ab_test_variant
attributes.description: Identifier for the A/B test variant this funnel measures (e.g., 'control', 'treatment_a', 'treatment_b'). Null if is_ab_test_funnel is False. Used to segment funnel analysis by experiment arm.

attributes.name: attribution_window_hours
attributes.description: Time window in hours within which all funnel steps must be completed for a player to be counted as a conversion. For example, a 24-hour window means all steps must occur within 24 hours of the first step. Used to define conversion time constraints.

attributes.name: benchmark_conversion_rate
attributes.description: Industry or historical benchmark conversion rate percentage for this funnel type, expressed as a decimal. Used for comparative analysis and goal setting. May be sourced from industry reports or historical game performance.

attributes.name: business_objective
attributes.description: Description of the business objective this funnel measures. Examples: 'Increase Day 1 retention to 40%', 'Improve battle pass purchase conversion to 15%', 'Reduce tutorial drop-off by 20%'. Links funnel to Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Objectives and Key Results (OKRs).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this funnel definition record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: data_retention_days
attributes.description: Number of days that funnel analysis results should be retained before archival or deletion. Aligns with data retention policies and regulatory requirements such as General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 - Data Retention Principles, COPPA - Data Retention Requirements

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this funnel definition version was superseded or deactivated. Null for currently active versions. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Used to support historical funnel analysis and version comparison.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this funnel definition version became active and started being used for player behavior analysis. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: funnel_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier code for the funnel definition. Used in analytics queries and reporting systems to reference the funnel programmatically.

attributes.name: funnel_definition_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the funnel definition, including its purpose, key steps, and how it should be interpreted. Provides context for analysts and product managers using this funnel for conversion analysis.

attributes.name: funnel_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the funnel definition. Used by product managers and analysts to identify the funnel (e.g., 'New Player Onboarding', 'Battle Pass Purchase Flow', 'PvP First Match').

attributes.name: funnel_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the funnel definition. Active funnels are used in production analytics. Draft funnels are under development. Inactive funnels are temporarily disabled. Deprecated funnels are replaced by newer versions. Archived funnels are retained for historical analysis only.

attributes.name: funnel_steps
attributes.description: Ordered list of funnel steps stored as JSON array of event type references. Each step represents a player behavior event that must occur in sequence. Example: ['player_registered', 'tutorial_started', 'tutorial_completed', 'first_match_entered', 'first_match_completed']. The order defines the conversion path.

attributes.name: funnel_type
attributes.description: Classification of the funnel by its primary business purpose. Onboarding tracks new player progression through First-Time User Experience (FTUE). Monetization tracks conversion to paying users and In-App Purchase (IAP) flows. Feature adoption tracks engagement with new game features. PvP engagement tracks Player versus Player mode entry. Battle pass progression tracks seasonal content completion. Retention tracks Day 1/Day 7/Day 30 (D1/D7/D30) return behavior.

attributes.name: is_ab_test_funnel
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this funnel is part of an A/B experimentation framework. True if the funnel is used to measure treatment vs control group conversion. False for standard production funnels.

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is the current active version of the funnel. True for the latest version, False for historical versions. Only one version per funnel_code should be current at any time.

attributes.name: last_executed_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this funnel definition was last executed in an analytics query. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used to identify stale or unused funnels for archival.

attributes.name: max_player_level
attributes.description: Maximum player level for inclusion in this funnel analysis. Null if no upper level restriction applies. Used to create level-specific funnel segments (e.g., new player vs veteran player funnels).

attributes.name: min_player_level
attributes.description: Minimum player level required for inclusion in this funnel analysis. Null if no level restriction applies. Used to create level-gated funnel definitions (e.g., endgame content funnels).

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this funnel definition. Used for audit trail and change management.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this funnel definition record was last modified. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Updated whenever funnel metadata changes. Audit field for change tracking.

attributes.name: monetization_model_filter
attributes.description: Monetization model scope for this funnel. Free-to-Play (F2P) for games with In-App Purchases (IAP). Premium for paid upfront games. Subscription for recurring payment models. Game-as-a-Service (GaaS) for live operations models. All for cross-model funnels.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes field for additional context, assumptions, known issues, or interpretation guidance for this funnel definition. Used by analysts to document funnel-specific considerations.

attributes.name: owning_team
attributes.description: Name of the product or analytics team that owns and maintains this funnel definition. Responsible for funnel accuracy, updates, and interpretation of results.

attributes.name: platform_filter
attributes.description: Platform scope for this funnel definition. Specifies whether the funnel applies to all platforms or is specific to console, PC, mobile, or web. Used to create platform-specific conversion analysis.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs - Platform Standards

attributes.name: player_population_filter
attributes.description: JSON-encoded filter criteria defining which player population this funnel applies to. May include filters by player segment, acquisition channel, geographic region, platform, or cohort. Example: {'platform': 'mobile', 'region': 'NA', 'install_date_after': '2024-01-01'}. Empty string means all players.

attributes.name: region_filter
attributes.description: Geographic region filter for this funnel, using 3-letter ISO country codes or region groupings. Examples: 'USA', 'GBR', 'JPN', or 'all' for global. Used to create region-specific conversion analysis.

attributes.name: step_count
attributes.description: Total number of steps in the funnel. Derived from the funnel_steps array length. Used for quick filtering and funnel complexity classification.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of tags for categorization and discovery. Examples: 'monetization', 'mobile', 'high-priority', 'experiment-2024-Q1'. Used for filtering and organizing funnels in analytics tools.

attributes.name: target_conversion_rate
attributes.description: Target conversion rate percentage for this funnel, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 35.50 for 35.5%). Represents the business goal for end-to-end funnel completion. Used to evaluate funnel performance against objectives.

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Number of times this funnel definition has been used in analytics queries or reports. Incremented each time the funnel is executed. Used to identify popular funnels and prioritize maintenance.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of this funnel definition. Funnels are versioned to support historical comparison and A/B testing. Version 1 is the initial definition. Incremented when funnel steps, attribution window, or filters are modified.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the analyst or product manager who created this funnel definition. Used for accountability and collaboration.

products.name: funnel_step_event
products.description: Transactional record capturing each individual player's completion of a specific step within a defined conversion funnel. Stores funnel definition reference, funnel step ordinal, player reference, game title reference, step completion timestamp, time elapsed since funnel entry (seconds), time elapsed since previous step (seconds), platform, session reference, and whether the player subsequently completed the next step (lookahead flag for pipeline efficiency). Enables step-level drop-off analysis and cohort-level funnel visualization.

attributes.name: funnel_step_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each individual funnel step completion event. Primary key for the funnel step event entity.

attributes.name: ab_test_variant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the A/B test variant the player was assigned to when completing this step. Enables experimentation analysis and variant-specific funnel performance comparison.

attributes.name: achievement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to title.achievement. Business justification: Achievement unlocks are common funnel steps for progression analysis (first achievement → 10 achievements → platinum trophy). Essential for measuring engagement milestones and identifying drop-off poi

attributes.name: forum_thread_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.forum_thread. Business justification: Community engagement funnels track progression through forum interactions (view → read → reply → subscribe). Core analytics for community activation and measuring content stickiness.

attributes.name: funnel_definition_id
attributes.description: Reference to the funnel definition that this step belongs to. Links to the funnel configuration that defines the sequence of steps being tracked.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title in which this funnel step was completed. Enables funnel performance comparison across different games.

attributes.name: marketing_campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the marketing campaign that drove the player into this funnel. Enables campaign-specific funnel ROI analysis and attribution.

attributes.name: payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.payment. Business justification: Payment funnel analysis requires linking funnel steps to payment attempts and completions for payment success rate optimization and fraud detection funnel impact measurement.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player who completed this funnel step. Enables player-level funnel progression tracking and cohort analysis.

attributes.name: pricing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.pricing. Business justification: Funnel events must capture exact pricing tier and promotional status at time of conversion for price elasticity analysis, promotional effectiveness measurement, and regional pricing optimization. Esse

attributes.name: retention_cohort_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player cohort (e.g., install date cohort, acquisition channel cohort) for cohort-based funnel analysis and retention tracking.

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player session during which this funnel step was completed. Enables session-level funnel analysis and multi-step session tracking.

attributes.name: storefront_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.storefront_order. Business justification: Purchase funnel steps must link to completed orders for conversion rate calculation, funnel drop-off analysis, and revenue attribution—core e-commerce analytics in gaming.

attributes.name: support_ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.support_ticket. Business justification: Individual funnel steps tied to specific tickets for conversion analysis through support journey. Required for identifying drop-off points in ticket resolution and optimizing support workflows.

attributes.name: ugc_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.ugc_submission. Business justification: Creator funnels track UGC journey (browse → download → rate → create own). Core creator economy analytics for measuring conversion to active creators and content ecosystem health.

attributes.name: app_version
attributes.description: Version of the game application in which this funnel step was completed. Enables version-specific funnel performance tracking and regression detection.

attributes.name: completed_next_step_flag
attributes.description: Lookahead indicator showing whether the player subsequently completed the next step in the funnel. Pre-computed for pipeline efficiency to enable fast drop-off rate calculations without self-joins.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code representing the players geographic location when completing this step. Enables geo-specific funnel analysis and localization optimization.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this funnel step event record was first created in the analytics system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and late-arriving event detection.

attributes.name: days_since_install
attributes.description: Number of days elapsed between the players initial game install and the completion of this funnel step. Used for lifecycle-based funnel analysis and retention correlation.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Category of device used to complete this funnel step. Enables device-specific funnel optimization and cross-device journey analysis.

attributes.name: funnel_instance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for a single players journey through a specific funnel. Groups all step events for one player in one funnel attempt, enabling instance-level analysis and abandoned funnel recovery.

attributes.name: funnel_step_ordinal
attributes.description: Sequential position of this step within the funnel (1 for first step, 2 for second, etc.). Used to order steps and calculate drop-off rates between consecutive steps.

attributes.name: is_first_time_completion
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the first time this player has ever completed this specific funnel step across all funnel instances. Used to distinguish new vs. repeat step completions.

attributes.name: platform
attributes.description: Gaming platform on which the player completed this funnel step. Enables platform-specific funnel performance analysis and optimization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ios|android|windows|macos|playstation|xbox|nintendo_switch|web — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Platform SDK Standards (Steamworks, Epic Games Store, Console SDKs)

attributes.name: player_level_at_step
attributes.description: The players in-game level or progression tier at the time of completing this funnel step. Enables analysis of how player progression correlates with funnel conversion.

attributes.name: player_lifetime_spend_at_step
attributes.description: Cumulative amount the player has spent in the game up to the point of completing this funnel step. Enables monetization-based funnel segmentation and high-value player tracking.

attributes.name: referrer_url
attributes.description: URL of the page or source that referred the player to this funnel step. Enables attribution analysis and traffic source funnel performance tracking.

attributes.name: step_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the player completed this specific funnel step. Primary business event timestamp for funnel progression analysis.

attributes.name: step_event_name
attributes.description: Name of the specific event that triggered this funnel step completion (e.g., tutorial_started, first_purchase_completed, level_10_reached). Provides semantic context for what action the player took.

attributes.name: step_metadata_json
attributes.description: JSON string containing additional step-specific contextual data (e.g., item purchased, level reached, tutorial section). Provides flexible schema for step-specific attributes without schema changes.

attributes.name: time_since_funnel_entry_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds from when the player first entered the funnel (completed step 1) to when they completed this step. Used to measure overall funnel velocity and identify slow progression patterns.

attributes.name: time_since_previous_step_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds from the completion of the immediately preceding funnel step to this step. Used to identify bottlenecks and friction points between consecutive steps.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this funnel step event record was last modified. Used for tracking lookahead flag updates and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: user_agent
attributes.description: Browser or client user agent string captured at the time of step completion. Provides detailed device and browser context for web-based funnels.

attributes.name: previous_funnel_step_event_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on funnel_step_event (previous_funnel_step_event_id)

attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the KPI definition that replaces this deprecated KPI. Enables continuity tracking when KPIs evolve or are redefined.

attributes.name: business_definition
attributes.description: Comprehensive business definition of what this KPI measures, why it matters to the business, and how it should be interpreted by stakeholders. Serves as the authoritative business glossary entry.

attributes.name: calculation_formula_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of how the KPI is calculated, including the mathematical formula, business logic, and any filters or conditions applied (e.g., 'Count of unique player_ids with at least one session event in the calendar day').

attributes.name: calculation_logic_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the calculation logic or formula used to compute this KPI. Enables tracking of changes to KPI definitions over time and ensures historical comparability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this KPI definition record was first created in the catalog.

attributes.name: data_freshness_sla_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Freshness Service Level Agreement (SLA) in Minutes
attributes.description: The maximum acceptable delay in minutes between the source event occurring and the KPI value being available for reporting. Defines the data freshness commitment for this KPI.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the operational system or analytics platform that provides the source data for this KPI (e.g., GameAnalytics, Amplitude, Unity Analytics, custom telemetry pipeline).

attributes.name: denominator_event_type
attributes.description: The event type or population that forms the denominator of the KPI calculation (e.g., 'active_players', 'paying_users', 'installs'). Null for count-based KPIs.

attributes.name: deprecation_date
attributes.description: The date on which this KPI definition was deprecated or retired from active use. Null if the KPI is still active.

attributes.name: deprecation_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why this KPI was deprecated (e.g., 'Replaced by more granular cohort-based retention metric', 'Business priority shifted', 'Data source no longer available').

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this KPI definition version ceased to be effective. Null if the definition is currently active. Supports temporal validity tracking.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this KPI definition became effective and started being calculated. Supports temporal validity tracking for KPI definitions.

attributes.name: green_threshold_value
attributes.description: The threshold value at or above which the KPI is considered on-target or exceeding expectations (green status). Used for traffic-light reporting.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this KPI definition is currently active and being calculated. False indicates the KPI has been deprecated or retired.

attributes.name: kpi_category
attributes.description: The primary business category this KPI belongs to: engagement (player activity metrics), monetization (revenue and spending metrics), retention (player return behavior), acquisition (new player metrics), performance (technical performance metrics), or balance (game economy and fairness metrics).

attributes.name: kpi_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code or abbreviation for the KPI used in reports and dashboards (e.g., DAU, ARPU, D7RET).

attributes.name: kpi_name
attributes.description: The canonical business name of the KPI metric (e.g., Daily Active Users, Average Revenue Per User, Day 7 Retention Rate).

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the person who last modified this KPI definition record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this KPI definition record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: measurement_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the KPI value (e.g., 'count', 'USD', 'percentage', 'minutes', 'ratio', 'score'). Provides context for interpreting the KPI value.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, caveats, known limitations, or special instructions related to this KPI definition.

attributes.name: numerator_event_type
attributes.description: The event type or metric that forms the numerator of the KPI calculation (e.g., 'purchase_completed', 'session_start', 'level_completed'). Null for KPIs that are not ratio-based.

attributes.name: owning_analytics_team
attributes.description: The name of the analytics team or business intelligence unit responsible for maintaining this KPI definition, ensuring data quality, and supporting business users.

attributes.name: red_threshold_value
attributes.description: The lower bound threshold value below which the KPI is considered critically underperforming (red status). Used for traffic-light reporting and alerting.

attributes.name: related_okr
attributes.description: Reference to the company or team OKR (Objectives and Key Results) that this KPI supports or measures progress against.

attributes.name: reporting_dashboard_url
attributes.description: The URL link to the primary business intelligence dashboard or report where this KPI is visualized (e.g., Tableau, Looker, Amplitude dashboard).

attributes.name: scope_type
attributes.description: The organizational scope at which this KPI is measured: platform-level (across all games), title-specific (single game), studio-level (development team), region-specific (geographic market), segment-specific (player cohort), or global (enterprise-wide).

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The business target or goal value for this KPI. Used to assess performance against objectives and key results (OKRs).

attributes.name: threshold_direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether higher values are better (e.g., revenue, retention), lower values are better (e.g., churn, cost per install), or the target value is optimal (e.g., game balance metrics).

attributes.name: parent_kpi_definition_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on kpi_definition (parent_kpi_definition_id)

products.name: kpi_target

Separates the KPI definition (what we measure) from the KPI target (what we aim for), enabling target versioning and accountability tracking across planning cycles.

attributes.description: Reference to the prior version of this target if it has been revised. Supports target history and change tracking.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this KPI target was formally approved. Marks the official commitment to the target value.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The approval workflow status for this target. Tracks whether the target has been formally reviewed and approved by leadership.

attributes.name: baseline_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the period used to calculate the baseline value. Completes the historical comparison window definition.

attributes.name: baseline_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the period used to calculate the baseline value. Defines the historical comparison window.

attributes.name: baseline_value
attributes.description: The historical or current baseline performance value from which improvement is measured. Provides context for target ambition and growth expectations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this KPI target record was first created in the system. Audit field for record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: floor_value
attributes.description: The minimum acceptable value or threshold below which performance is considered unsatisfactory. Defines the lower bound for acceptable performance.

attributes.name: is_public_commitment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this target has been publicly communicated to investors, partners, or external stakeholders. Flags targets with external accountability.

attributes.name: linked_okr_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Linked Objectives and Key Results (OKR) ID
attributes.description: Reference to the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) framework objective that this KPI target supports. Aligns operational targets with strategic objectives.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this KPI target record was last modified. Audit field for change tracking and data lineage.

attributes.name: planning_cycle
attributes.description: The business planning cycle or period identifier during which this target was established (e.g., FY2024, Q1-2024, Season-3). Links targets to strategic planning windows.

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: Geographic region code for which this target applies (e.g., NAM, EUR, APAC). Supports regional performance management and localized target-setting.

attributes.name: stretch_target_value
attributes.description: The aspirational or stretch target value that represents exceptional performance beyond the committed target. Used for incentive planning and goal-setting.

attributes.name: target_confidence_level
attributes.description: The level of confidence or certainty that the target can be achieved based on current conditions and assumptions. Supports risk assessment and scenario planning.

attributes.name: target_notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or context about this target. Captures supplementary information for planning and review discussions.

attributes.name: target_owner_type
attributes.description: The type of organizational entity responsible for achieving this KPI target. Categorizes ownership by functional area.

attributes.name: target_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the period for which this KPI target applies. Defines the conclusion of the measurement window.

attributes.name: target_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the period for which this KPI target applies. Defines the beginning of the measurement window.

attributes.name: target_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measurement for the target values (e.g., count, percentage, currency, ratio, minutes, sessions). Provides context for interpreting target values.

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The primary target value that the organization aims to achieve for this KPI during the specified period. This is the committed performance goal.

attributes.name: target_version

attributes.name: superseded_kpi_target_id

attributes.name: churn_risk_score

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: d7_retention_rate

attributes.name: effective_end_date

attributes.name: last_refresh_timestamp

attributes.name: model_training_date

attributes.name: modified_by

attributes.name: next_refresh_timestamp

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: player_count_percentage

attributes.name: playtime_weight
attributes.description: Relative weight or importance of playtime-related features in the segmentation model, expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Used for model interpretability.

attributes.name: refresh_cadence
attributes.description: Frequency at which player assignments to this segment are recalculated and updated. Determines data freshness for targeting and analytics.

attributes.name: segment_boundary_criteria
attributes.description: Technical definition of the thresholds, ranges, or clustering boundaries that define membership in this segment (e.g., 'avg_daily_playtime > 120 min AND mtx_spend_30d > 50 USD'). Used for segment assignment logic.

attributes.name: segment_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code for the segment used in technical systems and data pipelines (e.g., 'HG01', 'SB02', 'WW03').

attributes.name: segment_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the behavioral characteristics, play patterns, and defining traits of players in this segment.

attributes.name: segment_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the behavioral segment (e.g., 'Hardcore Grinders', 'Social Butterflies', 'Weekend Warriors', 'Whales', 'Casual Explorers'). Used for reporting and targeting.

attributes.name: segment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the segment. Active segments are used for targeting and analytics; deprecated segments are retained for historical analysis only.

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Primary categorization of the segment based on the dominant behavioral dimension: engagement (activity level), monetization (spending behavior), retention (churn risk), playstyle (gameplay preferences), social (community interaction), or hybrid (multi-dimensional).

attributes.name: segmentation_model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the data science model or algorithm used to generate this segment (e.g., 'v2.3.1', 'kmeans_v5'). Enables tracking of model evolution and A/B testing of segmentation approaches.

attributes.name: session_frequency_weight
attributes.description: Relative weight of session frequency features in the segmentation model, expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: social_weight
attributes.description: Relative weight of social interaction and community engagement features in the segmentation model, expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: target_audience

products.name: behavior_segment_membership
products.description: Association record tracking which players belong to which analytics behavioral segments at each point in time. Captures player reference, player_behavior_segment reference, assignment timestamp, assignment method (rule-based, ML model), model version used, segment score or confidence value, previous segment reference (for migration tracking), and expiry timestamp. Enables cohort analysis, segment migration tracking, and behavioral drift detection. Distinct from player.segment_membership which tracks live-ops operational segments.

attributes.name: behavior_segment_membership_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the behavior segment membership record. Primary key for tracking player-to-segment associations over time.

attributes.name: ab_experiment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the A/B test or experimentation framework that may have influenced this segment assignment. Null if not part of an experiment. Used for measuring experiment impact on segmentation.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific game title for which this behavioral segment membership applies. Enables game-specific segmentation and cross-title behavioral analysis.

attributes.name: guild_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.guild. Business justification: Guild membership influences behavioral segmentation (guild-focused players vs solo). Real segmentation dimension for retention modeling and social feature targeting in multiplayer games.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player who is assigned to this behavioral segment. Links to the player master entity.

attributes.name: primary_player_behavior_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the behavioral segment definition that this player is assigned to. Links to the segment taxonomy maintained by analytics.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the gaming platform (console, PC, mobile) where this behavioral segment membership was observed. Enables platform-specific segmentation and cross-platform behavior tracking.

attributes.name: subscription_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.subscription. Business justification: Subscription tier and engagement segments need direct links to subscription records for targeted retention campaigns, upgrade offers, and churn prevention interventions.

attributes.name: assignment_batch_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the batch or job run that created this segment assignment. Enables grouping of assignments from the same processing cycle for quality control and rollback scenarios.

attributes.name: assignment_method
attributes.description: The mechanism used to assign the player to this segment. Rule-based uses predefined business logic, ML model uses machine learning predictions, manual is analyst-driven, hybrid combines multiple methods, cohort import is bulk assignment, and API is external system integration.

attributes.name: assignment_reason
attributes.description: Human-readable explanation or business justification for why the player was assigned to this segment. May include rule criteria met, model features that triggered assignment, or analyst notes for manual assignments.

attributes.name: assignment_source_system
attributes.description: The system or platform that generated this segment assignment. Examples include GameAnalytics, Amplitude, internal ML pipeline, or manual analyst tools. Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: assignment_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the player was assigned to this behavioral segment. Represents the business event time of segment assignment.

attributes.name: confidence_value
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level of the segment assignment, typically expressed as a probability between 0.0 and 1.0. Used for quality control and filtering low-confidence assignments in downstream analytics.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this segment membership record was first created in the analytics system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of the data quality or reliability of this segment assignment. Valid means high confidence, suspect indicates potential issues, incomplete means missing input data, stale means outdated, anomaly indicates statistical outlier.

attributes.name: expiry_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this segment membership expires or is superseded by a new assignment. Null indicates the membership is currently active. Used for temporal segment analysis and cohort tracking.

attributes.name: feature_vector_hash
attributes.description: Hash of the feature vector or input data used to generate this segment assignment. Enables reproducibility checks and detection of data drift in ML-based segmentation.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this segment membership is currently active. True means the player is currently in this segment, False means the membership has expired or been superseded.

attributes.name: is_primary_segment
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this is the players primary behavioral segment when they belong to multiple segments. True for the highest-priority or most relevant segment, False for secondary segments.

attributes.name: last_recalculation_timestamp
attributes.description: The most recent date and time when this segment membership was re-evaluated, regardless of whether the assignment changed. Used to track data freshness and identify stale assignments.

attributes.name: migration_count
attributes.description: The number of times this player has moved between behavioral segments. Used to identify players with unstable or evolving behavior patterns and to measure segment churn.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: The version identifier of the machine learning model or rule set used to generate this segment assignment. Enables tracking of model performance and segment drift over time. Null for manual assignments.

attributes.name: next_recalculation_timestamp
attributes.description: The scheduled date and time for the next re-evaluation of this segment membership. Used for planning refresh cycles and ensuring timely segment updates.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, observations, or metadata about this segment membership. Used by analysts to document special cases, data quality issues, or business insights.

attributes.name: override_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the analyst or business user who performed the manual override. Null if override_flag is False. Used for accountability and audit purposes.

attributes.name: override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment assignment was manually overridden by an analyst or business user, superseding the automated assignment logic. Used for audit trails and understanding manual interventions.

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: Business justification for why this segment assignment was manually overridden. Null if override_flag is False. Provides context for understanding exceptions to automated segmentation.

attributes.name: recalculation_frequency
attributes.description: The cadence at which this segment membership is re-evaluated and potentially updated. Indicates how fresh the segment assignment is and when the next refresh is expected.

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: Geographic region code where the player was located when assigned to this segment. Enables regional behavioral analysis and localized segment strategies. Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or custom regional groupings.

attributes.name: segment_entry_date
attributes.description: The calendar date when the player first entered this behavioral segment, used for day-level cohort analysis and retention tracking. Complements assignment_timestamp for date-grain reporting.

attributes.name: segment_exit_date
attributes.description: The calendar date when the player exited this behavioral segment, either by moving to another segment or becoming inactive. Null for currently active memberships. Used for segment tenure and churn analysis.

attributes.name: segment_priority
attributes.description: Priority ranking when a player qualifies for multiple behavioral segments simultaneously. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used to resolve segment conflicts and determine primary segment assignment.

attributes.name: segment_score
attributes.description: The confidence score or probability value indicating how strongly the player matches this segment profile. Range typically 0.0 to 1.0 for ML models, or custom scoring for rule-based assignments. Higher values indicate stronger segment affinity.

attributes.name: segment_stability_score
attributes.description: Metric indicating how stable or volatile this players segment membership has been over time. Higher scores indicate consistent segment membership, lower scores indicate frequent segment changes. Used for behavioral drift detection.

attributes.name: tenure_days
attributes.description: The number of days the player has been or was a member of this behavioral segment. Calculated as the difference between entry and exit dates, or entry date and current date for active memberships.

attributes.name: treatment_variant
attributes.description: The specific experiment treatment or variant the player was exposed to that may have influenced their behavioral segment. Null if not part of an experiment. Used for causal analysis of segment drivers.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this segment membership record was last modified. Used for tracking changes and ensuring data freshness in downstream analytics.

attributes.name: previous_behavior_segment_membership_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on behavior_segment_membership (previous_behavior_segment_membership_id)

products.name: model_serving_event
products.description: Transactional record of each real-time or batch model inference event executed by a deployed ML model. Captures ml_model_registry reference, inference timestamp, inference mode (real-time API, batch job), player reference (if applicable), input feature vector hash, output prediction value or class, prediction confidence score, serving latency (ms), serving infrastructure endpoint, and whether the prediction was acted upon (e.g., triggered a live-ops action). Enables model performance monitoring, prediction drift detection, and A/B comparison of model versions in production.

attributes.name: model_serving_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each model inference event. Primary key for the model serving event record.

attributes.name: ab_experiment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the A/B test or experiment this inference is part of. Enables comparison of model versions and treatment effects.

attributes.name: game_session_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game session during which this inference was executed. Links predictions to player gameplay context.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the game title for which this prediction was made. Enables game-specific model performance analysis.

attributes.name: ml_model_registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the deployed ML model that executed this inference. Links to the ML model registry.

attributes.name: model_deployment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific deployment instance of the model. Enables tracking of deployment-specific performance issues.

attributes.name: model_version_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific version of the ML model used for this inference. Enables A/B testing and version comparison.

attributes.name: payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.payment. Business justification: Real-time fraud detection models score payment attempts. Predictions must link to payment records for model validation, false positive analysis, and fraud prevention effectiveness measurement.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player for whom the prediction was made. Nullable for non-player-specific batch predictions.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Reference to the gaming platform (console, PC, mobile) where the inference was executed. Enables platform-specific model tuning.

attributes.name: subscription_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.subscription. Business justification: Churn prediction models target subscribers. Serving events must link to subscription records for intervention tracking, model validation, and retention campaign effectiveness measurement.

attributes.name: support_ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.support_ticket. Business justification: ML models serve predictions during support interactions (churn risk, satisfaction prediction, intelligent routing). Live ops use case for predictive support and agent assist systems.

attributes.name: ugc_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.ugc_submission. Business justification: UGC moderation and recommendation models score submissions (safety, quality, discoverability). Core content safety and discovery systems for user-generated content platforms.

attributes.name: action_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the downstream action was executed based on this prediction. Nullable if no action taken.

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: The type of action triggered by this prediction (e.g., push notification, in-game offer, content recommendation, matchmaking adjustment). Nullable if no action taken.

attributes.name: batch_job_reference
attributes.description: Identifier for the batch job if this inference was part of a batch scoring run. Nullable for real-time inferences.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this model serving event record was created in the data lakehouse. Used for data pipeline monitoring and audit trails.

attributes.name: data_drift_score
attributes.description: Calculated drift score comparing input feature distribution to training data distribution. Used for model retraining triggers.

attributes.name: error_code
attributes.description: The error code if the inference failed (e.g., feature_missing, timeout, model_unavailable). Nullable if no error occurred.

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: Detailed error message if the inference failed. Nullable if no error occurred.

attributes.name: experiment_variant
attributes.description: The experiment variant or treatment group this inference belongs to (e.g., control, treatment_a, treatment_b). Nullable if not part of an experiment.

attributes.name: feature_extraction_latency_ms
attributes.description: Time spent extracting and preparing input features before model inference. Helps identify preprocessing bottlenecks.

attributes.name: feature_store_version
attributes.description: Version of the feature store schema used to retrieve input features. Tracks feature engineering pipeline changes.

attributes.name: inference_mode
attributes.description: The execution mode of the inference: real-time API call, scheduled batch job, streaming pipeline, or edge device inference.

attributes.name: inference_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the model inference was executed. Critical for latency analysis and temporal drift detection.

attributes.name: input_feature_vector_hash
attributes.description: Hash of the input feature vector used for the prediction. Enables detection of duplicate requests and feature drift analysis without storing full feature vectors.

attributes.name: model_compute_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated compute cost in USD for executing this inference. Enables cost-per-prediction analysis and ROI calculation.

attributes.name: model_framework
attributes.description: The machine learning framework used for this model (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, XGBoost). Supports framework-specific performance analysis.

attributes.name: model_inference_latency_ms
attributes.description: Time spent in the actual model inference computation, excluding feature preparation and post-processing.

attributes.name: model_input_feature_count
attributes.description: The number of features in the input vector for this inference. Helps detect feature schema drift.

attributes.name: model_type
attributes.description: The type of machine learning model (e.g., classification, regression, ranking, recommendation, reinforcement_learning). Enables model category performance comparison.

attributes.name: prediction_acted_upon_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the prediction triggered a downstream action (e.g., live-ops intervention, personalized offer, content recommendation displayed).

attributes.name: prediction_cache_hit_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this prediction was served from cache rather than computed. Affects latency and cost metrics.

attributes.name: prediction_class
attributes.description: The predicted class label for classification models (e.g., churn risk tier, player segment, content recommendation category). Nullable for regression models.

attributes.name: prediction_confidence_score
attributes.description: The model's confidence score for the prediction, typically ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. Used for threshold-based decision making and model quality monitoring.

attributes.name: prediction_error_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the inference encountered an error during execution. Used for model reliability monitoring.

attributes.name: prediction_output_value
attributes.description: The primary prediction output from the model. May be a numeric value, class label, or JSON-encoded complex output depending on model type.

attributes.name: prediction_probability_distribution
attributes.description: JSON-encoded probability distribution across all possible classes for classification models. Enables detailed analysis of model uncertainty.

attributes.name: prediction_shap_values
attributes.description: JSON-encoded SHAP values explaining feature contributions to the prediction. Enables model interpretability and explainability analysis.

attributes.name: prediction_use_case
attributes.description: The business use case for this prediction (e.g., churn_prediction, ltv_forecast, content_recommendation, matchmaking, game_balance). Enables use-case-specific ROI analysis.

attributes.name: request_trace_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the inference request. Enables end-to-end tracing across distributed systems.

attributes.name: serving_endpoint
attributes.description: The infrastructure endpoint or service that executed the inference (e.g., API gateway URL, batch job name, edge node identifier).

attributes.name: serving_latency_ms
attributes.description: The total time in milliseconds from inference request to response delivery. Critical KPI for real-time serving performance monitoring.

attributes.name: fallback_model_serving_event_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on model_serving_event (fallback_model_serving_event_id)

products.name: feature_store_definition
products.description: Master catalog of ML feature definitions registered in the analytics feature store (Databricks Feature Store). Each record defines feature name, feature group, owning use case, source entity type (player, session, title, match), computation logic description, aggregation window (e.g., 7d, 30d, lifetime), data type, freshness SLA, backfill availability date, and serving mode (online, offline, both). Provides a governed, discoverable registry of reusable ML features to prevent redundant feature engineering across data science teams.

attributes.name: feature_store_definition_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the feature store definition record. Primary key for the feature registry catalog.

attributes.name: processing_activity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.processing_activity. Business justification: Feature engineering creates derived personal data (aggregations, embeddings). Each feature group is a processing activity requiring documented legal basis and purpose limitation. DPO audits feature pi

attributes.name: aggregation_window

attributes.name: backfill_available_from_date
attributes.description: Earliest date for which historical feature values are available for backfill and training dataset generation. Defines the temporal coverage of the feature.

attributes.name: computation_cost_tier
attributes.description: Relative computational cost tier for calculating this feature. Used for resource planning and optimization prioritization.

attributes.name: computation_logic_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of how the feature is calculated, including source tables, aggregation functions, filters, and business rules. Provides transparency for feature interpretation and debugging.

attributes.name: dependent_features

attributes.name: feature_approval_status

attributes.name: feature_approved_by_email

attributes.name: feature_approved_timestamp

attributes.name: feature_cardinality
